title: /api/optimise computes empty_arrivals from the 40-row display slice but places it over the whole-census denominator, so the published share is 4-13x low and falls as the window widens
area: Optimise page (#optimise), caption under 'Work that started where no car was standing'; repeated on the mobile Optimise screen
reproduced: GET https://fleet-dashboard-wpeqb.ondigitalocean.app/api/optimise?days=30&_=R now returns empty_arrivals 593, empty_arrival_pct 10.8, placed_bookings 5515, totals.moves 445, moves.length 40. Summing gap over the 40 returned rows = 593 exactly. Summing gap over all 445 rows of the body's own `slots` array matching the identical filter (gap>0 AND pickups>=4) = 2485 = 45.1%. Reproduced at every window: ?period=month 200/30.8% published vs 237/36.5% over 55 rows; ?days=90 1354/8.3% vs 6958/42.8% over 973; ?days=365 4707/3.0% vs 60609/38.1% over 6894. Code matches verbatim: api/supply_routes.js:388 `const moves = movesAll.slice(0, 40);`, :458 `const totalGap = moves.reduce((a, x) => a + Math.max(0, x.gap), 0);`, :464-465 feed empty_arrivals and empty_arrival_pct. The denominator at :457 (`totalPickups`) is summed over ALL slots, so numerator and denominator are drawn from different populations.
intent_check: Not deliberate. The surrounding comments defend the address-parsed area, the one-hour arrival shift and the 'arrivals are an upper bound' direction, and the totals/shown block at api/supply_routes.js:495-507 exists specifically so 'each list names the population it was cut from' — the author was demonstrably alert to head-vs-census, but only for the LISTS. The scalar was never brought back. api/public/optimise.js:261-263 prints 'Arrivals are an upper bound on cars present, so that share is a floor', which the slice makes false in the wrong direction. The table above it renders only moves.slice(0,15) (optimise.js:241), so the printed total is not even the sum of the rows on screen. Neither docs/COVERAGE.md nor docs/AUDIT.md mentions empty_arrival at all.
user_visible: Yes. The caption reads '593 of 5,515 placeable bookings (10.8%)... that share is a floor' when the same response body supports 2,485 (45.1%). An operator widening from a month to a year watches the figure fall 30.8% -> 10.8% -> 8.3% -> 3.0% while the real share barely moves (36.5 / 45.1 / 42.8 / 38.1) — the metric inverts against the window. api/public/m/screens.js:1375 prints the same percentage on the phone.
fix: api/supply_routes.js:458 — sum over `movesAll` rather than `moves`. One identifier; it moves days=30 from 593/10.8% to 2485/45.1% and makes the scalar invariant to the display cap. While there, name the numerator's filter (pickups >= 4) beside it, because every positive-gap slot totals 3,192 (57.9%) at days=30 and a reader cannot tell which population the share is over.

title: Playbook headline prints the window's measured money as 'worth AED X a month' while its own unit line beneath says 'over N days' — and the client's default window is five days
area: Playbook / action list (#playbook), the verdict tile at the top of the page
reproduced: api/public/playbook.js:68 reads verbatim ``claim: `${countOf(d.actions.length,'thing')} to do, worth ${money(measured)} a month` `` with `measured = +t.aed_measured` (line 64), and :70 sets ``unit: `over ${d.window_days} days` `` — the two halves of one tile disagree. totals.aed_measured is a plain window sum, never normalised, unlike every ceiling (api/playbook_routes.js:331 scales those to 30 days). Fetched now: /api/playbook?period=month -> window 2026-09-01..09-05, window_days 5, aed_measured 28,979; ?days=7 39,115; ?days=30 150,385; ?days=90 352,930; ?days=365 1,925,352 (the finder quoted 1,802,474 — the only number that moved, and only because it is a rolling 365-day window; the four that anchor the defect reproduce to the dirham). /data.js served from production carries `days: 30, period: 'month'`, and GET /api/playbook?days=30&period=month returns window_days 5 — period wins — so the default view really is the five-day one.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and the file proves the author knew the shape of this bug. The comment at api/public/playbook.js:100-105 explains that the Idle-capacity tile is 'Named for the unit the server actually computed' because 'a tile reading bookings/month is only true at one of the five ranges the page offers'. The identical reasoning was simply never applied to the AED claim one tile earlier. Nothing in docs/AUDIT.md or docs/COVERAGE.md defends it.
user_visible: Yes, and it is the largest number on the one page that tells somebody to act. On the default view a reader sees 'worth AED 28,979 a month' with 'over 5 days' printed directly underneath. The true 30-day measured figure is 150,385, so the default understates ~5x; the 365-day chip reads 'AED 1,925,352 a month' and overstates ~12x. Same figure, opposite errors, chosen by a range chip.
fix: api/public/playbook.js:68 — drop 'a month' and use the phrase the sub-line already uses ('over this window'). If a monthly figure is genuinely wanted, normalise server-side and return aed_measured_per_30d beside the raw window sum, the way api/playbook_routes.js:331 already does for ceilings.

title: The insights 'Measured cost' tile is 54% a hotel partner's revenue and 46% an undeclared 30% recovery assumption, both stamped impact_kind 'measured'
area: Insights / action list (#insights), the 'Measured cost' KPI tile in the page header
reproduced: GET /api/insights/summary?_=R now returns total.measured_impact '5176'. GET /api/insights?limit=500&_=R returns 104 live rows; exactly three carry a non-null impact_aed outside idle_vehicle: cancellation_rate/platform/bolt 701.34, cancellation_rate/platform/uber 1658.81, partner_concentration/partner/'Le Meridien Dubai Hotel & Conference Centre' 2816.00 — 5176.15, and all three come back impact_kind 'measured'. Code matches: src/insights.js:870 `impact_aed: money(top.revenue), metric: share,` inside partnerMix, where `top` is `rows[0]` of `SELECT partner_name, count(*) trips, sum(price) revenue ... ORDER BY 2 DESC` — the top partner's revenue in the window. src/insights.js:816 `impact_aed: r.avg_price == null ? null : money((r.cancels || 0) * Number(r.avg_price) * 0.3)`. api/server.js:3512 `CASE WHEN impact_aed IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN code = 'idle_vehicle' THEN 'modelled' ELSE 'measured' END AS impact_kind`. api/public/app.js:3721-3722 prints it as 'Measured cost' / 'only findings that carry a real figure'.
intent_check: The measured/modelled split was itself a deliberate fix — api/public/app.js:3696-3700 records that the old 'Quantified cost' tile summed everything and read AED 1,424,592 — so this finding is consistent with the author's own stated principle rather than against it. The defect is that the split was implemented as a CASE on one hard-coded code instead of a property of the number. Two things are bundled here and both are real: (a) partner revenue as an impact_aed has no comment anywhere justifying it, and (b) the 0.3 factor sits in a line whose long comment explains only the NULL-fare handling, never the 30%. In fairness to the rule, partner_concentration's impact could be read as 'revenue at risk if this account leaves', which is a coherent quantity — it is still not a cost and still must not be added to loss figures, which is exactly what api/playbook_routes.js:355-356 warns against in this codebase's own words.
user_visible: Yes, but small. The header tile reads 'AED 5,176' under 'only findings that carry a real figure'. Removing the partner revenue drops it to AED 2,360 (5176.15 - 2816.00), and the remainder is a modelled 30% of cancelled fares, so on today's data nothing in the tile is a measured cost. Against a fleet doing AED 740,768 in August the absolute sum is immaterial; the category error is not.
fix: src/insights.js:870 — set `impact_aed: null` on partner_concentration and move the revenue into `detail` (its metric is already the concentration share). That alone takes the tile to AED 2,360. Then make impact_kind a stored column written by put() rather than the CASE at api/server.js:3512, so src/insights.js:816's 0.3 declares itself modelled where it is written.

title: The end-of-run prune keys on (code, entity_type, entity_id) without the window, so the nightly 30-day findings are deleted by the next 30-minute incremental and every windowed finding on production is a 3-day one
area: Insights / action list (#insights) — every windowed finding (cancellation_rate, partner_concentration, unsafe_driving) and the from/to filter on /api/insights
reproduced: src/insights.js:1110-1117 is verbatim `WITH keep AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (code, entity_type, entity_id) id FROM insight ORDER BY code, entity_type, entity_id, computed_at DESC, id DESC) DELETE FROM insight i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM keep k WHERE k.id = i.id)` — no window in the key. put() at src/insights.js:143-148 does arbitrate non-fleet windowed rows on (code, entity_type, entity_id, window_start, window_end), so distinct windows do get inserted before the prune removes them. GET /api/insights?limit=500&_=R now returns 104 rows: 93 carry NULL windows, 10 carry 2026-09-02 -> 2026-09-05 (2x cancellation_rate, 1x partner_concentration, 7x unsafe_driving) and 1 carries 2026-09-04 -> 2026-09-04; every windowed row has computed_at 2026-09-05T03:39-03:40Z, an incremental, not the 21:00Z catch-up. 2026-09-02 -> 2026-09-05 is exactly config.incrementalDays=3 (.env.example:10). GET /api/insights?from=2026-08-06&to=2026-09-01&limit=500&_=R returns 93 rows, 0 of them windowed. src/index.js:48 schedules `*/30 * * * *` incremental and :98 `0 21 * * *` catchUp(30); src/run.js:250 runs computeInsights with each pass's own bounds, so the 30-day set is written nightly and destroyed within 30 minutes.
intent_check: This is two documented decisions in direct conflict, not one undocumented lapse. src/insights.js:465-479 (unsafe_driving) explains at length that seven different 'fleet medians' over four denominators were being ranked against each other and concludes 'Naming the window makes each row true on its own terms, and /api/insights can now filter to one window so a list is comparable'; api/server.js:3432-3440 repeats that rationale for the from/to parameters. The prune's own comment at src/insights.js:1094-1096 asserts 'no number on any page moves' — true of the default read, because api/server.js:3497-3500 dedups on the same three columns, but false of the from/to filter, which filters BEFORE the dedup and would have worked had the rows survived. docs/AUDIT.md:90 records the prune rewrite and says nothing about the window collision.
user_visible: Yes. Every windowed finding on the board is sized on three days with no period stated on the summary tile: '44% of Bolt jobs cancel (38 of 86)' is flagged critical off an 86-trip sample; partner_concentration's AED 2,816 (which is 54% of the 'Measured cost' tile — see the tile finding) is three days of one hotel's billing; the seven unsafe_driving rows rank against a median computed over three days of telematics distance. And the from/to filter shipped to make lists comparable cannot ever return a windowed row.
fix: src/insights.js:1112,1114 — add window_start, window_end to both the DISTINCT ON and the ORDER BY. Default reads are unchanged (api/server.js still dedups to the newest per code/entity), and the nightly 30-day evaluation survives so ?from/&to can reach it. If keeping both sets is unwanted, the alternative is to skip the windowed rules on the 3-day incremental entirely and leave them to catchUp(30) — the incremental already skips the Uber fare walk for the same reason.

title: Playbook's window-to-30-day median normalisation does not stabilise the ceilings it was written to stabilise: the same fleet is sized 44,669 bookings/month on the default 5-day view and 345 over the full record
area: Playbook (#playbook), Deploy group + the 'Idle capacity' and 'Modelled upside' tiles
reproduced: api/playbook_routes.js:328-331 matches: `const windowDays = Math.max(1, Math.round((Date.parse(to) - Date.parse(from)) / 864e5) + 1); const medianWindow = Number(fleet?.median_bookings) || 0; const median = medianWindow * 30 / windowDays;`. Fetched now, /api/playbook?period=month (the client default, window 2026-09-01..09-05, window_days 5) returns fleet.median_bookings_window 35 -> median_bookings 210, redeploy_idle_vehicles size 180 / ceiling 37,800 bookings/month, totals.bookings_ceiling 44,669. The same endpoint at ?days=30 returns median_bookings 143 measured directly, so the 5-day basis is +47%. totals.bookings_ceiling across the six windows now: 44,669 (5d) / 42,846 (7d) / 29,081 (30d) / 22,589 (90d) / 26,122 (365d) / 345 (unbounded, where median_bookings collapses to 2) — a 129x spread on one fleet. /api/forecast .observed puts August 2026 at 13,950 trips, 98 vehicles, AED 740,768, so 44,669 is 3.2x the whole month's actual output. /api/playbook?period=month&aed_per_trip=50 returns totals.aed_modelled 2,233,450, rendered as 'Modelled upside' at api/public/playbook.js:144-148. fleet.still on the unbounded window = 132, against size 180 idle at the default window.
intent_check: Half this finding runs straight into a documented decision and must be dropped. api/playbook_routes.js:62-70 states plainly that the vehicle universe is deliberately the union of every plate ever seen in a trip, a fix or a document, because 'counting only plates seen in THIS window reported 93 vehicles where the directory reported 131, which understates idle capacity by exactly the vehicles that are most idle'. The proposed 'exclude from idle any plate with no booking ever' reverses a reasoned choice, and the page already discloses the split ('N of the idle ones did not move either'). The surviving half is stronger than the finder framed it: api/playbook_routes.js:310-327 documents the normalisation as the fix that makes 'every downstream figure agree at every window', and the six measurements above show it does not — a 5-day median only sees vehicles that worked in those five days (93 earning vs 102 at 30 days vs 141 ever), so scaling it by six compounds the selection bias rather than removing it, and at the unbounded window the same arithmetic divides by 36,526 and produces a median of 2.
user_visible: Yes. The Deploy group's headline ceiling is 3.2x the entire business's monthly bookings, and the number a reader compares between range chips is not comparable at all despite a comment promising it is. With a revenue rate entered, 'Modelled upside AED 2,233,450' stands against actual August revenue of AED 740,768. Mitigating: the action carries certainty 'ceiling', ceiling_unit 'bookings/month', and a basis sentence that discloses '210 bookings a month, from 35 over the 5 days requested' — so a careful reader can see the derivation, and aed_per_trip is empty by default.
fix: api/playbook_routes.js:328-331 — compute the per-vehicle median over a fixed trailing 30-day window independent of the request window (the pattern new_driver_first_month already uses to stay window-invariant at 12), and drop the `* 30 / windowDays` scaling. Do NOT change the idle plate universe; if the never-booked share matters, add it to `why` from the fleet.still figure the endpoint already computes.

title: Playbook receivables age the debt inside the request window, so the default view calls a 59-day debt 4 days old — while the settlement page it links to already ages the same book correctly
area: Playbook (#playbook), Collect group — and its contradiction with #settlement/receivables
reproduced: api/playbook_routes.js:171 and :241 both read `max((now()::date - local_day))::int AS oldest_days ... FROM trip_ext WHERE ${DAYWIN('requested_at')} AND is_receivable`, so oldest_days is arithmetically incapable of exceeding window_days. Surfaced at :379 as 'The oldest is ${recv.oldest_days} days old.' Fetched now: /api/playbook?period=month -> 'Chase AED 6,162 owed across 8 counterparties ... The oldest is 4 days old.'; ?days=7 -> 8,114 / 8 / 6; ?days=30 -> 36,280 / 12 / 29; ?days=90, ?days=365 and the unbounded window all -> 76,546 / 20 / 60, identical, proving the whole book sits inside 90 days and is fully knowable. Decisive corroboration: GET /api/settlement/receivables?period=month&_=R on the SAME default window returns oldest_days 59, ages_over_all_time true, and an ageing block totalling 37,776 + 38,770 = AED 76,546 over 634 trips.
intent_check: The opposite of deliberate — the identical bug was already found and fixed one file away, and the playbook was not updated. api/analytics_routes.js:336-349 carries the comment 'oldest_days was min(requested_at) inside the same window as everything else, so at days=7 the oldest receivable could not exceed seven days ... Ageing is a property of the receivable, not of the range chip', and implements RECV_TO_DATE (`local_day <= $1::date AND is_booking AND is_receivable`) plus AGE() buckets, backed by a partial index in sql/schema_v30.sql. The playbook action's own `link` field is '#settlement/receivables' — it opens the page that disagrees with it.
user_visible: Yes, and self-contradictory inside the product. On the default view the Collect card says 'Chase AED 6,162 owed across 8 counterparties ... The oldest is 4 days old' and names 8 counterparties; clicking through to the page it links to shows oldest 59 days, 20 counterparties, and AED 76,546 outstanding of which AED 38,770 is already 31-60 days old. Ageing is the entire basis on which a collections queue is ordered, and capping it at the window flattens the priority order to nothing.
fix: api/playbook_routes.js:171 and :241 — replace the DAYWIN predicate for the receivable queries with analytics_routes.js's RECV_TO_DATE (`local_day <= $2::date AND is_booking AND is_receivable`) so the amount and the age cover the whole unsettled book as at the window's end, exactly as the linked page already does. Report the two quantities separately in the `why` string: what newly landed on account this window, and what is outstanding with its oldest age.

title: drivers_online_no_trips writes every fleet and every period onto one row (entity_type 'fleet', entity_id 'all'), whose arbiter ignores the window entirely, so only the last-processed fleet-day survives
area: Insights / action list (#insights) — the drivers_online_no_trips finding, the list's only 'critical' utilisation rule
reproduced: src/insights.js:934 sets `entity_type: 'fleet', entity_id: 'all', fleet_id: r.fleet_id` on drivers_online_no_trips. put() at src/insights.js:141-146 gives entity_type 'fleet' the arbiter `(code, entity_type, entity_id) WHERE entity_type = 'fleet'` and :164-166 sets KEY to the same three columns, so window_start/window_end are in the UPDATE list, not the identity — every fleet and every period collapses onto one row and the last write wins. src/insights.js:918 iterates `ORDER BY period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20`, so the surviving row is the OLDEST qualifying row in the batch, not the newest. Fetched now: GET /api/insights?code=drivers_online_no_trips&_=R returns exactly 1 row — entity_id 'all', fleet_id 'egari', window 2026-09-04 -> 2026-09-04, title '1 driver was online but completed no trips', refs naming one driver at 1.2h. GET /api/insights?code=drivers_online_no_trips&fleet=ecosine&_=R returns 0 rows. GET /api/recommendations&_=R shows the newest RECOMMENDATION_TYPE_ORG_TRIP_COMPLETION at 2026-09-05 with flagged_count 2.
intent_check: This is a known bug class in this codebase that was fixed in one rule and left standing in another. src/insights.js:716-726, on tracker_feed_dark, spells it out: 'The fleet was missing, and put()'s arbiter is (code, entity_type, entity_id, window_start, window_end) with fleet_id in the SET list. So when both fleets' CABMAN vehicles fell dark inside the same hour ... it overwrote the first, flipped fleet_id to its own, and one fleet's outage left the board entirely. Nine ecosine vehicles became seven egari ones.' The fix there was entity_id `${source}:${fleetId}:${hour}`. platformFlags never got it, and for entity_type 'fleet' the collision is worse because the arbiter drops the window too. The same defect also affects weather_rain/weather_heat (src/insights.js:836), which likewise use entity_id 'all' with per-day windows.
user_visible: Yes. The rule the product itself calls 'the sharpest supply-side waste signal there is' shows one fleet's yesterday (1 driver, egari, 2026-09-04) while Uber's own payload for today names 2. Ecosine's flagged drivers are absent from the board with no indication anything is missing, and the driver ids in `refs` — which the action ('check whether they were genuinely available') cannot be taken without — belong to whichever row happened to be written last.
fix: src/insights.js:934 — key the finding on entity_id `${r.fleet_id}:${isoDay(r.period_start)}` (and drop entity_type 'fleet' for 'platform' or 'source' so put() uses the windowed arbiter rather than the fleet one), mirroring the tracker_feed_dark fix at :728. Apply the same to the acceptance/cancellation put at :955 and to weatherOutlook at :836.

title: Uber names 4 drivers below its acceptance target and 1 above its cancellation target; neither has ever produced a finding — the insight rows do not exist, they were never written
area: Insights / action list (#insights) — below_target_acceptance and above_target_cancellation are absent from the board
reproduced: GET /api/recommendations?_=R now returns RECOMMENDATION_TYPE_ORG_ACCEPTANCE_RATE for 2026-08-24 -> 2026-08-31, org 0.99827 against target 0.97698, flagged_count 4 with all four driver_ext_ids present, and RECOMMENDATION_TYPE_ORG_CANCELLATION_RATE for the same period with flagged_count 1; history 452 rows. GET /api/insights?code=below_target_acceptance&_=R and ?code=above_target_cancellation&_=R both return rows 0 AND cleared 0. That cleared=0 is the sharp result and it corrects the finder's stated mechanism: api/server.js:3502-3505 computes `cleared` over the deduped set BEFORE the still_found filter, so a stale, freshness-suppressed row would report cleared=1. It reports 0, which means no insight row with either code has ever existed. src/insights.js:1061-1062 confirms platform_flags owns both codes, and src/insights.js:955-969 confirms the put() would fire for any non-TRIP_COMPLETION row with a non-empty `flagged`.
intent_check: Nothing defends this. src/insights.js:912-914 introduces the rule as 'Uber computes acceptance/cancellation/completion against its own targets and names the drivers who miss. That is a second opinion on data we cannot see ourselves' — the rule is meant to fire. The remaining live candidate for the cause is src/insights.js:918 `ORDER BY period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20` over a 452-row table whose row types have different cadences: TRIP_COMPLETION rows are per fleet per day (the newest is 2026-09-05 -> 2026-09-05) while acceptance/cancellation are weekly (2026-08-24 -> 2026-08-31), so the daily rows crowd the weekly ones out of the batch. The surviving drivers_online row being dated 2026-09-04 is consistent with a batch that reaches back barely two days. I could not confirm the batch contents without database access, so treat the LIMIT as the strong hypothesis and the absence itself as the confirmed fact.
user_visible: Only as an omission — nothing on the dashboard is wrong, five named drivers are simply not on it. Uber's own adjudication against its own targets, with driver uuids attached, reaches /api/recommendations and never reaches the action list an operator works from. Corroborated by /api/insights/summary, whose by_category 'revenue' n is 3, and those three are 2x cancellation_rate plus 1x partner_concentration.
fix: src/insights.js:918 — replace the flat `ORDER BY period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20` with `SELECT DISTINCT ON (rec_type, fleet_id) ... ORDER BY rec_type, fleet_id, period_end DESC NULLS LAST`, so a weekly recommendation can never be crowded out by daily ones and each fleet keeps its own latest of each type. This is the same edit that the entity_id fix for drivers_online_no_trips wants, so land them together.

title: CABMAN's SeatSensorStatus is discarded, so a dead sensor's 0 is read as an empty car
area: Unauthorized journeys / #segments / sensor-health (CABMAN telemetry)
reproduced: The code claim is exact: src/sources/cabman.js:96 is `status: v.Status, seat_occupied: truthy(v.SeatSensorValue), odometer: v.odometer`, and `grep -rn SeatSensorStatus src/ api/ sql/ test/` returns only two comments (api/server.js:4501, test/route_smoke.test.mjs:409). The headline number also reproduces: GET /api/schema/raw-values?table=telemetry_snapshot&key=SeatSensorStatus&from=2000-01-01&to=2100-01-01 returns [{"value":"Not Active","n":34051},{"value":"Active","n":12430}] = 73.3% of 46,481. But the PREMISE is refuted by the neighbouring fields. Same endpoint, key=SeatSensorValue: 0 -> 33,319; 1 -> 10,680; 2 -> 2,130; 3 -> 325; 4 -> 19; 5 -> 8, so value>=1 on 13,162 fixes. If 'Not Active' meant the sensor was unpowered, only 12,430 fixes would have a live sensor while 13,162 report one to five occupants -- 732 occupancy readings from sensors the finder says are switched off, which is impossible. And key=Status returns [{"Active",34051},{"Engaged",12430}] -- exactly the same 34,051/12,430 partition. SeatSensorStatus tracks whether a passenger is aboard (Engaged), not whether the device has power.
intent_check: The two comments the finder found (api/server.js:4501, test/route_smoke.test.mjs:409) say the field exists and is unstored -- they are an admission that nobody had looked, not a reasoned decision, so the finder was right that no one had measured it. Measuring it is what refutes the finding: SeatSensorValue is an occupant COUNT (0-5) and SeatSensorStatus is its Active/Not-Active restatement, so `truthy(v.SeatSensorValue)` already captures exactly the fact the finder wanted stored. The reconciler is also not blind to hardware faults: src/reconcile.js:129-131 raises `sensor_suspect` on implausible durations and on long occupancy with ignition off, described at :193 as 'treated as a hardware fault, not a journey'. /api/sensor-health returns judgeable:false on 94 of its 100 rows rather than judging them.
user_visible: Nothing. The signal is not unpowered on three quarters of the fixes; 'Not Active' is an empty seat, which is what seat_occupied=false already says.
fix: None -- and the proposed fix must NOT be applied. Setting seat_occupied to NULL wherever SeatSensorStatus='Not Active' (src/sources/cabman.js:96) would null every genuine empty-seat reading and destroy the occupancy signal the unauthorized-journey product is built on.

title: cabman.js stamps fleet_id from config, never from the payload's CompanyName, so 132 vehicles belonging to three other operators are stored as this fleet's and are half of /api/live
area: Live map / #map vehicle list, and /api/sensor-health
reproduced: src/sources/cabman.js:89 is `source: SRC, fleet_id: f.fleet, plate: normPlate(v.VehicleID)` -- the fleet comes from config (src/config.js:64-73, the single ecosine entry), never from the row. GET /api/schema/raw-values?table=telemetry_snapshot&key=CompanyName&from=2000-01-01&to=2100-01-01 returns Ecosine Transports LLC 46,349 / Sahalat 65 / Star Skyline Luxury Transport LLC 45 / VOLYA LIMOUSINE SERVICES L.L.C 22 -- 132 non-Ecosine rows. I confirmed the causal link the finder only asserted: GET /api/live returns 264 rows, of which 175 are source=cabman, and those cluster into exactly four poll cycles -- 2026-08-31T08:35 (65 plates), 2026-09-04T05:20 (45), 2026-08-30T12:45 (22) and 2026-09-05T07:20 (43). The first three are 65/45/22, matching Sahalat/Star Skyline/VOLYA one for one; all 132 carry stale:true. So /api/live is 264 rows of which 132 are foreign and 132 are this fleet's -- exactly half. All five trips cited fetch as predicted via /api/trip?platform=uber&id=...: 1032b169-9834-4b01-bf7d-adca09d3613e (price null, completed, uber_payments fare null / tip 5 / earnings 5 / adjustment 5 / transactions 1), 485bc357-284c-4893-acc6-24fe402a04f9, 0f192d74-ff5c-469d-bcce-279adad8c995, 3134158b-6f66-4578-9cef-6f7cdbc9330d (earnings 63.79, adjustment 63.79) and 00baafd1-6a58-4cf4-ba81-fca41f790d9b -- every one price null with a surviving fare-null payments blob. I verified the finder's inference that this proves the payments UPDATE was the last write: `grep -n 'price:' src/sources/uber.js` returns nothing, so the TRIP_ACTIVITY upsert at :701 carries no price and replaces `raw` wholesale, meaning a surviving uber_payments blob can only mean the payments UPDATE ran last.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and actively misfiled as a provider limit in the product's own reference. docs/COVERAGE.md:72-75 books these rows as an irreducible ceiling -- 'The residual 0.0-0.1% is a handful of rows per month (7 in August) that are completed and unpriced' -- and api/server.js:776-779 tells the reader in the list note that 'a completed ride with no fare is a week the provider's separate payments report has not been collected for yet'. Both are false for these ten rows: the week WAS collected, and the payments blob sitting on the row is the proof. Nothing anywhere argues for unpricing a trip.
user_visible: Yes, but small. Ten completed August rides show a dash where a fare should be, with a note under the table blaming an uncollected provider report. At the fleet's AED 57.91 average that is roughly AED 580 against ~11,200 chargeable August Uber bookings (0.09%), and it moves no headline. Lowering from the filed 'high' on magnitude -- but the mechanism is a scheduled job that deletes money it already collected, and it re-fires on every backfill that re-walks the weeks, so it grows rather than heals.
fix: One line: change src/sources/uber.js:535 to `SET price = coalesce($3, price)` (or tighten the guard at :533 to skip when t.fare == null), so a transaction row that prices nothing cannot unprice the trip. Settings exact: CABMAN_CRON '*/5 * * * *' at src/settings.js:50, liveStatusSeconds 120 at src/config.js:36, both wired at src/index.js:44 and :46. My own /api/track fetches (2026-09-02..09-05) are STRONGER than the finder's: L12617 727 fixes, min gap 0.33 min, p10 3.01, p25 4.25, median 5.02, 323 of 726 gaps under 5 min (44%); L46706 961 fixes, min 0.87, p25 4.02, median 5.02, 304 of 960 under 5 min (32%).
intent_check: PARTIAL INTENT HIT the finder missed, and it costs the finding its headline. The `partial` bucket is deliberate and documented: docs/unauthorized-trips.md:57 — "Segments touching a gap > 15 min are marked `partial` and reported separately — we cannot claim a trip was unauthorized if we couldn't see it." Reporting "46% unjudgeable" as a defect misreads designed conservatism as breakage. What IS undocumented and is genuinely wrong is the premise underneath: docs/unauthorized-trips.md:10 asserts "CABMAN `GetIVDData` gives, per vehicle, every 5 minutes" — the author believed 5 minutes was the DEVICE's emission rate. Production disproves it (gaps of 0.33 and 0.87 min; a third to a half of stored gaps under 5 min). RULES.pollMinutes=5 (src/reconcile.js:10) and minDurationMin=5 ("at least two consecutive polls", doc:39) are both derived from that mistaken belief. No provider throttle, rate limit or since-filter is documented anywhere — grep across src/ and docs/ finds none, and the provider help page declares no parameters at all.
user_visible: Yes, and this is what carries the severity: 23 of the 59 unauthorized verdicts (39%) rest on four fixes or fewer, and the top row of the accusation list is a 3-fix, 6-minute allegation against a named plate. These are printed as findings about a driver's conduct. Holding severity at high for that reason alone. I am correcting the finder's mechanism claim, though: faster polling will NOT reliably convert `partial` into judgeable. `partial` means max_gap > 15 min, which under a reliable 5-minute cron means the device itself was silent for 15+ minutes (parked, ignition off, out of coverage); GetIVDData returns each vehicle's LATEST report, so polling more often cannot manufacture a report the device never sent. The real, provable gain is resolution INSIDE segments — up to 5x more fixes under each accusation — not shrinking the 46%.
fix: Set CABMAN_CRON to '*/1 * * * *' at src/settings.js:50, and derive RULES.pollMinutes from config.cabmanCron at src/reconcile.js:10 instead of hardcoding 5 so minDurationMin stops silently meaning "two polls". Correct the false claim at docs/unauthorized-trips.md:10. Measure the partial rate before and after rather than assuming it moves.

title: On a genuinely shared plate-day the whole day's harsh-driving events are charged to one name, ties are settled by arrival time alone, and no field says the car was shared
area: #safety coaching list (/api/alerts/by-driver), per-vehicle safety panel, /api/playbook held_by
reproduced: The mechanism reproduces exactly. sql/schema_v19.sql:76-78 settles is_primary with `ORDER BY trips DESC, first_trip_at ASC`, so a tie is decided by arrival time and nothing else. api/server.js:1796-1800 collapses custody to one row per plate-day and gives that custodian the whole day's alerts; the returned row carries no co-custodian and no shared-day field (keys: driver_name, driver_ext_id, alerts, driving_alerts, device_alerts, harsh_brake, harsh_accel, sharp_turn, overspeed, other, plates, plate_list, booked_km, alert_km, per_100km, per_100km_absent), and /api/vehicle/safety by_driver likewise (driver_name, n, booked_km, per_100km, days_held). The grep for 'ambiguous'/'ambiguity'/'tie-break' over api/, src/, sql/ returns nothing about custody, as claimed. The L45243 worked example reproduces exactly: 29 driving days, 18 shared between Waseem Abbas Nabi and Zain Hassan Raja Nasrullah Khan (two genuinely different humans), tied 1-1 on 2026-08-09 and 3-3 on 2026-09-03, with is_primary going to Waseem both times.
intent_check: The disclosure gap is real and undefended — nothing in api/, src/ or sql/ discusses custody ambiguity or tie-breaks, and there is no comment beside sql/schema_v19.sql:78 explaining what a tie means. This directly contravenes the product's own house rule, stated in docs/COVERAGE.md ('a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON, never as zero') and in api/custody_sql.js:1-8, which says naming the person is what turns an accusation into 'a conversation' — on a shared day the name is one of two. But the finder's 30.8% headline conflates this with finding 1 and did not read that far.
why_refuted: The HEADLINE is refuted and has been rewritten. I reproduce 531 of 1,729 plate-days (30.7%) carrying more than one person_key and 26 tied — close to the claimed 533/30.8% and 27 — but the word 'genuinely' is exactly wrong. Collapse the name twins and genuine multi-human plate-days fall to 156 (9.0%) and genuine ties to 18. Three quarters of the claimed sharing IS the identity defect of finding 1, counted a third time; that half is MERGED into finding 1. The /api/playbook evidence has also drifted: production now returns 24 held_by objects, not 16, and two of the three cited days (L19261 2026-06-25, L40547 2026-05-21) are no longer in the list — only L45235 remains.
user_visible: Yes, but narrower than claimed. On L45243 Waseem Abbas Nabi carries 4,238 alerts at 222.23 per 100 km — rank 8 in the fleet — while sharing the car on 18 of his 29 days; on those shared days Zain took 35 of the 127 trips (27.6%), and nothing on the row says the car was shared or that two of those days were coin-flips. title: Yango's stored earnings are the gross fare, while every surface labels the figure "net payout … the money that arrived"; the net formula shipped after the park went 403, so no collection can restate it
area: Revenue page — Yango channel row and its "Why" cell; every Yango per-driver earnings figure
reproduced: Decisive single-period test reproduced exactly. GET /api/revenue?platform=yango&from=2026-08-31&to=2026-09-06 → payouts 311.00, cash 28, payout_periods 1. GET /api/funnel/drivers?from=2026-08-31&to=2026-09-06 → Tariq Afzal cash 0 / cashless 235 / commission -52.44; Aliyan Khalil cash 28 / cashless 48 / commission -15.25; five drivers all zero. Gross = 311.00, commission = -67.69, net = 243.31. Production serves 311.00 — the gross, to the fils. Whole record GET /api/revenue?platform=yango → payouts 17788.93, basis_note "net payout, after the platform's commission — this is the money that arrived". Code checks out: src/sources/yango.js:312-313 does hold the net formula (cash + cashless + price_platform_commission); `git show cc85c15 -- src/sources/yango.js` confirms the pre-fix line was `earnings: (Number(it.price_cash)||0) + (Number(it.price_cashless)||0)`, and cc85c15 is dated 2026-09-04 20:32:04 +0000. The 403 ceiling is real and worse than the finder said: GET /api/status shows all three Yango modes error with rows_written 0, and the backfill run (finished_at 2026-09-03T18:50:22.177Z) 403s on /api/reports-api/v2/summary/drivers/list — the driver-summary endpoint itself, not merely the trips endpoint. So no re-collection can rewrite these rows.
intent_check: Not a deliberate choice — the opposite. src/sources/yango.js:310 says in terms "RESTATING HISTORY NEEDS A BACKFILL: rows already stored keep the gross until this window is collected again", and the backfill is the run that 403s. docs/COVERAGE.md:168 asserts "Yango | yes — 100% | yes | earnings are NET: cash + cashless + commission (commission is negative)" — the documentation states as fact something production contradicts, which makes this a live doc/data divergence rather than a reasoned trade-off.
user_visible: Yes. The Revenue page prints the Yango row at AED 17,788.93 with the "Why" cell reading "net payout, after the platform's commission — this is the money that arrived". It is the gross. I re-derived the magnitude rather than taking the finder's: two independently measured commission rates are 67.69/311.00 = 21.8% (2026-08-31→09-06) and 1,419.55/5,928.15 = 23.95% (the 07-24→08-23 covering periods), so roughly AED 3,900–4,300 of the 17,788.93 is Yango's own cut, not money that arrived. CORRECT THE FINDER'S FLEET-LEVEL ARITHMETIC: they wrote that "the fleet accounted total … overstate[s] … by ~24%". It does not. Accounted is 3,708,133.28, of which Yango is 17,788.93 (0.48%), so the fleet total is overstated by ~0.11%. The 24% error is confined to the Yango row and to 12 drivers' earnings. That is why this is high, not critical.
fix: Restate in SQL, since re-collection is impossible: UPDATE the Yango rows in driver_performance to earnings = (raw->>'price_cash')::numeric + (raw->>'price_cashless')::numeric + (raw->>'price_platform_commission')::numeric WHERE platform='yango' AND raw ? 'price_platform_commission', then re-run refreshPayouts (src/rollup.js:470) to rebuild driver_payout_day. Rows lacking the commission key must not be silently left as gross under a "net" label — add an earnings_basis column ('net'|'gross') written by src/sources/yango.js and have api/income_sql.js:219-230 pick the basis_note from it, because today a restated row and an un-restated one are indistinguishable in the same column with one sentence printed over both.

area: Revenue page → "What each channel tells us" table, Per km column
reproduced: GET /api/revenue?platform=yango → revenue_per_km 39.18, per_km_basis "payout", per_km_km 454; payouts 17788.93 over payout_days 119 and payout_drivers 12, while km 454 comes from bookings 36, drivers 3, booking_days 14. Same numbers on the unfiltered GET /api/revenue, where the neighbouring channels read uber 0.62, bolt 4.68, hotel 6.73. Also reproduced on two sub-windows: GET /api/revenue?platform=yango&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 → 14.69 = 5846.06/398; GET /api/revenue?from=2026-07-24&to=2026-08-23 → yango 38.64 over 148 km against uber 2.68, hotel 5.04, bolt 4.96. Code confirmed at api/revenue_routes.js:365-366 (`r.revenue_per_km = r2(r.payouts / r.km)`), with no check that numerator and denominator share a population. CITATION CORRECTION: the finder's second render site, api/public/m/screens.js:362, is NOT this figure — that tile renders k.revenue_per_km from /api/kpis, a fleet-wide fares-over-priced-measured-trips number, and the mobile shell has no per-platform per-km cell. The only render site is api/public/revenue.js:330-338.
intent_check: Partially anticipated, but not this case. The comment at api/revenue_routes.js:347-360 is a deliberate decision — it explains why a payout row divides by every booking's distance rather than only priced km, and says "The denominator differs between the two, so it is reported rather than assumed: per_km_basis says which money, per_km_km says over what." That reasoning is entirely about which distance to use. It never contemplates a payout population that is wider than the booking population, which is Yango's situation and only Yango's. So the guard the finder proposes is genuinely missing rather than consciously declined.
user_visible: Yes, and it is worse than a bare wrong number because the cell shows its own working. api/public/revenue.js:333-338 renders "AED 39.18" with a sub-line "net payout over 454 km", so a reader who checks the arithmetic finds it self-consistent and concludes Yango earns 6× the next-best channel and 63× Uber. The honest fares-basis answer over the same rows is 1,812/454 = AED 3.99/km, plausible for Dubai — so the printed figure is roughly 10× too high. Note the compounding with the finding above: the numerator is itself ~24% too large, so even a population-matched ratio would still be inflated.
fix: In api/revenue_routes.js, guard the payout branch at :363-367: when r.payout_days > r.booking_days * 1.25 or r.payout_drivers > r.drivers, fall through to the fares basis if one exists, otherwise set revenue_per_km null and carry a reason string that api/public/revenue.js:333 renders in place of the number ("the payout covers 119 days and 12 drivers; the distance covers 14 days and 3"). Yango would then show a dash with a reason; no other channel's row changes, since Uber's payout population is a subset of its bookings.

(b) PAYOUT SIDE (absorbed from the payout_coverage finding): api/income_sql.js:163 `const base = r.booking_days > 0 ? r.booking_days : windowDays` and :176-179 `Math.min(r.payout_days, base) / base`; GET /api/revenue?platform=yango → payout_days 119, booking_days 14, payout_coverage_pct 100, payout_coverage_days 14, payout_coverage_base 14, basis "payout", and measured_platforms includes yango.

WORSE: on the 07-24→08-23 window the unfiltered /api/revenue returns silent_platforms [] — empty — so the "Channels that reported nothing at all" panel does not fire and nothing on the Revenue page tells the reader Yango's trip collector is 403. The 403 means the 66 rides cannot be fetched — that is a ceiling — but printing 100% over a 6.5× hole is closable today.
merged_with: Absorbs the separate finding "Yango's coverage percentages divide by a base that shrinks with the hole, so a channel missing 85% of its rides reports as fully measured with zero dark money" (api/income_sql.js:162-180, :219). Same defect — coverage measured against what we hold rather than what exists — seen through two formulas (priced/chargeable, and min(payout_days, booking_days)/booking_days), with one shared user-visible outcome and one overlapping fix.

title: /api/economics/assets drops chargeable_bookings in its JS hand-off, so the vehicle ledger reads Bolt as 'partial' where the Revenue page reads it clean
area: Unit Economics page, 'per-km yield by channel' table
reproduced: Exact, with zero drift (closed month). GET /api/economics/assets?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 by_platform: uber chargeable_bookings 12431 (identical to bookings 12431), fare_coverage_pct 90.3, uncharged_bookings null; bolt chargeable_bookings 560 (= bookings 560), priced 357, fare_coverage_pct 63.8, basis 'partial_fares', note 'fares on only 357 of 560 bookings (63.8%) - the rest of this channel's money is not collected'. Code confirmed: computed in SQL at api/economics_routes.js:242-243; the plat() seed at :450-452 omits both fields; the Object.assign at :456-459 copies bookings/priced_bookings/fares/km/booking_days and not them; the sibling chanOf() at :1010-1012 seeds both and the drivers merge at :1077-1078 copies both.
intent_check: Not deliberate. The SQL deliberately computes both columns with a comment (economics_routes.js:237-241) citing the very 63.8% figure this endpoint still prints, ships them nested in `channels`, and the JS then drops them on the floor - while the sibling endpoint in the same file does it correctly. coverage() at income_sql.js:168 then silently falls back to `r.bookings`, which is the documented compatibility shim ('so an old row reads as it always did rather than dividing by undefined'), not a decision about this caller.
user_visible: Yes, but less than the finder claimed, and I corrected the severity down for it. I re-derived the money: it does NOT move. Both the `fares` and `partial_fares` branches set best = r.fares, and uber stays on basis 'payout' because its payout coverage clears 80 - so every `money` column on the page is unchanged. What a person actually sees is at api/public/economics.js:487-492: Bolt renders a warn 'partial' pill and its 'gross fare' pill loses its 'ok' tone on Unit Economics, while the Revenue page shows the same channel in the same month as clean `fares`. title: /api/alerts/by-driver groups on the raw driver name but joins distance on person_key, so one person appears twice and each row claims the other's kilometres
area: Safety page driver leaderboard, and the driver cohort chips built from it
reproduced: Verbatim, no drift. GET /api/alerts/by-driver?days=365 returns BOTH 'Sajid Gul Muhammad' (driver_ext_id a2692332-5580-4aef-890b-48416e7eeed0, alerts 8551, booked_km 26232, alert_km 5684, per_100km 150.44, plates 1, plate_list ['L90721']) AND 'Sajid Gul Gul Muhammad' (driver_ext_id 7644369, alerts 227, booked_km 26232, alert_km 5684, per_100km 3.99, plates 1, plate_list ['L90721']). totals.drivers 119. The byte-identical booked_km/alert_km under two different driver_ext_ids is itself the proof that both rows matched one km row. Mechanism verified in source: personFold (api/custody_sql.js:137-139) is `regexp_replace(btrim(regexp_replace(lower(col),'\s+',' ','g')), '(\m\w+)( \1)+', '\1','g')`, which collapses the repeated 'gul', so both names fold to 'sajid gul muhammad' and personKey (:164-165) returns the same key for both. Line numbers: api/server.js:1803 correct; the GROUP BY 1 is at :1845 (finding said :1846, off by one); km CTE `SELECT t.person_key AS person` at :1901 correct; `FROM shown s LEFT JOIN km ON km.person = s.person` at :1927 correct; `_drivers` is `count(*) FILTER (WHERE named) OVER ()` at :1858.
intent_check: Genuinely wrong, and the comment shows the reasoning slip rather than a decision. api/server.js:1805-1810 justifies carrying person_key through a name-grouped CTE: 'It is a function of the grouping key - vehicle_driver_day generates person_key out of the same driver_name - so every row in a group agrees on it and max() is choosing between identical values.' That is true in the safe direction and misses the one that bites: the function is deliberately many-to-one - collapsing spellings is the entire purpose of personFold - so distinct name groups can and do share one person_key. The km CTE's own comment at :1870-1873 names the same bug ('Grouping on the raw string split one human across their platform spellings and gave the rate a denominator covering only one of their accounts') and the fix was applied to the denominator but not to the rows it decorates.
user_visible: Yes. The Safety leaderboard (fetched at api/public/app.js:2739, and reused as a cohort source at api/public/cohorts.js:236) names one man twice on one car: once as fourth-worst in the fleet at 150.44 alerts per 100 km and once as near-spotless at 3.99. I re-derived his true rate: (8551+227)*100/5684 = 154.4, which appears nowhere on the page. An operator coaching from this table would read the second row as a clean record for the same person they just flagged. The driver count printed under the table (119) counts spellings, not people, for the same reason.
fix: api/server.js:1803 - group on the key the km CTE already joins by: replace `coalesce(c.driver_name, '(unattributed)') AS driver_name` with `coalesce(nullif(c.person_key,''), c.driver_ext_id) AS person` as the grouping expression, take the label as `coalesce(max(c.driver_name), '(unattributed)') AS driver_name` alongside the existing `max(c.driver_ext_id)`, and drop the now-redundant `max(c.person_key) AS person` at :1810. `_drivers` at :1858 then counts people rather than spellings with no further change.

title: The partial_fares sentence prints a numerator and denominator that do not produce the percentage printed beside them
area: Revenue page channel table, 'Why' column - reachable by picking a historical date range
reproduced: Verbatim, no drift. GET /api/revenue?from=2025-08-01&to=2025-08-31 -> uber.basis_note = 'fares on only 5283 of 13568 bookings (43.6%) - the rest of this channel's money is not collected', on a row with bookings 13568, chargeable_bookings 12111, priced_bookings 5283, fare_coverage_pct 43.6. I re-derived both: 5283/13568 = 38.94%, 5283/12111 = 43.62% -> 43.6. So the printed percentage is the chargeable ratio and the printed fraction is the raw-bookings ratio. Code confirmed: api/income_sql.js:266-267 interpolates `${r.bookings}` while coverage() at :164-168 computes fare_coverage_pct over `r.chargeable_bookings ?? r.bookings`. The adjacent fares branch at :247 already uses `${r.chargeable_bookings ?? r.bookings}`.
intent_check: Not deliberate - the chargeable-denominator change was landed at :247 and this branch was left behind. income_sql.js:69-85 states the rule the sentence breaks: 'A ride nobody took has no fare and never will. Counting it as missing coverage is how Bolt came to read 63.8% covered on a month where it priced 312 of its 313 completed rides.' The same doctrine is asserted in test/income_basis.test.mjs:118-119 ('and the note counts over the chargeable bookings, not every offer'), but that check is written against the `fares` branch only, so the partial_fares note is untested.
user_visible: Yes - api/public/revenue.js:341 prints basis_note verbatim in the channel table's 'Why' column, so a reader can falsify the arithmetic in their head on a money page. But no money figure is wrong: best = r.fares in both the fares and partial_fares branches, so `accounted` is unaffected. The sentence also overstates the hole - 'the rest' reads as 8,285 bookings where the bookings that could have carried a fare and did not number 6,828, the other 1,457 being cancellations the file's own comment says must not count. This is a credibility defect, not a wrong total, and no channel is partial_fares on any current default window, so a reader has to select a historical range to hit it. Medium, not high.
fix: api/income_sql.js:266 - use the same denominator and the same wording as line 247: `fares on only ${r.priced_bookings} of ${r.chargeable_bookings ?? r.bookings} bookings that could carry one (${r.fare_coverage_pct}%)`, so the printed ratio and the printed percentage are the same measurement.
