title: Ten Bolt trip fields sit in raw on 48,301 rows and are reachable by no query — including the tip the revenue model prints as null
area: Revenue page Tips tile and the per-platform bolt row (tips: null); any per-ride fee or duration analysis for Bolt
reproduced: Numbers exact, list sloppy. /api/schema/raw-fields?platform=bolt&_=$RANDOM -> rows_with_raw 48,301, sampled 4,000, 23 raw keys, only price and status with already_a_column:true. /api/schema/raw-values?platform=bolt&key=... reproduced to the row: booking_fee {0:26302, 5:21915, 21:52, 15.5:27, 13:2, 16:1, 18:1, 25:1}; toll_fee {0:42772, 4:2361, 6:1247, 8:699, ...}; tip {0:47965, 5:96, 3:68, 10:39, ...}; cancellation_fee {0:48061, 15.6:142, 15:74, ...}; order_type {Regular:48076, Scheduled:225}. Re-derived independently rather than trusted: non-zero booking_fee 21,999, toll_fee 5,529, tip 336, cancellation_fee 240 — the finder's arithmetic is exact. /api/revenue?days=365 bolt "tips": null — confirmed. src/sources/bolt.js:465-467 is verbatim the quoted comment. Two corrections: ride_duration/pickup_duration distincts measure 1,243 / 589 in the 4,000-row sample, not the claimed 1,259 / 594 (sampling, immaterial); and the evidence's "only price and status map" is the ENDPOINT's answer, not the collector's — api/server.js:4588-4590 computes already_a_column/mapped_to by name match plus an alias table, so a raw key consumed under a different column name reads as unmapped. Five of the fifteen keys listed are in fact consumed by portalRow (src/sources/bolt.js:430-471): route -> pickup_addr/dropoff_addr, arrived_to_destinations -> ended_at, category -> product; partner_identifier is not dropped but deliberately REJECTED with a ten-line comment at bolt.js:433-447 (it is the driver's uuid; using it as the key would have collapsed 547 trips into 71); created_by has one distinct value, "created_by_rider". The genuinely unused set is exactly the ten in the title.
intent_check: Half-read, and the finder said so honestly. src/sources/bolt.js:465-467 forbids folding the itemised fees INTO price ("a booking fee added to the fare would silently change what every per-trip figure in this product means"); it does not forbid separate columns, so promoting them does not contradict the decision. But the zero-is-absence essay and money() at src/sources/bolt.js:415-428 is the pattern any new column must follow, or 26,302 zero booking_fees become "AED 0 charged" rather than "not charged" — the exact defect that essay was written about.
user_visible: Yes, but small, and the finder's framing oversells it. Re-derived: lifetime Bolt tips total roughly AED 2,250 across 336 rows — 0.35% of the 365-day gross — and that is the one figure the product already has a slot for and prints as null. booking_fee is about AED 111,171 lifetime and toll_fee about AED 35,000, but both are pass-throughs whose ownership is precisely the ambiguity bolt.js:465 refuses to guess at, and neither becomes fleet revenue without the net figure that findings 1 and 2 supply. The counts are all-time (back to 2024-12-26) while 646,773.30 is 365-day, so they do not divide into each other. The durable value is the two duration fields: ride_duration and pickup_duration are non-zero on roughly 21,200 rows each and are the only on-trip and dead-time measures Bolt has, on the one channel with no hours (finding 4). High -> medium.
fix: No network call needed — the payloads are already in trip.raw, so history backfills from the database. Add tip, booking_fee, toll_fee, cancellation_fee, ride_duration and pickup_duration to portalRow (src/sources/bolt.js:430-471) using the same money()/zero-is-absence rule at :427, add the columns in a NEW sql/schema_v24.sql (never edit v23 — the ledger skips unchanged shas, per docs/COVERAGE.md), and populate from raw. Do tip first: it is the only one that closes a null the product already renders. Trim the reported field list from fifteen to the ten that are genuinely unused.

title: The Yango trip feed holds only 2026-08-18..2026-09-01; the driver-summary feed carries 264 completed orders and AED 15,499.70 across the 14 closed weeks 2026-05-11..2026-08-16 that have no trip row at all
area: Revenue page, per-channel table (Bookings, Per km, Drivers columns) and /api/coverage
reproduced: GET /api/coverage?_=$RANDOM now -> trips {platform:yango, n:36, from_ts:2026-08-18T07:47:39.259Z, to_ts:2026-09-01T23:50:37.765Z} and earnings {platform:yango, n:855, from_day:2026-05-11}; exact match to the finding. GET /api/drivers/performance?platform=yango&from=2024-01-01&to=2026-12-31 -> 141 rows; filtering to period_days==7 and period_start<=2026-08-10 gives 92 rows over 14 non-overlapping weeks, zero duplicate (driver, week) pairs, summing trips=264, earnings=15499.70, cash=5944, hours_online=4089.9 -- all four figures reproduce to the digit. Boundary is sharp: GET /api/revenue?from=2026-08-10&to=2026-08-16 -> yango bookings 0, payouts 1430; GET /api/revenue?from=2026-08-17&to=2026-08-23 -> yango bookings 12. GET /api/schema/raw-values?platform=yango&key=short_id -> 3909..3962, as claimed. THREE SUB-CLAIMS FAIL. (a) 'where the two feeds DO overlap they agree' is false at the first overlapping week: summary 2026-08-17..08-23 reads trips=2 / earnings 1251.30 while the trip feed reads 12 bookings / AED 568 -- a 6x disagreement the finder did not report. (b) the finder quotes week 2026-08-24 as 'trips 12'; /api/revenue?from=2026-08-24&to=2026-08-30 returns bookings 16, chargeable 16, uncharged 0, so there is no cancelled remainder to explain the gap to its quoted 12. Only week 2026-08-31 (summary 7 vs trip feed 8) is as stated. (c) the short_id argument over-reaches: an index starting at 3909 implies ~3,900 prior park orders, which cannot be reconciled with the same driver-summary feed showing the park's first earning week as 2026-05-11 and only 264 completed orders in the 14 weeks after it. short_id proves 'far more than 36 orders exist', not '264'. NEW, and it cuts against the finding: the 36 held rows cover a span of 54 short_ids and 18 are missing -- 3923-3932 and 3938-3945 -- so the trip feed is incomplete inside its own fortnight too, and 'the trip feed is accurate for the fortnight it covers' is not established.
intent_check: NOT a documented decision, and I looked hard. src/sources/yango.js:1 states '>=12 months retention' for this source, so the collector does not believe there is a retention ceiling here. docs/COVERAGE.md 'Known holes' documents exactly one Yango hole -- 'Yango Ecosine / YANGO_PARK_ID -> HTTP 403 (401 without a cookie) / park entitlement' -- and its channel table claims 'Yango | fares on the trip row? yes -- 100%', which is 100% of the 36 rows held rather than of the channel. Nothing anywhere weighs or accepts a trips-vs-summaries gap. /api/coverage already carries an earnings_gaps row for the reverse shape on Uber (trips_from 2025-04-05 vs earnings_from 2026-02-06) and has no equivalent for trips missing under earnings, which is why this went unnoticed.
user_visible: Yes, two ways. (1) GET /api/revenue?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31 returns yango bookings 0, drivers 0, km null, fares null beside payouts 4150.55 and payout_drivers 10 -- the Revenue page shows ten Yango drivers paid on zero rides for the month. (2) On a window that straddles the boundary the Per-km column prints an absurd figure: GET /api/revenue?from=2026-05-01&to=2026-09-05 -> yango revenue_per_km 39.08, per_km_km 454, rendered by api/public/revenue.js:330-338 as 'AED 39.08 / net payout over 454 km' against Uber's 2.85, because api/revenue_routes.js:365 divides 118 days of payout by 14 days of distance. The same column reads a sane 4.72 and 5.55 on single weeks inside the covered fortnight, so the absurdity is created purely by the gap. What is NOT wrong: the money. chooseBasis picks payout for Yango, so all AED 17,744.50 is counted and the basis_note says so. Scale check: Yango is AED 17,744.50 of AED 1,760,702 across the four channels over 2026-05-01..2026-09-05 -- 1.0% of revenue -- which is why this is high and not critical.
fix: Two small things, neither of which needs the entitlement. (1) src/sources/yango.js: give pullTrips and pullLedger the per-window error isolation and chunk reporting that pullDrivers already has (src/sources/yango.js:250-266) -- today a 403 partway through the cursor walk throws out of the whole surface while the pages already upserted stay, which is exactly the 36-rows-with-18-holes shape observed, and the run records it as 'trips: refused' with no window detail. (2) api/coverage: add the mirror of the existing earnings_gaps row -- earnings present with no trip rows -- so a channel paying drivers on zero bookings raises itself. The actual repull of 2026-05-11..2026-08-16 is gated on the Yango 403 and cannot be scheduled until that is settled.

title: The documented Yango Fleet API (fleet-api.yango.tech, X-Client-ID + X-API-Key, no cookie) has never been called, so the 403 the product blames on park entitlement is the console refusing a Yandex session, not the API key being refused a park
area: Collector credentials / the Auth panel and the Yango row in docs/COVERAGE.md 'Known holes'
reproduced: src/settings.js:69 is exactly `  YANGO_BASE: 'https://fleet.yango.com',`. src/sources/yango.js:14-17 is exactly `const headers = () => ({ 'X-Park-Id': config.yango.parkId, 'X-API-Key': config.yango.apiKey, 'content-type': 'application/json', 'Accept-Language': 'en', cookie: config.yango.cookie, });`. `grep -rn 'X-Client-ID|X-Client-Id|YANGO_CLIENT|fleet-api.yango' src/ api/ sql/ .env.example` returns nothing, exit 1 -- the Client ID half of the documented pair has never been held. Docs fetched live today: https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/interaction says 'Interaction with the API via: https://fleet-api.yango.tech', general headers X-Client-ID / X-API-Key / Accept-Language, and 401 = 'Unauthorized / Missing authorization parameters'; https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/authorization says 'Partner ID park_id, Client ID X-Client-ID, Secret API Key X-API-Key ... select the Settings section in the Control room and proceed to the API section. Only an employee with the Director role can edit it', and its sample curl to https://fleet-api.yango.tech/v1/parks/driver-profiles/list carries no cookie. GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM still returns the yango backfill error naming muzammil16075 and park a23aade0e2ac4f93a2f5d4b51ef1478b on all three modes (backfill 2026-09-03, catchup 2026-09-03 with 5/5 windows failed, incremental 2026-09-05). docs/COVERAGE.md 'Known holes' carries the row verbatim. Also confirmed: the three paths the repo actually calls -- /api/reports-api/v1/orders/list, /api/reports-api/v2/summary/drivers/list, /api/v1/reports/transactions/park/list -- appear nowhere in the documented resource index, which lists only /v1|/v2/parks/... operations. The repo is on an undocumented console surface.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and this is the case where the codebase's heavy documentation is evidence FOR the finding rather than against it. src/sources/yango.js carries roughly 120 lines of careful reasoning about this 403 -- the cookie-free probe, the 401-vs-403 comparison, why re-pasting the cookie cannot help, why the red row must be clearable -- and every line of it takes the console surface as the only surface there is. The strings fleet-api.yango.tech, X-Client-ID and 'Client ID' occur nowhere in src/, api/, sql/ or .env.example. Nothing weighed the documented host and rejected it; it was never seen.
user_visible: Nothing renders wrong -- Yango correctly renders absent-with-a-reason, which is the house rule. The harm is to the operator: src/sources/yango.js's hint tells them 'either this account is not on park a23aade0e2ac4f93a2f5d4b51ef1478b, or YANGO_PARK_ID or YANGO_API_KEY names a park it cannot see', and COVERAGE.md files it under 'park entitlement'. On a cookie-authenticated console surface X-API-Key is most likely ignored outright, so naming YANGO_API_KEY there is a guess presented with the same confidence as the measured parts. This is also the gate on findings 1, 4, 5 and 6 -- every Yango repair in this cluster is behind it -- and it is the cheapest action in the whole cluster.
fix: Add YANGO_CLIENT_ID to src/settings.js (beside YANGO_PARK_ID at src/settings.js:129) and to the yango getter in src/config.js:134-143, then add one probe to src/credcheck.js beside the existing ask() at src/credcheck.js:121: POST https://fleet-api.yango.tech/v1/parks/driver-profiles/list with headers X-Client-ID + X-API-Key and body {query:{park:{id: YANGO_PARK_ID}}}, limit 1. That single call distinguishes 'the API key is not entitled to this park' (403 on the documented host) from 'the Yandex account is not a member of this park in the console' (403 only on fleet.yango.com), which is the question the product has been guessing at. Until it returns, soften the COVERAGE.md row and the hint from 'park entitlement' to 'the console refuses this session on this park; the documented API has not been tried'.

title: Six varying money fields -- including the per-trip platform commission -- arrive on every Yango trip row, are stored in trip.raw and are read by nothing
area: Yango trip rows; the Revenue page's Fares column and any per-ride net for this channel
reproduced: GET /api/schema/raw-fields?platform=yango&_=$RANDOM (rows_with_raw 36, sampled 36) returns every named field at fill_pct 100 with already_a_column false and mapped_to null: price_commission_service (27 distinct), price_card (18), price_cash (9), price_tip (4: 0 / 2.6 / 7.2 / 7.5), price_mandatory_taxes_fee (2), price_promotion (2), plus short_id, car_id, car_brand_model ('BYD Han') and cancellation_description ('Ride canceled by client'). GET /api/schema/raw-values?platform=yango&key=price_mandatory_taxes_fee -> [{-5, n:12},{0, n:24}] -- the finding's '-5 on 12 of 36' is exact. src/sources/yango.js:214-222 is the whole mapping and `price: o.price` at line 221 is its only monetary field. `grep -rn 'price_commission_service|price_tip|price_card|short_id|cancellation_description|price_cash' api/ src/ sql/` finds no reader; the only price_cash hits are api/analytics_routes.js:1732 and 1774-1778, which read driver_performance.raw, not these. CORRECTION TO THE COUNT: 'ten money fields ... every one discarded' overstates. Four of the ten named -- price_bonus, price_corporate, price_platform_cash_collection, price_commission_park -- have distinct_values 1 with the single value '0' on all 36 rows, as do price_contractor_balance_topup, price_other, price_partner_cashless, price_partner_rides and price_platform_marketing_other. Six carry any variation at all. And nothing is 'discarded': src/sources/yango.js:221 stores `raw: o`, which is precisely what /api/schema/raw-fields is reading. Unmapped and unread, not lost.
intent_check: No comment claims the omission is deliberate, and I checked the obvious place it would be. docs/COVERAGE.md documents the opposite decision at the other grain -- 'Yango | earnings are NET: cash + cashless + commission (commission is negative)' -- which src/sources/yango.js:288-315 implements off the WEEKLY summary's price_platform_commission with a long comment. So the fleet-level net is already handled on purpose; the per-ride commission is genuinely unclaimed rather than considered and declined.
user_visible: Barely anything today. 36 trips, AED 1,812 of gross fare. GET /api/revenue?from=2026-05-01&to=2026-09-05 already picks basis=payout for Yango and its basis_note already tells the reader the fares are 'the gross the riders paid, which is a larger and different figure' -- so no page states a gross as a net. The value is latent: the moment the trip backfill in finding 1 lands, this is the difference between a gross and a net on every Yango ride, on the one channel that publishes its cut per ride. A TRAP THE REPORT MUST CARRY: these price_* fields are a CONSOLE payload. The documented fleet-api.yango.tech orders/list response (verified today) carries a single `price` and no breakdown at all, so migrating to the documented host as findings 2 and 6 propose would LOSE exactly these fields. Whoever acts on this cluster has to keep both surfaces or choose between them knowingly.
fix: src/sources/yango.js:214-222: add commission (Number(o.price_commission_service) || 0), tip, tax and the cash/card split to the trip row mapping, and derive a net alongside `price`. Six lines. Do it in the same change that decides the console-vs-documented-host question from finding 2, not before it.

title: GET /v2/parks/contractors/supply-hours would give per-driver online seconds at any grain -- but the KPI it claims this would repair was re-sourced, not deleted, and the wrong figures it quotes are historical
area: Driver page, Activity tab -- the online-hours KPI and the per-day hours panel
reproduced: The endpoint half reproduces verbatim. https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/openapi/ContractorProfiles/v2parkscontractorssupply-hours-get fetched today: 'Request GET https://fleet-api.yango.tech/v2/parks/contractors/supply-hours', query parameters contractor_profile_id / period_from / period_to (ISO 8601 with time zone, URL-encoding required), 200 body {supply_duration_seconds, total_seconds}, headers X-API-Key AND X-Client-ID AND X-Park-ID -- all three, exactly as claimed. The cited code also reads as claimed: api/driver_routes.js:863-882 is the comment block quoting 428.8 h for Khalil Aliyan and 485.7 h for Fahad Ali; api/driver_routes.js:1213-1236 says 'driver_performance.hours_online has exactly one writer in this codebase -- src/sources/yango.js:86 -- and it files SEVEN-DAY windows, which the period_start = period_end predicate directly above then discards'; sql/schema_v23.sql:64 is exactly `p.hours_online / (p.period_end - p.period_start + 1) AS hours_online`. THE IMPACT CLAIM DOES NOT SURVIVE. 'the daily grain the product had to delete a KPI over' -- the KPI was not deleted, it was re-sourced. The same comment at api/driver_routes.js:876-882 says 'The hours now come from driver_day below, which is a measurement', and api/driver_routes.js:1290-1297 emits hours_online with an explicit hours_online_basis of 'platform' or 'availability'. And 428.8 / 485.7 are quoted in the present tense ('printing 428.8 hours online'); they are historical figures inside a comment describing an already-fixed defect. I could not find either on any live endpoint and the code path that produced them is gone.
intent_check: This is the commonest failure mode in these audits and it happened here. The two comment blocks the finder cites as evidence of a hole are the fix write-ups for that hole. They say in plain English what was wrong, what replaced it, and why the weekly figure is still shown where its grain is visible (the periods table at api/driver_routes.js:1934-1949 groups by period_start/period_end and prints the real bounds). The finder read the description of the bug and reported it as the current state.
user_visible: Nothing. Online hours on the Driver page come from driver_day (spans from driver_timeline_event, clamped to Dubai days by src/rollup.js) with the basis named on the row, and that covers all 289 people on the roster rather than the 12 Yango drivers this endpoint would reach. What supply-hours would add is the platform's own arithmetic as a cross-check on a twelfth of the roster. It is a nice-to-have, it is blocked behind the X-Client-ID the product does not hold (finding 2), and the call shape is one request per driver per day against a documented 429 -- roughly 4,400 calls to cover the 12 drivers for the year the summaries already cover.
fix: If finding 2's probe succeeds and someone still wants it: a per-driver-per-day pull writing driver_performance rows with period_start = period_end, which api/driver_routes.js:1207-1212 already has a query waiting for ('h is left in place because a channel that starts filing daily rows should still win'). Nothing needs changing to receive it. Rank this last in the cluster.

title: POST /v1/parks/driver-profiles/list publishes real driver licence numbers, expiry, country and birth date plus balances -- while the Compliance page states in prose that Yango files no compliance record at all
area: Compliance page -- the Licence expiry / Licence number columns and the emirates_id_caveat sentence
reproduced: Doc fetched today, verbatim: https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/openapi/ContractorProfiles/v1parksdriver-profileslist-post returns {limit, offset, total, driver_profiles:[{accounts:[{id, type, balance, balance_limit, currency}], car:{id, status, amenities, category, callsign, brand, model, year, color, number, registration_cert, vin}, current_status, driver_profile:{id, park_id, created_date, last_name, first_name, middle_name, driver_license:{issue_date, expiration_date, number, normalized_number, country, birth_date}, phones, work_rule_id, work_status, check_message, comment, employment_type, has_contract_issue}}]} -- every field the finding names, with `total` (example 728) and offset/limit paging, so roster size is knowable. https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/openapi/ContractorProfiles/v1parkscontractorsblocked-balance-get: GET /v1/parks/contractors/blocked-balance, query contractor_id, returns balance + blocked_balance + details{blocked_tips, blocked_cashless, blocked_bonuses, blocked_financial_statements, blocked_closing_documents} -- exact. The resource index at https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/all-resources contains no park-level balance operation; ContractorProfiles carries only the per-driver one. api/server.js:4190 is exactly `+ 'every type it exposes, and Bolt and Yango file no compliance record at all, so a '`. GET /api/compliance/drivers?_=$RANDOM now -> emirates_id_by_platform [{hotel, n:123, of_n:132}, {uber, n:0, of_n:157}], and the string 'yango' appears 0 times in the entire payload. STRONGER THAN CLAIMED: the same payload's totals read {total:289, with_date:94, expired:0, within_45:0, placeholder:94, no_date_at_all:195, with_number:94, placeholder_numbers:94, real_numbers:0} -- every licence date and every licence number the product currently holds is a placeholder. This endpoint is the only source anywhere in this cluster that would supply a real expiration_date and a real normalized_number. WEAKER IN ONE RESPECT: it would not supply an Emirates ID, which is what the sentence at server.js:4190 is nominally about. The overclaim is the words 'no compliance record at all', not the Emirates-ID part.
intent_check: The sentence is true of the surface in use -- the console summary endpoint returns driver{id, first_name, last_name, status} and nothing documentary, which is why src/sources/yango.js:333-343 builds driver_platform_state out of status and plate alone. But it is written about the CHANNEL, not about the surface, and nothing anywhere weighs the documented endpoint and declines it. This is an untested assertion in a product whose house rule (docs/COVERAGE.md) is that a figure which cannot be measured renders absent with a reason -- the reason given here is stronger than what was measured.
user_visible: Yes, mildly. Twelve Yango drivers are absent entirely from a 289-person compliance roster, and the Compliance page prints a caveat asserting that the channel publishes nothing when nobody has asked it. Against a page whose real_numbers count is 0, a channel that would answer 12 real licence expiries is not nothing. Blocked behind finding 2.
fix: Two steps and the first is free: soften api/server.js:4190 from 'Bolt and Yango file no compliance record at all' to a statement about the surface in use ('the endpoints this product reads for Bolt and Yango carry no documentary fields'), which is the honest version today. Then, if finding 2's probe returns 200, add a driver-profiles/list pull to src/sources/yango.js writing licence_expires / licence_number into the compliance roster alongside the existing driver_platform_state upsert.

title: The documented orders/list carries pickup lat/lon, route_points, a status event timeline, passenger and corporate-client identity and the driver's work rule -- none of which the console shape the product reads has
area: Yango trip rows; the map/geography surfaces and the unauthorized-trips analysis
reproduced: Doc fetched today, verbatim: https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/openapi/Orders/v1parksorderslist-post 200 body carries address_from:{address, lat, lon}, route_points[], events:[{event_at, order_status}], created_at distinct from booked_at, provider, category, amenities[], type:{id,name}, driver_work_rule:{id,name}, cancellation_description, and park_details:{tariff, passenger:{name, phones}, company:{id, name, slip, comment}}; the request filters are order.ids, short_ids, booked_at, ended_at, type, statuses, payment_methods, providers, categories, price{from,to}, driver_profile.id and car.id, with limit and cursor. OrderShortId is documented exactly as 'Index number of the order (with canceled orders taken into account)'. https://fleet.yango.com/docs/api/en/openapi/Orders/v1parksorderstrack-post: POST /v1/parks/orders/track, query order_id + park_id, returns track:[{tracked_at, location:{lat,lon}, speed, order_status, direction, distance}] -- exact. Against that: src/sources/yango.js:218 is `pickup_addr: o.address_from, dropoff_addr: o.address_to`, and GET /api/schema/raw-fields?platform=yango shows address_from at fill 100 with plain string examples ('12, Al Hubob Street, Dubai Marina, Jumeirah, Dubai') and no lat, lon, events, passenger or work-rule key anywhere in the 33 fields sampled. GET /api/coverage geo -> {dataset:'trip:yango', n:36, with_pickup:0, with_dropoff:0, pickup_pct:0, dropoff_pct:0}. CORRECTION: 'the only booking-channel GPS in this whole product' is too strong -- the same /api/coverage geo block shows trip:fms at 100%/100% and trip:hotel at 68%/66% pickup/dropoff. Yango's track would be the only per-order GPS TRACK from a ride-hailing channel, which is the defensible version.
intent_check: Not a decision anybody made. The console payload simply has no such fields, and src/sources/yango.js's mapping stores what arrives. No comment anywhere considers the documented order shape. Same root as finding 2 -- I considered merging 4, 5 and 6 into it and did not, because they name three different capabilities with three different fixes and only share a precondition; the report should carry finding 2 first and these three as gated on it.
user_visible: Nothing today -- 36 bookings with pickup_pct 0 is invisible next to 221,119 FMS journeys at 100%. It matters only if the trip feed is repaired: docs/AUDIT.md's unauthorized-trips section turns on matching telemetry to bookings channel by channel, and a Yango channel with per-order tracks and status events would be the strongest matchable booking feed in the product. Blocked behind finding 2. Note the same trap as finding 3: the documented order object has a single `price` and none of the ten console price_* fields, so this and finding 3 cannot both be satisfied by one surface.
fix: Nothing until finding 2's probe answers. If it returns 200, the decision to write down is which surface is canonical -- documented host for geo/events/passenger/work-rule, console for the per-trip money breakdown, or both -- and src/sources/yango.js pullTrips gains address_from.lat/lon into the existing pickup/dropoff geo columns plus events[] into raw. Do not schedule the per-order track pull until the trip feed itself is whole.

title: occupancy_segment accumulates the output of every reconcile pass — 59.6% of rows are superseded fragments, and one is a live accusation against a named driver that the current build no longer makes
area: #unauthorized (every KPI tile, the donut, the daily chart), #segments/* and its facets, the vehicle Segments tab, #day
reproduced: Pulled every day 2026-08-20..2026-09-05 via GET /api/segments?from=D&to=D&limit=500&_=$RANDOM: 3,284 rows, which equals GET /api/unauthorized/summary?days=30&_=$RANDOM (segments 3,284; km 41,035+31,661+378+2,559+741 = 76,374). Grouping by plate, 1,958 rows (59.6%, 47,291 km) are intervals strictly contained inside a longer segment on the SAME plate; de-duplicated that leaves exactly 1,326 segments and 29,084 km — the finder's kept-side numbers to the unit. 1,380 of the superseded rows carry boundary_gap_min = NULL (pre-schema_v8). Stronger proof than nesting: channels_checked is written once per pass, and six distinct values coexist on the same days — 2026-08-23 holds 139 rows reading 'hotel,uber,yango' and 56 reading 'bolt,hotel,uber,yango'; 2026-08-26 holds three different cohorts. intent_check: The guard IS deliberate and heavily documented — src/reconcile.js:209-218, AUDIT.md finding 16, and sql/schema_v8.sql cause 2 ('Bolt and Yango had zero trip rows in the database while their collectors reported ok... A segment could not possibly be matched to a Bolt booking, and was called unauthorised'). It was written after the detector named eleven drivers for trips they had genuinely run. So this is not a bug report; it is a threshold that has no share weighting. The finder did not read that history, and the report must say the guard is doing what it was built to do. What is NOT deliberate is the silence: api/server.js:2383 computes totals.low_confidence as `count(*) FILTER (WHERE verdict='unauthorized' AND low_confidence)`, while src/reconcile.js:373 sets low_confidence only for verdict 'unverifiable' or 'pending'. user_visible: Yes. For four days running #unauthorized has led with 'Every journey in this window has a booking behind it' and 'Unexplained trips 0'. Nothing on that page names Yango or says the detector is refusing to judge: the tiles say 'Could not be verified 17 — a revenue channel was unreadable at the time' without naming which, and the banner written to name it is dead code. (1) api/server.js:2383 — drop the impossible `verdict='unauthorized' AND` so the banner at app.js:3151 can fire; that alone makes the Yango veto visible on the page instead of silent. (2) src/reconcile.js:215-218 — weight blockingChannels by share: keep a channel as blocking only if it produced some minimum fraction (say >=1%) of bookings in a comparable recent window, or has ever matched a segment on this fleet; otherwise issue `unauthorized` with unavailable_sources set and low_confidence true, so the caveat travels with the verdict rather than replacing it. user_visible: Yes. It is 12:27 Dubai and #unauthorized on the 'today' chip reports 7 occupancy intervals, 3 matched, covering nothing after 06:59 Dubai — and /api/unauthorized/summary?period=today returns coverage {days_with_data 1, days_in_window 1, complete: true}, so the one warning that exists for thin evidence explicitly tells the reader the day is fully covered. The same latency is what decides how long a false accusation stands: a segment flagged at 09:00 is only re-judged when the next full pass completes, which on this measurement is not for another seven hours, against a design cadence of 30 minutes. Pair it with the finding-1 delete so an out-of-band pass corrects rows rather than adding to them. Separately, the coverage.complete flag in api/server.js should compare against the newest reconciled segment, not against days_with_data, so a half-reconciled today does not report as complete.

title: snapToBucket widens the month and week grains on a partial refresh but not the day grain, so rollup_day keeps rows the live table has lost
area: Overview daily bars vs the KPI row above them; /api/rollups health table
reproduced: Mechanism proven with a controlled split the finder did not run. Across 2026-08-01..08-21 (BEFORE the 14-day cutoff of 08-22): /api/trips/daily summed = 7,779 priced / 461,134.34 against /api/kpis = 7,778 / 461,045 - differs. Across 2026-08-22..08-31 (INSIDE the refresh window): 4,742 / 279,723.10 against 4,742 / 279,723 - agrees exactly. Whole month: /api/trips/daily 12,521 / 740,857.44 vs /api/kpis and /api/trend/monthly both 12,520 / 740,768. Isolated day: /api/trips/daily?from=2026-08-19&to=2026-08-19 -> priced 405, revenue 24,655.01; /api/day?day=2026-08-19 -> priced 404, revenue 24,566. Code confirmed: src/rollup.js:141 returns 'since' unchanged for day, :132 snaps month to the 1st, :136-139 snaps week to Monday; src/index.js:65 is the '*/15' refreshRollups({days:14}) pass and :72 the '40 22 * * *' full rebuild; src/index.js:129 is the 01:45 uberAuditTick. The health-table claim also holds: src/rollup.js:226-231 writes covers_from/covers_to from 'SELECT min(local_day), max(local_day) FROM trip_norm' - the whole table - so /api/rollups shows rollup_day covering 2024-10-01 -> 2026-09-05 at age_min 15 after a pass that only recomputed 14 days. The drift persisted across ~13 quarter-hourly passes between my first and last check, confirming it is structural rather than lag.
intent_check: Partly anticipated, not fully. src/rollup.js:121-130 documents snapToBucket's purpose precisely - 'a partial pass must never rebuild a bucket from part of it' - which is about wholeness, not freshness; the day-grain widening is a side effect nobody wrote down. src/index.js:67-71 shows the authors know the narrow pass is blind beyond a fortnight and intend the nightly full rebuild as the remedy. What is undocumented is the asymmetry INSIDE the fortnight: rollup_month is rebuilt whole from 08-01 every 15 minutes while rollup_day is untouched before 08-22, so the two grains disagree for up to ~21 hours. Real, and no doc covers it.
user_visible: Barely - and the finder's severity is wrong. The whole discrepancy is one trip of 12,520 and AED 89.34 of AED 740,768: 0.012%. No reader sees it without summing 31 bars by hand; the only click-through symptom is 19 Aug reading 24,655 on the Overview chart and 24,566 on its own day page, 0.36% of that day. The finder's claim that #reconcile shows it does NOT hold: /api/reconcile?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 returns trips 13,950 for 2026-08, which matches /api/kpis exactly - the drift is confined to priced_trips and revenue, and reconcile's visible trips column is unaffected. It also self-heals at the 22:40 UTC full rebuild. Downgraded high -> low: the mechanism is sound and cheap to fix, and the latent hazard (an upsert that never deletes, so a bucket that has lost rows keeps them) could bite harder after a large backfill correction, but nothing a person reads today is meaningfully wrong.
fix: Make the narrow pass DELETE-then-INSERT the affected day range in refreshGrain (src/rollup.js:144+) so a bucket that has lost rows cannot keep them - that closes the class, not just today's one trip. Separately, record on rollup_state what the pass actually recomputed (the snapped 'since' -> covers_to) instead of min/max local_day of the whole table at src/rollup.js:226-231, so /api/rollups stops asserting a two-year span is 15 minutes old.

title: /api/day compares a part-finished today against a fortnight median of whole days and the page tones it critical - the rule the codebase documents for #compare and never applied here
area: The day page for today, which COVERAGE.md records as the link target of both the desktop live band and the phone's 'Today so far' card
reproduced: GET /api/day?day=2026-09-05 at 08:31 UTC (12:31 Dubai) -> headline.bookings 71, first_at 2026-09-04T20:00:03Z (00:00 Dubai), last_at 2026-09-05T03:24:22Z (07:24 Dubai), versus_neighbours.median_bookings 689, delta_pct -89.7, series 08-29 569, 08-30 466, 08-31 666, 09-01 689, 09-02 787, 09-03 817, 09-04 800 - seven whole neighbour days plus today (the finder wrote 'eight whole days' and listed seven; the eighth entry is today itself). The response carries no cut_minutes, cut_label, is_today or partial field. Code confirmed exactly: api/day_routes.js:296 'delta_pct: median ? round(((h.bookings - median) / median) * 100, 1) : null' with no cut term; api/public/day.js:65 'vs.delta_pct < -30 ? critical : vs.delta_pct < -10 ? warn'. Grepping today|partial|is_today|cut across api/day_routes.js and api/public/day.js returns only three unrelated comment hits. The contrast is live: GET /api/compare?a=2026-09-04&b=2026-09-05 returns is_today, cut_minutes 765, cut_label '12:45', cut_mode and cut_note. (Finder cited cut 555/'09:15'; it moved because time passed, which is the field working.)
intent_check: The opposite of a deliberate choice - the codebase states this exact rule and fails to apply it here. api/compare_routes.js:1-15 opens: 'TODAY IS NOT OVER. At 11:00 Dubai, today holds seven hours of work and yesterday holds twenty-four. Subtract them and every driver on the fleet is down 70%, every platform is collapsing, and the page says so in red. That page is worse than no page - it manufactures an alarm every morning and cries wolf by lunchtime.' /api/day does precisely what that paragraph forbids. This is the strongest intent verdict in the cluster: the house rule is written down, and one page follows it while its neighbour does not.
user_visible: Yes, every morning, on the most-linked-to day page in the product. The Bookings tile renders 71 with the sub-line '-89.7% on the fortnight median of 689' toned critical (below the -30 threshold), for a day that is a third over. Worth noting the underlying figure is stale as well - last_at has not moved past 07:24 Dubai in the three hours I was checking - which makes the manufactured delta larger still, but the comparison would be wrong even with fresh data.
fix: Give /api/day the cut /api/compare already computes: when the requested day is the Dubai today, count the neighbour days to the same wall-clock minute and return cut_minutes/cut_label on the response so api/public/day.js:65 can tone against a like-for-like number. If that is too much for now, return delta_pct as null with a stated reason ('this day is still running') from api/day_routes.js:296 - a null already suppresses both the sub-line and the tone at api/public/day.js:63-65, so the page needs no change to stop crying wolf.

title: /api/vehicle/kpis never selects booking_days, so payout coverage divides by the calendar window and 45 of 98 earning plates report Uber's gross fare as the car's income — AED 64,548.64 above the asset ledger
area: Vehicle page (#vehicle/<plate>), the 'Money in' and 'Fares' tiles — contradicting the same car's row in the fleet directory (#vehicles) and the asset ledger (#unit)
reproduced:
Swept all 98 earning plates for 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 today. sum of /api/vehicle/kpis?plate=

&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 .accounted = 567,258.53; /api/economics/assets?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 .totals.money = 502,709.89 (fares 95,365.70 + payouts 407,344.19) and /api/vehicles/directory sums to 502,709.89 to the cent. Excess 64,548.64 on exactly 45 plates, every one with accounted_payouts null and undercovered_bookings 0. /api/vehicle/kpis?plate=L46185&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 -> accounted 11,986.98, accounted_fares 11,986.98, accounted_payouts null, attributed_earnings 6,355.12; directory row 1,842.00 + 6,355.12 = 8,197.12 (+46.2%). /api/vehicle/earnings?plate=L46185 -> uber fares 10,244.98 over 188 priced bookings. Worst overstatements now: L12615 1,372.46 -> 3,310.87 (+141.2%), L64172 683.93 -> 1,475.65 (+115.8%), L44286 1,492.62 -> 3,017.72 (+102.2%), L91636 (+89.7%), L41443 (+84.7%). Code matches: api/vehicle_routes.js:826 seeds booking_days:0; the fareByPlat SQL at api/vehicle_routes.js:808-818 selects bookings/priced/chargeable/uncharged/fares and no booking_days; api/vehicle_routes.js:832-834 carries only those; api/income_sql.js:163 `const base = r.booking_days > 0 ? r.booking_days : windowDays;`.
intent_check: The opposite of deliberate — the repo documents this exact denominator as required and then missed this copy. api/income_sql.js:87-89 labels booking_days 'The days this channel actually worked inside the window. This is the denominator payout coverage needs'; :112-131 gives two reasons it must not be the calendar. Commit 56a20d2 ('An open window reported a complete record as 0.1% covered') introduced booking_days and touched vehicle_routes.js by two lines — the fleet-level platformFares path only, not the per-plate fareByPlat copy. The file has been through this class of miss twice already (9296e6b 'The finer denominator was computed and then not carried', ea85d05 'Six queries compute fare coverage and only one had learned the denominator') for chargeable_bookings, on these same queries. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md or docs/AUDIT.md defends a calendar denominator here. api/income_sql.js:183-214 states the governing rule (THE PAYOUT WINS) and warns in terms that describe this bug exactly: 'at 80% the old rule would have flipped Uber's August from AED 428,083 to roughly AED 640,000 with nothing on the page to mark the change'.
user_visible: Yes, and worse than the finding said. The 'Money in' tile (api/public/vehicle.js:144-148) prints AED 11,986.98 for L46185 with the subtitle 'AED 11,986.98 in fares · AED 0 attributed from platform payouts' — on a car whose own earnings panel three sections down shows AED 6,355.12 attributed from Uber. So the page contradicts itself, not just the fleet table. The money substituted in is Uber's gross, which Uber takes 25% of before the fleet is paid, captioned 'in fares'. undercovered_bookings is 0, so nothing marks the substitution. 45 of the 98 cars an operator would rank by earnings are affected, up to +141.2%.
fix: Add `count(DISTINCT local_day)::int booking_days` to the fareByPlat SELECT at api/vehicle_routes.js:808-818 and carry it in the Object.assign at api/vehicle_routes.js:832-834 — exactly what api/economics_routes.js:246/459 and the directory's `chan` CTE at api/vehicle_routes.js:169 already do. Fix the identical omission at api/driver_routes.js:983-994 / 1010-1012 in the same change, or /api/driver/kpis keeps the bug. Optional belt-and-braces, and consistent with the documented rule: in api/income_sql.js:235 require `r.payouts == null` on the `fares` branch so a channel that HAS a payout falls through to partial_payout instead of reporting its gross.

title: /api/vehicle/kpis computes windowDays one day too long, because it subtracts win()'s endOfDay-widened bound
area: Vehicle page 'Money in' tile and every basis_note it prints; worst on short windows
reproduced: api/vehicle_routes.js:837 reads `const windowDays = Math.round((Date.parse(p[1]) - Date.parse(p[0])) / 86400000) + 1;` and p comes from `[...win(req), plate]` (api/vehicle_routes.js:42), where win() returns `[from, `${to} 23:59:59.999`]` (api/window.js:288-292). Ran the expression: 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 -> 32 (true 31); 2026-08-30..2026-09-05 -> 8 (true 7); 2026-09-05..2026-09-05 -> 2 (true 1). Robust to timezone — the non-ISO bound parses as local time, so under Asia/Dubai the span is 30d20h, which still rounds to 31 and yields 32. Money claim verified: of the 45 plates in finding 1, exactly 5 have payout_days 25 (25/31 = 80.6% passes the gate, 25/32 = 78.1% fails) — L29405 +3,581.97, L40959 +3,049.76, L45235 +2,821.69, L46173 +1,590.40, L16308 +1,541.47 = 12,585.29, matching the finding to the fils. Short-window effect live today: /api/vehicle/kpis?plate=L36397&from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-01 -> accounted 1,124.29 with accounted_payouts null, against attributed_earnings 798.86 on the same response. api/economics_routes.js:78-79 does the same sum correctly.
intent_check: Not deliberate. api/vehicle_routes.js:346-350, in the sibling /api/vehicles/directory handler in the same file, spells out the correct form and why — 'Whole Dubai days, inclusive — the denominator chooseBasis measures a channel's payout coverage against. Date.parse on a bare YYYY-MM-DD is UTC midnight for both ends, so the subtraction is exact' — and computes it from winDays. The kpis handler simply reuses the timestamp bounds it already had in `p`. No comment anywhere defends a +1 day span.
user_visible: Yes today, but nothing that finding 1's fix would not also cure. Its whole measured money impact (AED 12,585.29 over 5 plates) is a subset of finding 1's AED 64,548.64, and once booking_days is carried, windowDays becomes the fallback only for a channel with a payout and no booking in the window. What survives independently is the basis_note text — 'net payout covering only N of the M day(s) this channel worked' names an M one larger than any window ever requested — and the short-window flip demonstrated above.
fix: One line. api/vehicle_routes.js:837 -> `const windowDays = Math.max(1, Math.round((Date.parse(`${to}T00:00:00Z`) - Date.parse(`${from}T00:00:00Z`)) / 864e5) + 1);` with `const [from, to] = winDays(req);`, copying api/vehicle_routes.js:349-350 verbatim. api/driver_routes.js:1015 carries the identical expression and needs the same edit.

area: Vehicle page — 'Idle days' and 'Bookings' tiles, the trips-and-idle daily chart, the movement day list; and the mismatch against #vehicles and #unit
reproduced: All reproduced today. /api/vehicle/daily?plate=L36397&from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-01 returns TWO rows: 2026-09-01 (24 trips) and 2026-09-02 (0 trips, 29 fixes). /api/vehicle/kpis for that identical single-day window returns days_earning 1 AND idle_days 1. /api/vehicle/movement?plate=L36397&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 -> days run 2026-08-21..2026-09-01, the last entry being 2026-09-01 with 38 fixes. Fleet-wide over 2026-08-01..2026-08-31: 15 of the 98 earning plates report days_earning 31 with idle_days > 0 (L36397, L90721, L36395, L46174, L46183, L45243, L95161, L45227, L45205, L64921, L44305, L45255, L60853, L19249, L57952); 24 of 98 disagree with /api/economics/assets on booking count; totals 13,936 (assets/directory) vs 13,923 (kpis) and km 170,809 vs 170,527. Sharpest single instance: /api/vehicle/kpis?plate=L46183&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 reports days_worked 32 for a 31-day window. Code matches: api/vehicle_routes.js:29 `const TW = 'plate = $3 AND requested_at BETWEEN $1 AND $2'`, used at :667, :746, :780, :818, :871, :959, :981, :997, :1198, :1203, :1218, :1220, alongside raw `captured_at`/`occurred_at`/`started_at` BETWEEN at :760, :766, :772, :876, :879, :1038-1078 — while the SELECTs bucket on local_day or `AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Dubai'`.
intent_check: Documented as a bug, already fixed elsewhere. api/driver_routes.js:251-254 names this exact defect on the driver directory — 'the window was bound as a raw timestamptz in a UTC session, so it dropped the Dubai 00:00-04:00 slice of the first day and added a phantom one after the last — and the /api/vehicles panel on the same screen used Dubai days, so the two disagreed about the same plate.' And this very handler already knows: api/vehicle_routes.js:684-686 says 'on the Dubai calendar this product keys every day on — winDays, not the timestamp bounds in p' and uses winDays for the alert-coverage half while leaving TW on the timestamp bounds. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md or docs/AUDIT.md defends it.
user_visible: Yes. The 'Idle days' tile is painted warn at 1-3 and critical above (api/public/vehicle.js:167-169) and shows 1 idle day on 15 cars that earned on all 31 days of the window; on a single-day view it shows 'days earning 1, idle days 1' for the same day. The daily chart draws a bar for a day the reader did not ask for, and movement lists 2026-09-01 under an August window. And the same car reads 387 bookings on the fleet table and 386 on its own page (L36397), 200 vs 196 (L45243), 131 vs 132 (L38439) — it shifts in both directions, so it cannot be read as a truncation.
fix: Make withVehicle pass Dubai days: api/vehicle_routes.js:42 -> `fn(req, res, plate, [...winDays(req), plate])`, and change TW at :29 to `plate = $3 AND local_day BETWEEN $1::date AND $2::date`. Then convert the raw-timestamp predicates in the same pass to `(captured_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Dubai')::date BETWEEN $1::date AND $2::date` (and the same for alert.occurred_at and occupancy_segment.started_at) — with winDays bounds, a bare `BETWEEN $1 AND $2` on a timestamptz would now drop the last day entirely. The ::date comparisons already in the file (e.g. :912, :1104) are unaffected. About 20 predicates in one file; /api/vehicles/handover at :508 already uses winDays and is correct.

title: The handover panel's improvement target is built largely on one person's two platform accounts: 50 of its 68 cars name two spellings of one name as their worst change-over, and none of the 58 such pairs shares a platform
area: Vehicles page, 'Hours between drivers' panel — its lede, its 'Change-overs'/'Hours idle' ranking and its 'That one was' column
reproduced: Fetched today. /api/vehicles/handover?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 -> totals handovers 583, plates 68, handover_h 4,602.1, quick_h 1.9, recoverable_h 3,494.4. Of the 68 plate rows, 50 have worst_from and worst_to as whitespace-token subsets of one another; those 50 carry 376 of the 583 change-overs and 3,311.3 of the 4,602.1 idle hours (72%) — the finding's figures, exact. I went further than the finding and reconstructed the gaps themselves from /api/vehicle/drivers-detail on all 68 plates (597 gaps / 4,824.6 h against the API's 583 / 4,602.1, the difference being last_end_at, which drivers-detail does not expose): 370 of 597 gaps and 3,422.1 of 4,824.6 hours (71%) fall BETWEEN a token-subset name pair, so the plate-level proxy is not flattering itself. Across those 68 plates there are 58 such name pairs and ZERO of them share a platform — every one is an Uber UUID against a bolt/hotel/yango id. Top row L77062 verified: /api/vehicle/drivers-detail shows only 'Simon Leonard Mirano' (uber af95b655-7caf-43d5-920b-3ad907bbb3fb) and 'SIMON LEONARD SANMOCTE MIRANO' (bolt 8773066); /api/driver/vehicles for each id returns exactly one plate, L77062, both over 2026-03-10..2026-09-04.
intent_check: The register is deliberate and the finding correctly does not attack it: api/identity_map.js:1-45 states that the fold must never widen, that a merge is a hand-checked LIST and not a rule, and that 'a name it has not been told about is two people, which is the default this product is built to be wrong in the direction of.' Two corrections to the finding, neither fatal. (a) Its evidence for L40965 is wrong at the endpoint it cites: /api/driver/vehicles?id=6640364 returns FIVE plates (L40965, L74169, L82907, L44286, L44289), not 'only plate L40965' — only L40965 falls inside the window. (b) A token subset is not the register's signature on its own: api/identity_map.js:164-168 REFUSES 'Muhammad Khalid Gul' / 'Muhammad Khalid' as two people on 77 simultaneous trips, and the refused id 76ede4ae-768b-4126-804b-0b5c88043682 turns up inside one of my 58 pairs (against bolt 'Muhammad Khalifa Afzal Khalid' on L76092). What separates these 58 from that refusal is the discriminator the register itself uses — different channels, one shared plate, no platform overlap in any pair — which is suggestive, not proof. The panel's three caveats (api/public/vehicle.js:1078-1101: within-day alternation, day-plus gaps, missing drop-off times) do not mention this one.
user_visible: Yes, but as a missing caveat rather than a wrong number: every figure the panel prints is correct for its stated definition. What a reader sees is the lede '583 change-overs on 68 cars left the fleet standing for 4,602 h ... every change-over at that speed would give back 3,494 h' (api/public/vehicle.js:1029-1037) presented as the fleet's improvement target, with ~71% of those hours sitting between two spellings of one name; and the 'That one was' column (api/public/vehicle.js:1065-1073) rendering two clickable driver links that plausibly open the same human, asking the operator to have a 23.2-hour conversation with him about handing a car to himself.
fix: Do the cheap, safe half first: have /api/vehicles/handover return a count and hour-sum of gaps whose two person keys are one a whitespace-token subset of the other on different platforms, and print it beside the total in api/public/vehicle.js:1029-1037 as a fourth caveat, so the headline cannot be read as 583 changes of hands. The register half is a separate, manual job (the discriminator is api/identity_map.js:66-91 and /api/driver/vehicles answers it in one call per id) — and note before starting that api/identity_map.js:51's ID regex accepts only 24-hex, 32-hex or a dashed UUID, so the short numeric Bolt ids here (8773066, 6640364) would make assertRegister() throw at import; the regex has to be widened first.

title: /api/economics/assets over-reports the payout it cannot place, because unattributedEarnings sums whole payout periods that merely touch the window while its other half prorates
area: Economics / asset ledger (#unit), the 'Money we cannot place' tile
reproduced: Fetched today. /api/economics/assets?from=2026-08-15&to=2026-08-15 -> attributed 11,577.90, unplaced_payouts 1,549.61, unplaced_pct 11.8. /api/revenue?from=2026-08-15&to=2026-08-15 -> uber payouts 11,551.64 + yango 204.29 = 11,755.93, so the genuinely unplaced share of that day is about 178.03, i.e. ~1.5%. Decisive additional check the finding did not run: unplaced_payouts does not scale with the window at all. 2026-08-15..2026-08-15 -> 1,549.61; 2026-08-16..2026-08-16 -> 1,549.61 (identical); the whole week 2026-08-10..2026-08-16 -> 1,570.62 (1.9%); 2026-08-13..2026-08-17 -> 1,651.47; 2026-08-15..2026-08-22 -> 1,642.42; 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 -> 4,715.69 (1.1%). A one-day window returns essentially the whole week's unplaced pay. Code matches: api/attribution_sql.js:146-158 selects `sum(p.earnings)` for every period with `period_end >= $1 AND period_start <= $2` and no proration, while attributedEarnings beside it weights per vehicle-day and clips at api/attribution_sql.js:134 `WHERE vd.day BETWEEN $1::date AND $2::date`. Surfaced at api/economics_routes.js:663-665 and api/public/economics.js:428-432 (and again in prose at api/public/economics.js:358-359).
intent_check: Not deliberate — it violates an invariant this codebase states twice and asserts once. api/attribution_sql.js:30-33 (rule 3): 'the attributed total over all plates equals the payout total minus the unattributed remainder. That is an arithmetic identity, and test/attribution.test.mjs asserts it rather than trusting it.' api/economics_routes.js:659-662: 'Measured against the ATTRIBUTED total rather than against money in, so the two visibly partition one set of periods: attributed + unplaced is what the platforms paid.' test/economics.test.mjs:137-139 asserts `|placed + unplaced - sum(driver_payout_day.earnings)| < 1` over 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 — and on production that is 410,800.00 + 4,715.69 = 415,515.69 against 410,643.15, off by 4,872.54. The fixture window evidently contains whole periods; production's does not. attributedEarnings carries a long comment on why the window applies to the vehicle-day; unattributedEarnings carries none, which is the shape of an omission.
user_visible: Yes, on short windows. The tile reads 'Money we cannot place · AED 1,549.61 · 11.8% of what the platforms paid' for 2026-08-15 when the honest figures are roughly AED 178 and 1.5% — and it is exactly the tile a reader consults when the asset ledger does not sum to the Revenue page. Two corrections to the finding's framing, both downward. The percentage error is the dominant harm, not the money: on the default month the absolute overstatement is about AED 3-4k on a page showing AED 502,709.89. And the '4,872.54 more than the platforms paid' is not all this bug — attributed is trip-weighted while driver_payout_day is evenly spread (schema_v23.sql:53-96), so the two only reconcile exactly over whole periods; attributed alone already exceeds the payout total by 156.85 over August. The un-prorated unplaced sum is the large term, not the whole term.
fix: Prorate the unattributed half the way the attributed half is. Smallest change in api/attribution_sql.js:146-158: multiply each period's earnings by its overlap with the window — `sum(p.earnings * (least(p.period_end, $2::date) - greatest(p.period_start, $1::date) + 1)::numeric / (p.period_end - p.period_start + 1))`. Cleaner and exactly consistent with the other half: read driver_payout_day instead of driver_payout and filter `day BETWEEN $1::date AND $2::date`, since driver_payout is defined as its per-period aggregate (sql/schema_v23.sql:146-165). Give test/economics.test.mjs a fixture whose window clips a period mid-way, or the assertion at :137-139 keeps passing on whole periods.

title: The Calendar column of #demand's context panel is dropped on every window and its absent line — "no public holiday, Ramadan day or forecast day falls in this window" — prints unconditionally, including over a year containing Ramadan
area: #demand — "Volume against the weather and the calendar" panel (NOT the Overview, as the finding says)
reproduced: GET /api/context?days=365&_=$RANDOM returns 46 rows, 2026-07-22 → 2026-09-05, is_ramadan true on 0, is_holiday true on 0; /api/context?days=90 returns the identical 46 rows. calendar_day does hold the data: /api/day?day=2026-02-18&_=$RANDOM → hijri_month "Ramaḍān", is_ramadan true. Code at api/server.js:3908-3911 is `FROM weather_daily w LEFT JOIN calendar_day c USING (day) WHERE w.day BETWEEN $1 AND $2` — as claimed. Rendered (headless chromium over production data): on #demand?days=365 the table shows 13 monthly rows including Feb 1 and Mar 1 2026, and underneath prints verbatim "Calendar — no public holiday, Ramadan day or forecast day falls in this window". On #demand?from=2026-02-18&to=2026-03-19 — the exact span of Ramadan 1447 — the whole panel collapses to "No weather rows for this range yet." On the default 5-day window the same denial sentence prints.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and the finder found only half the cause. api/public/app.js:1325-1327 says the absent line exists because "A window with no marked day in it is the normal case" — written on the assumption the column can ever be populated. It cannot: the column is declared `{ label: 'Calendar', key: '_c', absent: … }` at api/public/app.js:1327-1334, and api/public/ui.js:194-196 prunes a column whose declared `absent` and whose raw field `r[c.key]` is blank on every row — `_c` is never a row field, so filled() is 0 on every window and the column is dropped and the denial printed whatever the calendar says. app.js:1232-1234 documents this exact trap for the neighbouring `open_yet` column ("tableFrom prunes a column no row carries a key for, so a value derived purely inside render() vanishes") and the Calendar column was not given the same treatment. So the finding's proposed fix — flipping the join — is necessary but NOT sufficient: the sentence would still print.
user_visible: An affirmative false statement on a live page: over a 365-day window whose own table lists February and March 2026, #demand asserts that no public holiday or Ramadan day falls in the window. Over a window that is Ramadan, the panel renders nothing at all. The "Ramadan days" and "Holidays" KPI tiles (app.js:1220-1221, 1307-1311) are computed off the same 46-day payload, so they silently never appear.
fix: Two changes, both needed. (1) api/server.js:3908-3911: join FROM calendar_day c LEFT JOIN weather_daily w USING (day) and bound on c.day, so the 731 calendar days survive and the weather columns come back null outside the ~46-day horizon (the page already renders null weather as em-dashes). (2) api/public/app.js:1230-1234: stamp the calendar flag onto the row the way `open_yet` is stamped (e.g. `_c: [holiday, ramadan, forecast].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || null`) so ui.js:194 sees a real field and the column survives when there is something to show. Without (2), (1) changes nothing on screen.

title: Errored audit windows leave the agreement denominator silently, and the count of what was excluded is printed on a different tile than the number it qualifies

title: The probe counts Bolt's in-body refusals as ANSWERING and offers the refusal's own error keys as fields we could store; the fleet-orders probe sends company_id where Bolt wants company_ids, so that surface has never been validly asked
area: Providers page ("What each provider sends") — the Answering / Refused / Fields-we-are-not-keeping tiles
reproduced: GET /api/probe/results?_=$RANDOM, last_probe 2026-09-05T03:33:56.352Z. bolt/ecosine:getDrivers ok=true http_status=200 record_count=0, fields code=503, error_hint=COMPANIES_NOT_ALLOWED, message=NOT_AUTHORIZED, unmapped=['code','error_hint','message']. bolt/ecosine:getFleetOrders and bolt/egari:getFleetOrders both ok=true record_count=1, top_keys ['code','message','validation_errors'], the single 'record' being {error:'Is not array', property:'company_ids'}, unmapped=['error','property']. src/probe.js:90 ERROR_KEYS lacks 'code'/'error_hint' and payloadError requires EVERY top-level key to match, so it returns null; src/probe.js:494 `const refusal = arr ? null : payloadError(data)` skips the check entirely once firstList() finds validation_errors. api/public/providers.js:35 requires every field key to match /^(error|message|fault|status|code)$/, which 'error_hint' and 'property' do not. intent_check: Not a deliberate choice — the opposite, and this strengthens the finding. src/probe.js:85-90 and api/public/providers.js:28-35 both carry comments saying they exist specifically to catch "a 200 whose body is only an error object ... a refusal wearing a success code". Nothing in docs/AUDIT.md or docs/COVERAGE.md covers it.
user_visible: On the Providers page: "Answering 18 of 28" (should be 15), "Refused or missing 10" (should be 13), and the verdict headline "10 surfaces would not answer". "Fields we are not keeping" reads 136, of which 7 are the refusals' own error keys (code, error_hint, message, error, property) offered as columns to go and build. (a) Replace the ERROR_KEYS enumeration at src/probe.js:90-97 with Bolt's documented envelope test — a non-zero numeric `code` with no data array, or a `validation_errors` key present — reusing fiRefusal()/NOT_ENTITLED from src/sources/bolt.js:97-124, and move the check at src/probe.js:494 ahead of the `arr ?` guard so a validation_errors array cannot mask it. (b) At src/probe.js:440 send `company_ids: [company.companyId]` for getFleetOrders so the surface can be evaluated at all. Then relax api/public/providers.js:35 to trust the probe's refusal flag rather than re-deriving it from field names.

area: Money/overview page (#money, and the header on every window-scoped page) and the Revenue page platform table
reproduced: Per-day GET /api/revenue?from=D&to=D&_=$RANDOM at 08:56Z, uber row, statement_net: 08-25 18773.40, 08-27 18773.40, 08-29 18773.40, 08-30 18773.40 | 08-31 14874.92, 09-01 14874.92, 09-02 14874.92, 09-03 14874.92, 09-04 14874.92, 09-05 14874.92, 09-06 14874.92 — identical to the cent, statement_drivers 229 on all seven, while measured fares on the same rows run 31798.19 / 31966.58 / 37549.77 / 40667.22 / 39076.65 / 2898.54 / null and payouts DO vary (19871.39 / 19429.74 / 24283.98 / 24546.77 / 25913.23 / 2265.94 / 12673.86). GET /api/kpis?period=today → statement_net 14874.92 beside accounted 3026.37, window.partial true. Every figure the finder quoted is unchanged. The spread is deliberate and defended in two places: src/rollup.js:643-645 ("spreading each week evenly over its days the same way the payout resolution spreads its periods") and sql/schema_v44.sql, which states outright "Not a fix to the allocation itself — spreading is the right thing to do with a weekly total that has to join to days... The fix is that it stops being silent." The money is real and correct over a whole week. What IS a defect is the second half of that same decision: schema_v44 added driver_statement_day.period_days precisely so "a page can then say 'a seventh of a week' instead of stating an allocation as a fact", and its COMMENT ON COLUMN reads "A row with period_days > 1 is an allocation and must not be presented as a measurement of its day." driver.js, trip.js, reconcile.js, provenance.js and m/screens.js all honour that column; api/income_sql.js's platformStatements never selects it, so /api/revenue and /api/kpis — the two largest money surfaces — are the only readers still silent.
user_visible: Yes, on a fully UI-reachable path.
