GET /api/revenue?period=2026-09&_=$RANDOM -> totals.accounted 112470.34, accounted_payouts 96661.8, accounted_fares 15808.54. Gap +55,742.96 = +49.56%, still exactly as filed. I re-derived it rather than trusting it: the gap is precisely uber (152158.76 gross fares - 96439.66 net payout = 55719.10) plus yango (246.00 - 222.14 = 23.86) = 55742.96. The trend figure is the exact sum of all four channels' GROSS fares: 152158.76 + 4806.60 + 11001.94 + 246.00 = 168213.30. Code matches exactly at every cited line: api/server.js:3798-3800 assigns bookings/priced_bookings/fares onto the per-platform cell with no booking_days; :3811 calls fleetIncome([...inner.values()], daysInMonth); api/income_sql.js:163 is `const base = r.booking_days > 0 ? r.booking_days : windowDays;` so base falls back to 30; api/income_sql.js:219 is the `payout_coverage_pct >= 80` gate. Uber's 5 payout days over base 30 = 16.7%, gate fails, and the fare branch takes over because bookings-based fare coverage is 2598/2865 = 90.7% >= 80. /api/revenue passes booking_days 5, gets 5/5 = 100%, and keeps the payout.
intent_check: The opposite of deliberate — the codebase argues against this behaviour in two places. api/income_sql.js:120-129, the comment directly above coverage(), states the rule the trend route breaks: "a channel that started mid-window, or ran three days a week, is not half-covered because the calendar says thirty days. 'Of the days this channel worked, how many does a statement cover' is the question the number is trying to answer." And chooseBasis's own header (api/income_sql.js:196-215) says summing fares as income "states money the fleet never receives", with the measured Uber reconciliation (+0.06% on payouts) as the reason payouts win. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md or docs/AUDIT.md defends passing daysInMonth; grep for daysInMonth and booking_days across both docs returns zero hits. The trend route is simply a call site that was never taught the finer denominator.
user_visible: Yes, on both counts, but narrower than filed. The #causes trend chart plots m.trips, not money (causes.js:96-131) — there is no money line, so the finder's "the month-over-month money line is not comparable to itself" is wrong. The money appears only in the note a reader gets by picking a month, and causes.js:426 renders exactly `row.accounted`: picking September prints "AED 168,213 in" where #revenue and #finance print AED 112,470 for the identical month — gross of Uber's 25% commission. Picking the month beside it prints August's net 499,453, so a reader comparing two adjacent notes compares gross against net. Separately, causes.js:432 appends "— no platform statement covers this month; its money is not recoverable" to that same September note, for a month whose Uber statement is collected (statement_net 89,249.55 on the same row) and whose payouts /api/reconcile matches. That sentence exists for months past Uber's ~192-day earnings horizon (docs/COVERAGE.md:106) and is firing on the live month. Recurs every month: the gate needs payout_days >= 24 of 30, so days 1-24 of every month read gross, then the figure silently steps down ~33% (55,743 of 168,213 at today's mix).
fix: Carry a real working-day base onto the per-platform cell in api/server.js:3793-3800 so api/income_sql.js:163 stops falling back to windowDays. rollup_month already stores first_day and last_day (written by refreshMonthExtras in src/rollup.js), so adding them to platMonthSql at api/server.js:3758-3765 and setting cell.booking_days = last_day - first_day + 1 needs no schema change; count(DISTINCT local_day) added to the month rollup COLS in src/rollup.js:117-119 is the exact version. That one input clears accounted_payouts, which clears income_missing at api/server.js:3836 on its own. Optionally also harden api/server.js:3836 to gate income_missing on `inc.statement_net == null` rather than on accounted_payouts being null, so the sentence can never again claim a month with a collected statement is unrecoverable.

title: /api/trend/monthly serves rollup fares that predate the in-flight Egari backfill, so #causes understates the money of every pre-February month — January reads AED 1,273,940 against AED 1,469,523 on #revenue
area: #causes — the per-month note on the monthly trend (the only surface reading this endpoint; api/public/causes.js:218)
reproduced: The filed headline reproduces exactly: GET /api/trend/monthly?_=$RANDOM 2026-02 revenue "1019359", priced_trips 17253 vs GET /api/kpis?period=2026-02&_=$RANDOM revenue "1427908", priced_trips 24249 — -408,549 = -28.6%, -6,996 priced trips, unmoved. 2026-07 also unmoved (566367/9180 vs 589610/9612). 2026-08 agrees exactly (740768 both). But the January sub-figure HAS MOVED against the filing: the finder recorded /api/revenue?period=2026-01 accounted 1,379,251.76 / priced 23,505; it now returns accounted 1,469,523.10 / priced 25,116 against trend's 1,273,939.82 / 21,683 — the gap widened from -7.6% to -13.3% (-195,583) while I was verifying, which is the backfill still running. Staleness mechanism confirmed in code and corroborated by the docs: GET /api/trend/monthly?platform=uber gives 2026-01 priced 19,777 and 2026-02 priced 15,449, which are character-for-character the Ecosine-only counts in docs/COVERAGE.md:60-61, while live /api/revenue?period=2026-02 now shows uber priced 22,445 — ~7,000 Egari fares have landed since that table was measured today. Code cited is exact: api/server.js:3657-3661 SELECT ... FROM rollup_month; src/rollup.js:131 snapToBucket returns `${since.slice(0,7)}-01`; src/index.js:65 is refreshRollups({days:14}) on */15, src/index.js:72 is the single full refreshRollups() at '40 22 * * *'. Response keys are ['months','breaks','gaps','source'] with source:"rollup" — no as-of stamp, as filed.
intent_check: Half deliberate, and the finder did not read it. src/index.js:67-71 states the exact failure mode as a known one: "The quarter-hourly refresh only touches the last fortnight, which is right for new trips and blind to a backfill — a twelve-month re-collection rewrites months the incremental pass never looks at." The nightly 22:40 UTC full rebuild IS the chosen mitigation, and the lag is bounded under 24h by design. src/rollup.js:122-129 separately documents why the window is snapped to the month start. So "serves a stale rollup" as a standalone defect overstates it — this is deliberate eventual consistency. What is genuinely unaddressed, and what survives, is the second half of the finder's own proposed fix: the response carries no computed_at, so a reader has no way to know the month they are looking at is behind, and nothing triggers a full rebuild when a collector run writes outside the 14-day window.
user_visible: Yes, but not via the field the finding leads with. #causes renders exactly one money field from this endpoint — `row.accounted` at causes.js:426. It never renders `revenue` or `priced_trips`, so the -28.6% February headline is true of the payload and invisible to any human. February's *rendered* money is in fact correct (trend accounted 488,196.40 == /api/revenue accounted 488,196.40) because Uber is on the payout basis there and the stale fares are discarded. The real visible damage is on the fares-basis months, which have no payouts to mask it: picking January on #causes prints "AED 1,273,940 in" where #revenue prints AED 1,469,523 for the same month, -13.3%, with nothing on the page to reconcile them — and the same understatement applies across the ~14 fares-basis months from 2024-12 to 2026-01. The trips bars themselves are fine (trend 2026-02 trips 30,538 == kpis 30,538); the backfill wrote fares onto existing trip rows. Should self-heal at the next 22:40 UTC rebuild; if January is still -13.3% after that, this is high, not medium.
fix: Two small changes, both already named by the finder. (1) Add `min(computed_at)` over the months served to the /api/trend/monthly response beside source:"rollup" (api/server.js:3657-3661 selects from rollup_month, which already has the column) and have causes.js mark a month whose rollup predates the newest trip write. (2) Call the unwindowed refreshRollups() at the end of any collector run that wrote outside the 14-day incremental window, rather than waiting for the single 22:40 UTC cron at src/index.js:72.

title: /api/mix and /api/mix/detail count complimentary rides as priced revenue, violating the has_fare rule the schema created specifically to stop this — 11 given-away hotel rides carry AED 370 that every other surface reports as leakage
area: #finance — the product-tier table (api/public/app.js:2551-2568); also the fleet overview and corporate booking-type panels, which read the same endpoint
reproduced: Every number reproduces to the digit. GET /api/mix/detail?by=payment&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31&_=$RANDOM -> {platform:"hotel", label:"foc-complimentary", n:11, priced_n:11, revenue:370}. GET /api/settlement/mix same window -> settlement_class "complimentary": trips 11, priced_trips 0, revenue null, foc_trips 11. GET /api/mix?by=platform same window -> hotel n 916, priced_n 916, revenue 67840; GET /api/revenue?period=2026-08 -> hotel bookings 916, priced_bookings 905, fares 67469.98 (67840 - 67469.98 = 370.02, the eleven rides exactly). GET /api/corporate/summary -> bookings 916, priced 905, revenue 67470, foc_trips 11. Fleet total from /api/mix?by=product sums to 741,137 and by=platform to 741,138 against 740,768.19 on /api/revenue and 740,769 summed over /api/settlement/mix classes. Code is exactly as cited: api/server.js:993-994 (in /api/mix) and api/server.js:1071-1072 (in /api/mix/detail) both read `round(sum(price)::numeric,0) revenue` and `count(*) FILTER (WHERE price IS NOT NULL)::int priced_n` from trip_norm, which exposes has_fare and is never asked for it.
intent_check: Not deliberate — this is the one rule the schema author wrote a paragraph to prevent, and /api/mix is the call site that got missed. sql/schema_v18.sql:90-102 defines has_fare as `price IS NOT NULL AND lower(coalesce(payment_type,'')) NOT IN ('foc-complimentary','foc','complimentary')` and explains why: "A complimentary ride carries a price that is not a price: nobody paid it. This tested price IS NOT NULL alone, so the fleet's revenue headline included rides given away — while the settlement page, which excludes them explicitly, reported a figure AED 320 smaller over the same window. Two pages, two answers, and the one that was wrong is the one everybody reads. Excluded here rather than at each of the fifty call sites, because a rule applied in fifty places is applied in forty-nine." The finder read this correctly. Same window, same shape, AED 370 instead of AED 320.
user_visible: Yes, but far less than filed — I checked both claimed render sites and neither holds. (a) app.js:2557's totalRev is never printed as money; it is only the denominator of the "Share of revenue" percentage column at app.js:2564, so no page anywhere shows AED 741,137 next to a 740,768.19 tile. (b) The payment donut cannot show the AED 370 disagreement: charts.js:350 defines donut(host, data, {value = 'n'}), so it plots trips, and trips agree (11 on /api/mix/detail, 11 on /api/settlement/mix). The promise at app.js:85 that the two pages "cannot disagree" is about the class folding, and it holds on what is drawn. What a person actually sees wrong: on the #finance product-tier table the hotel tiers carry AED 370 of given-away money inside their Fares column (pick_and_drop 44,834 + drop_off 18,371 + hourly 4,635 = 67,840 vs a true 67,469.98), each tier reads "Priced 572 of 572" style — claiming every hotel ride was paid for — while #corporate on the same window reports foc_trips 11 as leakage and priced 905 of 916, and the Share-of-revenue and Per-priced-trip columns are computed off the inflated base. A 0.05% money error today that scales with FOC volume, and it silently reports given-away work as earned.
fix: Two SQL edits in one file, both against a column trip_norm already exposes to these queries. In api/server.js:993-994 (/api/mix) and api/server.js:1071-1072 (/api/mix/detail) replace `sum(price)` with `sum(price) FILTER (WHERE has_fare)` and `count(*) FILTER (WHERE price IS NOT NULL)` with `count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_fare)`. The adjacent priced_km FILTER (WHERE price IS NOT NULL) on the next line of each should move to has_fare in the same edit for the same reason.

title: /api/economics/assets drops chargeable_bookings on the way from its CTE to the platform row, so fare coverage divides by every booking and the Unit-economics page badges Bolt "partial" at 51% where /api/revenue reports 100%
area: #economics (Unit economics) — the channel-yield table's basis pill (api/public/economics.js:487-493)
reproduced: Exact, on both windows filed. GET /api/economics/assets?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-05&_=$RANDOM -> by_platform bolt: bookings 147, priced_bookings 75, chargeable_bookings 147, uncharged_bookings null, fare_coverage_pct 51, basis "partial_fares", basis_note "fares on only 75 of 147 bookings (51%) — the rest of this channel's money is not collected". GET /api/revenue?period=2026-09 same channel: bookings 147, priced 75, chargeable_bookings 75, uncharged 72, fare_coverage_pct 100, basis "fares". August reproduces too: assets bolt 63.8% partial_fares vs revenue 99.7% fares; assets uber 90.3% vs revenue 99.9%; September uber 90.8% vs 100%. chargeable_bookings == bookings on all four assets rows and uncharged_bookings is null on all four, as filed. Code confirmed and the finder's line numbers are within two: api/economics_routes.js:242-243 computes chargeable_bookings and uncharged_bookings correctly in the per_channel CTE; the plat() default object at :450-451 omits both; the Object.assign at :457-459 copies bookings, priced_bookings, fares, km and booking_days but not them; api/income_sql.js:168 is `const chargeable = r.chargeable_bookings ?? r.bookings;` and takes the fallback.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and the evidence is unusually direct — the comment explaining why this must not happen sits at api/economics_routes.js:238-241, four lines above the CTE that computes the right column: "A ride nobody took has no fare and never will; counting it as missing coverage made Bolt read 63.8% covered on a month it priced 99.7% of its completed rides." That is verbatim the number this endpoint prints for Bolt in August today. docs/COVERAGE.md:24-28 states it as the house denominator: "Every percentage below divides by chargeable bookings ... counting it as missing coverage understated three channels at once." The same file gets it right in another route — economics_routes.js:1011 and :1078-1079 both declare and accumulate chargeable_bookings/uncharged_bookings. This route computes the column and then drops it on the floor.
user_visible: Yes, but the money is fine and one of the two claimed symptoms is not rendered. I checked: basis_note appears nowhere in api/public/economics.js (only api/public/revenue.js:341 and :422-423 render it), so the assertion that Bolt's money "is not collected" is in the payload but is never shown on the Unit-economics page. fare_coverage_pct is not rendered on that page either. And the figure is unharmed — api/income_sql.js:265-267 sets `r.best = r.fares` on the partial_fares branch, the same value the fares branch would set, so Bolt's "Money in" and "Per km" are correct. What a person sees is the label: economics.js:492 appends pill('partial','warn') for any basis starting with "partial", so Bolt wears a warning badge on the Unit-economics channel table while #revenue shows the same channel, same window, as a clean "gross fare" on 100% coverage. A cross-page contradiction about data quality, not about money.
fix: Three sites, not the two the finder proposed — their fix would repair the per-plate rows and leave by_platform, which is what the finding is about, still wrong. Add chargeable_bookings and uncharged_bookings (1) to the plat() default object at api/economics_routes.js:450-451, (2) to the Object.assign at :457-459, and (3) to the chan accumulator at :576-578, which builds by_platform and must sum them (`c.chargeable_bookings += x.chargeable_bookings`) before chooseBasis runs at :589. Both values already come out of the per_channel CTE at :242-243, so nothing new is computed.

title: The report pipeline runs on an expiring supplier cookie while an unused OAuth-REST reports twin exists — but the OAuth client reaches only one of the two orgs, so the proposed migration would take Egari to zero
area: collector internals only — no page renders anything from this
reproduced: Mechanical claims all reproduce. src/config.js:125 does end the scope string with `solutions.suppliers.reports` (verbatim). `grep -rn 'vehicle-suppliers/suppliers' src/ api/` returns exactly one hit, api/probe.js:58, and it is a documentation URL inside a comment — nothing calls the REST reports API. src/sources/uber.js:26 is `const REPORTS = `${UBER_WEB_HOST}/api/vs-sp-reports-management``. uberWebHeaders is at src/auth/uber.js:108, not :107 (one-line drift). Live: GET /api/probe/results?_=$RANDOM (fetched 2026-09-05, last_probe 2026-09-05T03:33:56Z) does carry surface uber:trip-report-session with the note 'The trip export needs a fleethub.uber.com session cookie, which expires and has to be re-pasted', and the OAuth REST surfaces drivers/vehicles/driver-actions/earner-payments all return ok:true with 50/98/50/50 records.
intent_check: The finder misread the very comment they cite as evidence. src/sources/uber.js:35-70 exists to say the 2026-09-01 44-of-44 failure was NOT a cookie expiry: supplier.uber.com had begun answering 301 to fleethub.uber.com, a POST degrades to a GET on a 301 and lands on the login page, and the comment's closing words are that reading it as an expired session 'is exactly what sent this product to re-capture cookies that were never the problem'. src/auth/uber.js:4-18 records the fix (one UBER_WEB_HOST constant, measured 2026-09-02 against a good session: 200 with 98 vehicles). So the finding's headline measurement is a host rename that has already been fixed. Fatal to the remedy: the OAuth client reaches exactly ONE org. src/config.js:85-100, src/credkit.js:181-190 and src/auth_state.js:181-200 independently record that /v1/vehicle-suppliers/orgs on this client returns exactly one organisation, ECOSINE TRANSPORTS, that every Egari REST call answers 403 {"code":"rtapi.internal_server_error","message":"bad key"}, and that this is 'not a credential that expired; a client that was never scoped to the second business'. The cookie surface carries BOTH fleets today. Moving the report pipeline onto OAuth REST would zero Egari's trips, fares and quality until Uber registers a second application — an account change, not a code change. None of this is acknowledged in the finding.
user_visible: nothing. Uber collection is healthy right now — /api/status shows uber/incremental ecosine ok, 1,730 rows, finished 2026-09-05T03:34:44Z, and uber/incremental egari ok, 770 rows. The cookie fragility is real but is already surfaced by credential_state and by the trip-report-session probe row, which is green.
fix: Do not migrate. If the REST twin is worth knowing about, add one read-only entry to the fixed allowlist in api/probe.js (CANDIDATE_REPORTS there is already derived from the same GenerateReport doc page) so ListReports/GetReportByReportID are probed for Ecosine and the answer is on record; keep the cookie path, which is the only one that serves Egari.

title: Five payments weeks in Apr–Aug 2025 are unpriced because the 600s download poll ran out, and docs/COVERAGE.md — written this morning — blames Uber's retention horizon and records the fix as 'nothing'
area: Revenue / fare coverage for Apr–Aug 2025, plus the Known-holes table in docs/COVERAGE.md
reproduced: GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM (fetched 2026-09-05): source=uber mode=backfill fleet_id=ecosine, finished_at 2026-09-05T01:19:23.147Z, chunks_total 155, chunks_failed 38 — exactly 30 'outside retention: … invalid date range' plus 8 'Error: download timed out after 600s for report <uuid>' at the eight windows named, with be4ac21b-b4dd-40ec-9865-d60036bbb1b1 on 2025-08-25..2025-08-31. Code: the throw is at src/sources/uber.js:137 and the reportId is only interpolated into the message, never persisted; the checkpoint gate is at :609 (the finding said :614 — 5-line drift) and reads `if (!isOpen && (!chunk.error || chunk.expected))`; `expected` at :571 tests /invalid date range|retention|out of range/i, which a timeout does not match, so these eight are re-asked every backfill. Two of the finding's sub-claims are FALSE and I corrected them. (a) 'retries and re-fails forever': /api/settings/jobs shows job 50 running now (step 'fares 2025-08-11..2025-08-17', index 55 of 105), and it has already re-asked 2025-08-25..31 and got it — that week was 0 of 2,983 priced when COVERAGE.md was written at 02:56 and is 2,983/2,983 · AED 156,204.23 now. (b) 'recovers Mar–Aug 2025': March recovers nothing — /api/coverage puts the first Uber trip at 2025-04-04 and both March windows have 0 chargeable bookings. Six of the eight carry data; five are still outstanding.
intent_check: This is the rare case where the documented decision is itself the defect, so the usual 'the finder did not read the comment' does not apply. docs/COVERAGE.md is new — created in commit e67ff98 at 2026-09-05 02:56 UTC, one hour and thirty-seven minutes AFTER the backfill whose failed_windows say 'download timed out'. It states 'Before ~September 2025 the coverage is partial and can never be repaired… April–August 2025 sit outside [the ~12-month retention]… This is a ceiling, not a bug', and its Known-holes row reads 'Uber fares, Apr–Aug 2025 | 60–97%, permanently | nothing — past retention'. The same run contradicts it: Uber accepted every window from 2025-03-17 forward and refused only 2025-03-16 and earlier, so the served horizon is ~18 months here, not 12; and weeks interleaved with the failures inside those very months came back full — 2025-04-14..20 is 4,133/4,153 priced, 2025-05-19..25 is 2,365/2,377, 2025-08-04..10 is 1,636/1,645.
user_visible: Yes. /api/revenue?fleet=ecosine per month now: 2025-04 9,361/14,029 (66.7%), 2025-05 7,696/12,245 (62.9%), 2025-06 6,914/7,119 (97.1%), 2025-07 6,097/7,002 (87.1%), 2025-08 8,252/8,896 (92.8%, up from the 60.0% COVERAGE.md printed this morning because one window was recovered while I was checking). The five outstanding windows hold 10,916 chargeable-but-unpriced Uber bookings (847 + 3,801 + 2,822 + 1,912 + 1,534); at April's realised AED 57.31 a ride that is roughly AED 625,000 of fares missing from the record and documented as unrecoverable. The dashboard itself does not mislabel them — collectionDebt in api/public/app.js:4253 treats only /outside retention/i as unservable, so these eight count as owed debt. The false claim lives in the doc, and it is the one that tells a maintainer the fix is 'nothing'.
fix: Two changes, both small. In src/sources/uber.js, carry the reportId out of downloadReport's timeout (it is discarded into the string at :137) onto the chunk and into the checkpoint, so the next pass re-polls the report Uber already generated instead of paying the payments generation cap to make a new one; raising budgetMs alone just makes each failure cost longer. Then correct the two docs/COVERAGE.md passages — the 'ceiling, not a bug' paragraph and the Known-holes row — to name the timeout and the ~2025-03-17 served floor.

title: The weekly bank wire is parsed out of every payments CSV and only its row count is kept, while /api/reconcile prints a dash for the ten months it would fill
area: Reconciliation page (#reconcile) — the Bank payout column
reproduced: Every citation exact. src/sources/uber.js:360 `const settlements = []`; :367 the push with {transaction_id, driver_ext_id, description, amount, bank, kind}; :399 `return { trips, settlements }`; :526 destructures both; :553 `chunk.settlements = settlements.length`; :555 the log line. `grep -rn settlements src/ api/ sql/ bin/` returns those six lines and one unrelated use of the word in a comment at api/public/settlement.js:104 — no reader anywhere. PAY_COLS.bank = 'paid to you:trip balance:payouts:transferred to bank account' at :333, referenced only by the comment at :216-219 and by the push at :367. test/uber_payments_order.test.mjs:92 asserts settlements[0].bank === -66863.51.
intent_check: Not a decision. The header at :246-254 explains only why the so.payout row must not be written as a trip price ('writing it as a trip price would attribute a whole week's wire to one ride') — it calls the row 'the one that reconciles to the bank', and :216-219 records that its only non-zero value in the live probe was -66,863.51, 'exactly the AED 66,863.51 credited to the Ecosine ENBD account on 24 August. The wire is IN the report.' Nothing anywhere argues for dropping it. One correction to the finder's wording: the page does not reconcile against a hand-imported bank ledger — /api/reconcile's bank side is built from driver_payout_day (api/reconcile_routes.js:303), which comes from Uber's GraphQL earner surface on a 192-day rolling horizon; the operator's workbook import (src/sources/ledger.js) is a separate statement feed.
user_visible: Yes, and it makes the page assert something false. GET /api/reconcile?from=2025-04-01&to=2026-09-05&platform=uber&_=$RANDOM returns bank_payout: null for all ten months 2025-04 through 2026-01, and the caption at api/public/reconcile.js:69-72 tells the reader 'a blank here is a month the platform can no longer be asked about, not one whose statement nobody pulled… Earlier months are unknowable rather than zero.' For those same months the collector downloaded the weekly payments CSV, parsed the settlement rows out of it, and kept only the count.
fix: Persist the settlement rows in collectFareWeek (src/sources/uber.js:526-556) instead of counting them. ledger_entry (sql/schema.sql:110) is the fit that needs no migration — platform/external_id/amount/description/category/event_at are all present and transaction_id is a natural external_id. money_event (sql/schema_v42.sql) is the shape the reconcile side reads, but it is DELETEd and rebuilt wholesale by src/rollup.js:422 from other tables, so it needs a durable source first; that is what makes this medium rather than small. Same root as the fare-components finding — both are csvToPayments output that reaches no writer.

title: Eight of the nine children of the fare branch are not keyed into the trip row — true, but every one of them is already collected at driver-week grain and live on /api/earnings/components
area: trip.raw.uber_payments — no page shows the per-trip breakdown; the fleet-level breakdown is already on Revenue / driver pages
reproduced: All citations exact. src/sources/uber.js:263-269 (cited 264-270, one-line drift) lists the nine children — Fare, Surge, Wait time at pick-up, Time at stop, Cancellation, Additional cancellation fee for extended wait time, Reservation Fee, Business trip premium, Adjustment. PAY_COLS at :322-335 has twelve keys and only `fare` (:329) and `fare_base` (:330) touch that subtree; csvToPayments:389 adds exactly those two; the write at :534-543 puts fare, fare_base, earnings, service_fee, cash_collected, tip, adjustment, transactions into the uber_payments blob and no component. The measured leaf-vs-branch table is at :280-286 and api/probe.js:264 does say 'Earnings, Payouts, Cash Collected, Fare Details and Taxes'. So the mechanical claim holds.
intent_check: The comment the finding quotes exists to justify reading the BRANCH instead of the LEAF, and commit 8eae91d already did that. The '0.00 against 15.00' cancellation the finding offers as evidence of live harm is the bug that fix closed — trip.price now carries the branch, so an AED 15 cancellation is priced at 15. title: Driver bcrypt hashes and Expo push tokens from the corporate portal are stored in trip.raw and handed out by two anonymous production endpoints
area: Any trip detail view (/api/trip) and the provider Probe page (/api/probe/results)
reproduced: GET https://fleet-dashboard-wpeqb.ondigitalocean.app/api/trip?platform=hotel&id=6a9a93a8ef5f149a4440692c -> HTTP 200 with no cookie or token; key enumeration returns trip.raw.driver.password, trip.raw.driver.emiratesId, trip.raw.driver.notificationToken (values not read). GET /api/probe/results -> HTTP 200 anonymous, 42,366 bytes, and under provider=hotel surface=trip-report it prints 9 distinct $2b$10$... values verbatim in driver.password.values and 10 values in driver.notificationToken.values. Code matches exactly: src/sources/hotel.js:255 `raw: t,`; the contrary rule is at src/sources/hotel.js:271. Mechanism confirmed at src/probe.js:37 (MAX_VALUES = 12) and src/probe.js:80 `values: f.all.size <= maxValues ? [...f.values] : null` -- the finder cited probe.js:74, the line is now 80, mechanism identical. Blast radius is wider than claimed: /api/schema/raw-fields?platform=hotel shows `driver` fill_pct 100 over rows_with_raw 1714 with 39 distinct driver documents, and 59 of 59 trips in my own random sample carried driver.password.
intent_check: No documented intent supports this and the file argues the opposite. src/sources/hotel.js:271 states the rule in words -- 'password is a bcrypt hash the API returns unasked; never persist it' -- and applies it to driver_compliance.raw eleven lines below the `raw: t` that violates it. Neither docs/COVERAGE.md nor docs/AUDIT.md mentions password, PII or redaction. Read API being anonymous IS deliberate (api/admin_gate.js gates writes only, and its header says reads are handled separately), but that same header shows redaction-on-anonymous-read is an accepted principle here: GET /api/settings is answered REDACTED specifically to keep secret tails out of an anonymous GET. This exposure is the same class of thing, unredacted.
user_visible: Yes, and to anyone at all. /api/probe/results needs no credential and returns 9 drivers' bcrypt password hashes and 10 Expo push tokens in one response. The push token is a capability, not just data -- it lets a holder send arbitrary notifications to a driver's phone. emiratesId is the weakest leg: it is already published by api/driver_routes.js:729 and api/server.js:4074, so the genuinely new exposure is the password hash and the push token.
fix: Three parts, not the two proposed. (1) src/sources/hotel.js:255 -- replace `raw: t,` with a stripped copy that drops driver.password, driver.notificationToken and driver.emiratesId. (2) src/probe.js describe(), at the line 80 `values:` expression -- suppress sample values for keys matching /password|token|secret|otp/i so a narrow-cardinality secret can never be sampled. (3) The backfill the finder omitted: (1) and (2) only fix future writes. All 1,714 stored hotel trip rows already hold the hash, and src/probe.js:519 upserts probe output into provider_probe, so the stored probe rows serve it until purged. A one-off UPDATE stripping the three keys from trip.raw plus a purge/re-probe of provider_probe is required for the live exposure to actually stop.

I CLOSED the caveat the finder left open. /api/corporate/properties shows 'Office' (675d566697467adfe29a32c7) with exactly 219 bookings, all priced. Leakage rows cross-tabbed by property and has_authorization: zero_priced -> Office/True 13, Driver Self-Managed/False 12, Le Meridien/False 5; deadhead_exceeds_fare -> Office/True 2, Driver Self-Managed/False 5, Aloft/False 3. intent_check: Half the finding is contradicted by intent the finder did not quote. api/analytics_routes.js:764 labels the category 'Charged with no authorisation ON FILE' and LEAK_WHY at 776-778 defines it as 'A billed booking with NO AUTHORISATION OBJECT ATTACHED, at a property whose own workflow requires one'. The predicate implements that definition exactly, so this is a specification weakness, not code contradicting its own comment -- and the 685-694 comment shows the property qualifier was added deliberately after the category fired on 87% of bookings. The title's 'can never fire' is also overstated: it can fire, the provider has simply attached an object to every Office booking. The other half survives intact -- nothing reads operatorApproval, the decision half of the model. src/sources/hotel.js:254 does write it, but as `String(t.operatorApproval)`, which on an object yields the literal '[object Object]', and no route reads the column regardless.
user_visible: A reader of the Leakage panel sees 'Charged with no authorisation on file -- 0' and takes away that the approval control is clean. It is not: all 219 bookings at the only property that requires approval were driven on a request that was raised and never decided. Given the panel's own wording the printed 0 is literally true, so nothing on screen is arithmetically false -- which is why this is medium, not high. The blind spot is real; the displayed number is not wrong.
fix: Two changes in one place. (1) sql/schema_v18.sql:182-183 -- keep has_authorization as-is for the existing label, and add a sibling `t.raw #>> '{authorization,authorizationStatus}' AS authorization_status` plus `t.raw #>> '{operatorApproval,status}' AS operator_approval` to trip_ext. (2) api/analytics_routes.js:706 -- add a second kind, 'authorisation raised but never granted' (authorization_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'granted' at an approval-requiring property), and a third for operator_approval = 'rejected'. Relabel nothing else; the existing label stays honest because it keeps meaning what it says.

title: Two worked Ecosine July days carry AED 284.30 and AED 64.36 of Uber payout — about AED 14,565 (6.3%) missing from the month — and nothing on #revenue flags it; but the finding's cause and its headline fix are both wrong
area: #revenue for July 2026 / Ecosine — the Uber channel row's payout figure, its "payout" basis pill and basis_note, the Accounted-for tile, and /api/kpis which shares chooseBasis
reproduced: GET /api/reconcile?month=2026-07&fleet=ecosine&platform=uber&_=$RANDOM (fetched now) reproduces every figure exactly: 07-09 trips 250 bank_payout 8206.60 bank_period_days_min 1; 07-10 trips 231 bank_payout 284.30 min 7; 07-11 trips 210 bank_payout 64.36 min 7; 07-12 trips 181 bank_payout 6997.88 min 1. Mean of the other 29 days computed from the same response: 7456.85, exact. GET /api/revenue?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31&fleet=ecosine → uber payouts 216597.31, payout_days 31, payout_coverage_pct 100, payout_coverage_days 31, basis "payout", basis_note "net payout ... this is the money that arrived". GET /api/reconcile/periods?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31&fleet=ecosine&platform=uber → current_by_grain 1-day 216248.65 / 7-day 348.66, exact. Code exact: api/income_sql.js:103 `count(DISTINCT day)::int payout_days`, api/revenue_routes.js:236-237 `covered AS (SELECT platform, count(DISTINCT day)::int days FROM pay GROUP BY 1)`, api/income_sql.js:176 and :219. My own scan of Mar-Aug 2026 across both fleets for uber day rows under AED 1,500 returns these two Ecosine days and nothing else on Ecosine (the Egari hits are that fleet's normal ~AED 1,000/day scale).
intent_check: Two corrections against the code. First, the CAUSE is not what the finding says. It claims "schema_v58 blanks a coarse row's money but leaves the row standing, so every superseded day still counts toward coverage." GET /api/reconcile/periods?from=2026-07-10&to=2026-07-11&fleet=ecosine&platform=uber returns ONLY a 7-day grain — 235 driver-days, 119 drivers, 348.66, finest_grain 7. There are no 1-day rows on those two days at all: this is a two-day hole in the daily grid, not a supersession artefact. Second, the finding calls payout_coverage_pct "the one figure whose whole job is to catch this" and quotes its docstring — but that docstring (api/revenue_routes.js:227-228) scopes it precisely: "three days of payout on a thirty-day window made a channel read as fully accounted for." It is a DAYS metric by explicit design and never claimed to police magnitude. Consequently the proposed fix does not work: `count(DISTINCT day) FILTER (WHERE earnings IS NOT NULL)` still counts 2026-07-10 and 07-11, because both days carry non-null earnings (284.30 and 64.36). Coverage would remain 31/31 = 100% and the symptom would be untouched.
user_visible: Yes, but narrower than claimed. #revenue for July 2026 / Ecosine states Uber payouts of AED 216,597.31 under a basis pill reading "payout" and a note reading "this is the money that arrived". At the month's own 29-day mean of 7,456.85/day, those two days should carry about 14,913.70 and carry 348.66 — so roughly AED 14,565 never reaches the page, 6.3% of a corrected 231,162. Nothing on #revenue says so. It is one fleet-month, two days, and #reconcile's day table does print bank_payout 475.58 and 255.65 in plain sight beside 8,397.89 neighbours, which is why this is medium rather than high.
fix: Take the finding's SECOND suggestion, not its first. Add a per-day payout floor as its own alert: a day whose channel payout is under ~20% of the window's median with a normal trip count is flagged with a reason, the way api/alert_coverage_sql.js already states absences. Leave api/income_sql.js:103 and api/revenue_routes.js:237 alone — the FILTER changes nothing here and payout_coverage_pct is deliberately a days metric. Separately, this shares its two anomalous days with the deltaPill finding below, but the two are different defects in different files needing different fixes; do not fold them together.

title: deltaPill prints 2.9% as the headline agreement for 2026-07-10 when only AED 276.35 of that day's AED 7,208.97 expectation was compared — a real gap in the tone, but the page already discloses the coverage and two thirds of the proposed fix is wrong
area: #reconcile day table, July 2026 / Ecosine, the "Δ bank − expected" pill on rows 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-11
reproduced: GET /api/reconcile?month=2026-07&fleet=ecosine&_=$RANDOM (fetched now) reproduces to the fils: 2026-07-10 trips 263, ontrip_net 8702.63, expected_payout 7208.97, bank_payout 475.58, expected_covered 276.35, bank_covered 284.30, delta 7.95, delta_pct 2.9, matched_pairs 118, matched_drivers 118, bank_drivers 118; 2026-07-11 bank_payout 255.65, delta 3.24, delta_pct 5.3, 115 of 115; neighbours 07-09 at 13.8% and 07-12 at −2.9% on 161 of 161. Shortfall 1 − 475.58/7208.97 = 93.4%, as claimed. Code exact: api/reconcile_routes.js:186-193, `FROM bank b LEFT JOIN stmt s USING (platform, person, day)`, with expected_covered summed only where a bank row exists.
intent_check: This is largely the commonest failure mode — the finder did not read the design. (1) Restricting BOTH sides to the shared (person, day) pairs is deliberate and documented at length at api/reconcile_routes.js:120-150, with the measurement that forced it: "In August 2026 that compared AED 18,116 of on-trip net — fifty-three drivers — against AED 35,858 of bank money covering a hundred and eighty-nine, and reported a 153% gap. The money was fine. The two sides were answering about different people." (2) The disclosure the finding proposes ALREADY EXISTS. `withCompared` at api/public/reconcile.js:207-211 renders the Expected payout cell of that very row as "AED 7,208.97 · AED 276.35 compared" and the Bank payout cell as "AED 475.58 · AED 284.30 compared", with the docstring "Without the second number a partly-matched row reads as a wild discrepancy instead of a partial answer." (3) The bank_drivers claim is a misreading: `count(DISTINCT b.person)::int AS bank_drivers` carries no FILTER, so it is already the day's whole payout population and not the matched subset. "118 of 118" is literally true — the bank side genuinely held 118 people that day. (4) The tone claim is soft too: day rows carry salik = null, so floorApplies is true and 2.9%, 5.3%, 13.8% and −2.9% all render the same amber pill. The colour separates nothing on that table either way.
user_visible: Partly. What a reader sees on 2026-07-10 is a Δ column reading "+AED 7.95 · 2.9%" — the calmest number in the July table — on the worst payout day in the range. But the same row also prints "AED 7,208.97 · AED 276.35 compared", "AED 475.58 · AED 284.30 compared" and "118 of 118 drivers · 1 day", so the evidence is all on screen; only the summary number is over-confident. The one genuine hole in the disclosure is that "Compared over" carries a BANK denominator only, so a collapsed bank side cannot show up in it. Not the "single worst payout day of the year rendering as one of the calmest rows" with nothing said — the row says a great deal.
fix: One guard in api/public/reconcile.js deltaPill (lines 107-174), which is already exported as a pure function for exactly this kind of test: before computing tone, if expected_covered/expected_payout or bank_covered/bank_payout falls below ~0.5, return a dim pill whose title says how much of each side the comparison actually reached. Do not touch the coveredSql join — its shared-pairs restriction is load-bearing and documented. Do not change bank_drivers; it already reads the day's whole payout population.

title: /api/revenue and three pages sum parent-null component rows as if they were a partition, adding the REST `earnings` tree to the GraphQL `your_earnings` tree — AED 37,508.19 of double-counted money on the default #revenue window
area: #revenue "The payout, broken down" panel and its caption; the #finance components panel; and the per-driver components panel on #driver
reproduced: GET /api/revenue?days=30&_=$RANDOM (window 2026-08-07..2026-09-05, fetched now) → uber components 298686.73. GET /api/earnings/components?days=30 parent-null rows, exact: your_earnings 341358.39/234 drivers, payouts −82427.15/234, earnings 37508.19/82, reimbursements_expenses 2337.30/73, paid_to_third_parties −90.00/64, summing to 298686.73. `tip` appears under BOTH roots (your_earnings 3309.34/85 and earnings 500.00/31) and so does `taxes_earnings` (−5981.52/92 and −579.68/53), exactly as claimed. GET /api/earnings/components?from=2026-08-24&to=2026-08-30&fleet=egari → your_earnings 39103.11/71 AND earnings 977.74/23 with net_fare 990.31/23 — one week, both roots, exact. Code exact: api/revenue_routes.js:314 `if (c.parent == null) r.components = (r.components || 0) + num(c.amount)` and api/public/revenue.js:489 `const net = top.reduce(...)` with the caption at :491-492. TWO CITATIONS ARE WRONG and I corrected them: the #finance sum is api/public/app.js:184, not 2615 (2615 is the compRows/overlapping note); and the "130,396 over 234 drivers against net_fare's 3,747 over 81" quote is src/rollup.js:612, not api/reconcile_routes.js. The finder also MISSED a third copy of the same sum: api/public/driver.js:1199, per driver, with the same "not added again" caption. I also tightened the magnitude: I summed the `earnings` root inside each GraphQL week in the window — Aug 17-23 ecosine 23348.89, Aug 24-30 ecosine 2625.26 + egari 977.74 = 26951.89 — and 37508.19 − 26951.89 = 10556.30, which is exactly the Aug 21-24 REST period straddling the two weeks. So ALL 37,508.19 sits on days a GraphQL week in the same window also describes; none of it is additive.
intent_check: The codebase argues the finding's side, explicitly. src/rollup.js:575-593 sets out the identity — "REST earnings = net_fare + tip + taxes / GraphQL your_earnings = fare + service_fee + tip + taxes, so your_earnings − tip − taxes IS net_fare" — verified on driver 64686123 to the fils, and notes "taxes_earnings and tip hang under BOTH roots". NET_FARE_SQL at rollup.js:627-633 is a `coalesce`: the rollup treats the two roots as ALTERNATIVES. The read path treats them as ADDENDS. The one sentence that might excuse it — "one period holds one row per category whichever surface wrote it, and there is nothing to double count" — is scoped to a single (driver, period) key inside the subtraction and says nothing about summing roots across two surfaces' differently-shaped periods, which is what happens here. This is a genuine contradiction between two halves of the same product, not a decision the finder failed to read.
user_visible: Yes. #revenue's "The payout, broken down" caption prints "5 top-level components netting to AED 298,686.73. Everything in the table below is INSIDE one of these and is not added again." The second sentence is false: `tip` and `taxes_earnings` each hang under both counted roots. The figure is 12.6% of what it prints (14.4% over the correct AED 261,178.54) too large, and the hbar chart draws an AED 37,508 "earnings" bar beside a "your_earnings" bar that already contains the same money for the same 82 drivers. The same overstatement renders on #finance (api/public/app.js:184) and per-driver on #driver (api/public/driver.js:1199). Since the panel sits beside the fares and payout columns, it reads as the reconciliation between them.
fix: Resolve at read time the way src/rollup.js already does, in one place: in the /api/revenue and /api/earnings/components component query, drop the `earnings` root (and its subtree) on any (driver, day) a `your_earnings` period also covers, and mark it "the same week on the other surface". If that is too invasive, return the source surface on each component row so the three pages can group by tree and print two totals rather than one. Whatever is chosen must land in all three renderers — api/public/revenue.js:489, api/public/app.js:184, api/public/driver.js:1199 — or the pages will disagree with each other.

title: /api/supply/balance divides one fleet's job hours by BOTH fleets' online hours — and prints Uber's online hours under the Bolt and Hotel chips
area: Supply vs demand page (#supply) headline verdict and heatmap; carried into the Rota page (#optimise) upside
reproduced: Fetched now. https://fleet-dashboard-wpeqb.ondigitalocean.app/api/supply/balance?from=2026-08-06&to=2026-09-05&_=$RANDOM → totals {online_h 25907, on_job_h 6102, idle_h 19805, idle_pct 76}. Same URL &fleet=ecosine → online_h 25907 (byte-identical), on_job_h 4634, idle_pct 82. &fleet=egari → online_h 25907, on_job_h 1468, idle_pct 94. &platform=bolt → online_h 25907, on_job_h 138, idle_pct 99. &platform=hotel → online_h 25907, idle_pct 95. &platform=uber → online_h 25907, on_job_h 4595. Every cell matches too: dow0 h0 online_h is 30.45 under all six. The on-job side splits correctly (4634+1468=6102). Code confirmed: api/supply_routes.js:99-106 (span) and :119-141 (supply CTE) both read FROM driver_timeline_event with only `kind='status' AND status<>'' AND at BETWEEN $1 AND $2`, bound with [p[0], p[1]]; onJob (:146-160) and demand (:162-164) both bind ${FB} = W() (api/server.js:205-210,261), which carries platform=$3 and fleet_id=$4. driver_timeline_event.fleet_id is NOT NULL (sql/schema_v37.sql:27) and BOTH fleets are populated — /api/coverage?fleet=ecosine geo timeline:uber n=113645, ?fleet=egari n=69857. Front end: api/public/supply.js:106 fetches via q() (which sends the chips), and 'supply' is in neither NO_FILTER nor NO_PLATFORM_FLEET (api/public/data.js:363-373).
intent_check: Not deliberate. The 60-line comment above the span query (api/supply_routes.js:80-98) defends a completely different decision — clamping both halves to the days the availability feed covers, so widening the range cannot lower the idle rate. The per-occurrence comment at :166-180 defends a third. Neither says anything about fleet or platform. `grep -i fleet api/supply_routes.js` returns 13 hits and every one is prose about 'the fleet' as a business, never a bind. docs/COVERAGE.md and docs/AUDIT.md contain no occurrence of 'supply', 'driver_timeline_event', 'availability' or 'idle' at all. And the codebase treats exactly this defect as a bug elsewhere — the comment at api/server.js:4227-4236 fixes /api/earnings/components for the same reason ('the platform and fleet chips the Finance page displays did nothing to either').
user_visible: Yes, under every chip. With the Egari chip the headline reads '94% of the hours drivers are online, nobody is in the car · 0.17 jobs per online hour · 25,907 online h · 1,468 on job' and '24,439 driver-hours were available and not dispatched' — the two hour figures are the two-fleet total set against Egari-only jobs. Re-derived independently: the timeline event split is 113,645 ecosine / 69,857 egari (62/38), so Egari's own online hours are roughly 9,800 and its true idle is about 85%, not 94 — and idle_h is overstated roughly 3x (24,439 printed against ~8,400). Ecosine reads 82% against a true ~71%. The platform chips are worse than wrong, they are fabricated: driver_timeline_event holds only platform 'uber' (hard-coded SRC at src/sources/uber_timeline.js:29,143), so #supply?platform=bolt prints Uber's 25,907 online hours as Bolt's and calls that channel 99% idle, with no availability feed for Bolt existing at all. api/public/optimise.js:53 pulls the same object and :70,:89 build the jobs-recoverable upside off T.online_h/T.idle_h, so the Rota recommendation inherits the wrong denominator.
fix: api/supply_routes.js: pass the full `p` (range(req) already returns [from, to, platform, fleet]) instead of [p[0], p[1]] to both the span query at :99-106 and the supply CTE at :119-141, and add `AND ($3::text IS NULL OR platform=$3) AND ($4::text IS NULL OR fleet_id=$4)` to both WHERE clauses. Nothing downstream needs touching: `covered: supply.length > 0` at :235 already drives the absent-with-a-reason note at api/public/supply.js:110-114, so bolt/hotel then render 'Driver availability has not been collected for this window' instead of a fabricated 99%.

title: /api/recommendations collapses the two Uber orgs into one 3-row list — the rows are a mixture of Ecosine's and Egari's, unlabelled, and each org's other measure is unreachable
area: Action list page (#insights), panel 'What Uber is asking the fleet to fix' — NOT the Compliance page as the finding states
reproduced: Fetched now. /api/recommendations?_=$RANDOM → shown 3, history 452, no fleet field on any row. ?fleet=ecosine and ?fleet=egari return byte-identical payloads; the route signature at api/server.js:4215 is `wrap(async (_, res)` and never reads req.query.fleet. The query at :4216-4221 is `SELECT DISTINCT ON (platform, rec_type) platform, rec_type, … ORDER BY platform, rec_type, period_end DESC NULLS LAST` — fleet_id is in neither the DISTINCT ON key nor the SELECT list. The org mixture is measured, not inferred: resolving every id in each row's `flagged` array through /api/driver/profile now gives ACCEPTANCE_RATE (org 0.99827 vs target 0.97698, 4 flagged) = 04c30a0a Irfan Ullah Awal Ameen, d144a02a Ijaz Ahmed Khan, b8bbe67f Faiz Muhammad Muhammad, 4056c8cc Waseem Abbas Nabi — all four fleet ecosine; CANCELLATION_RATE (org 0.00196 vs 0.02163, 1 flagged) = e1fb2ce2 Asif Mehmood Abdul Qadeer — egari; TRIP_COMPLETION (2 flagged) = 12ce7e65 Siyad Kallyanathoppil Paramba and e1fb2ce2 — both egari. platform_recommendation carries fleet_id (sql/schema_v5.sql:51) and src/sources/uber_fleet.js:135 stamps it per org.
intent_check: Not deliberate. The route's own comment (api/server.js:4203-4214) reasons at length about why DISTINCT ON replaced a flat LIMIT 30 — 'with four platforms and three types republished monthly, thirty rows is under a year' — and names platform and type in every sentence. Fleet is never mentioned, on a codebase that documents two-fleet handling everywhere else. An oversight in a fix, not a decision. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING, though. (a) It puts the panel on the Compliance page. It is not: the panel is built at api/public/app.js:3866-3916 inside V.insights (api/public/app.js:3687-3916); V.compliance does not start until :3921. The page is labelled 'Action list' (app.js:306). (b) Its proposed fix says to take 'compliance' off NO_FILTER and to read req.query.fleet — both are dead ends. The panel fetches with `api('/api/recommendations')` at app.js:3873, not q(), so it would never send a fleet chip even if the chips were shown, and both 'insights' and 'compliance' sit in NO_FILTER (api/public/data.js:369-373) by design.
user_visible: Yes, but nothing on screen is arithmetically false — this is a labelling and coverage hole rather than a wrong number. The table prints three rows with a Platform column and no Fleet column, so one company's org acceptance rate (99.83% against Uber's 97.70%) sits in the same table as another company's cancellation rate with nothing to tell them apart, and the caption underneath asserts 'All 3 current targets are being met' over what should be up to six measures across two legal entities. The measure each org is NOT the DISTINCT ON winner for is unreachable from any page. Downgraded from the finder's 'high': the org values shown are real rows, both visible targets are being comfortably met, and the reader is not shown a false figure — they are shown an incomplete population described as complete.
fix: api/server.js:4216-4221 — `SELECT DISTINCT ON (platform, fleet_id, rec_type) platform, fleet_id, rec_type, …  ORDER BY platform, fleet_id, rec_type, period_end DESC NULLS LAST`. Then add a Fleet column to the tableFrom column list at api/public/app.js:3878. No chip work is needed or wanted: the page stays in NO_FILTER and simply shows both fleets' rows labelled.

title: Two of Uber's three recommendation types have never once become findings — platformFlags reads only the newest 20 rows by period_end, a window that spans about two days, and the daily type fills it
area: Action list page (#insights) — the codes below_target_acceptance and above_target_cancellation never appear in the ranked findings list
reproduced: Fetched now. /api/insights?code=below_target_acceptance&_=$RANDOM → {"insights":[],"cleared":0}; /api/insights?code=above_target_cancellation → identical. Meanwhile /api/recommendations is serving a live ACCEPTANCE_RATE row with 4 flagged drivers and a live CANCELLATION_RATE row with 1. The full live insight set (/api/insights, 104 rows) contains 12 codes and neither of these. Code confirmed verbatim at src/insights.js:916-918: `SELECT rec_type, period_start, period_end, org_value, target_value, flagged_count, flagged, fleet_id FROM platform_recommendation ORDER BY period_end DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20` over a 452-row table; the two codes are owned by the platform_flags job at src/insights.js:1052-1054.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and nothing defends it. The rule's header comment (src/insights.js:911-913) calls these recommendations 'a second opinion on data we cannot see ourselves' — i.e. the whole point is to surface them. docs/AUDIT.md and docs/COVERAGE.md say nothing about platform_recommendation, platformFlags or a row cap. The LIMIT 20 is an unexamined leftover, the same shape the codebase already fixed once in /api/recommendations (api/server.js:4203-4214).
user_visible: Yes, as an absence. TWO THINGS THE FINDER GOT RIGHT BUT UNDERSTATED, both of which I derived myself. (1) `cleared:0` is stronger evidence than 'the findings silently clear'. The reader's run CTE (api/server.js:3468-3479) only produces a row for a code that HAS insight rows, and nothing deletes non-current findings — the prune at src/insights.js:1112-1119 keeps one row per (code, entity_type, entity_id). So insights:[] with cleared:0 means these two codes have NEVER been emitted, not that they were emitted and expired. (2) The crowding mechanism is directly measurable from production. The live drivers_online_no_trips finding carries window 2026-09-04, while the current TRIP_COMPLETION rec row is period_end 2026-09-05. platformFlags writes every completion row it sees under the same key (entity_type 'fleet', entity_id 'all', src/insights.js:936-937), so after the prune the surviving row is the LAST one processed — the oldest completion row inside the LIMIT 20. That bottom is 09-04, so the 20-row window covers roughly two days, and the weekly acceptance/cancellation rows sitting five days back at period_end 2026-08-31 are nowhere near it. That also exposes a sibling defect on the same line: because entity_id is 'all' with no fleet in the key, the two fleets' completion findings overwrite each other — the live finding names 1 Egari driver while the current rec row names 2. Downgraded from the finder's 'high': the Action list makes no false statement (there is no 'rules that ran and found nothing' surface on the page), and the org itself comfortably meets both targets (99.83% acceptance against a 97.70% target; 0.196% cancellation against 2.16%), so what never lands is a per-driver coaching signal, not an org allocation risk.
fix: src/insights.js:916-918 — replace the flat cap with `SELECT DISTINCT ON (platform, fleet_id, rec_type) platform, fleet_id, rec_type, … ORDER BY platform, fleet_id, rec_type, period_end DESC NULLS LAST`, so every measure for every fleet is evaluated on every pass regardless of republication cadence. While there, put fleet_id into the finding key at :936-937 (entity_id `r.fleet_id` rather than the literal 'all') so the two fleets' completion findings stop overwriting each other in the prune.

title: uber_profile only profiles drivers already in driver_platform_state — at least 23 Egari and ~38 Ecosine Uber drivers who earned in the window have no rating, ban flag or compliance record, and the pass reports a green 'ok'
area: Data-sources page (#sources) status row for uber_profile; driver detail pages; Compliance page driver denominators
reproduced: Code confirmed: src/sources/uber_profile.js:177-184, driverIdsFor is `SELECT driver_ext_id FROM driver_platform_state WHERE platform='uber' AND fleet_id=$1 AND coalesce(btrim(driver_ext_id),'')<>'' ORDER BY observed_at DESC NULLS LAST` and nothing else. The sibling at src/sources/uber_timeline.js:184-208 solves exactly this with a same-fleet UNION against `trip`, under a comment that names the cause: 'driver_platform_state is written by the OAuth REST roster pull, and that surface 403s for Egari … the first roster sweep reported ecosine 113 drivers, 79,674 rows / egari 0 drivers, 0 rows'. That writer is src/sources/uber.js:1697. Production now: /api/status uber_profile ecosine rows_written 113, egari 44, both status 'ok' with error null, finished 2026-09-04. /api/compliance/drivers emirates_id_by_platform gives uber of_n 157 = 113 + 44 exactly. Against that: /api/roster?fleet=ecosine lists 151 uber people (of 312) and ?fleet=egari 60 (of 125). I re-derived the Egari gap rather than trusting the finder's 27 — /api/drivers/performance?from=2026-08-06&to=2026-09-05&fleet=egari returns totals people 71, platforms ['uber'], and the 300 rows it shows (of 1002, truncated) carry 67 DISTINCT driver_ext_id values against 44 profiled, so at least 23 Egari Uber drivers who earned money in the window were never asked about.
intent_check: There IS a deliberate, documented decision here and it is worth stating plainly — but it does not cover this. src/sources/uber_profile.js:29-33 says 'THE ORG MUST OWN THE DRIVER. Asking Ecosine's org about an Egari driver returns an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with an empty message — measured, and the reason the first live probe failed. So each org is asked only about the drivers its own roster names', and driverIdsFor's own comment at :175-176 repeats it. That decision is about not crossing orgs. It is silent on whether driver_platform_state is a complete statement of an org's own roster — and the sibling module documents in full that it is not, for Egari specifically. The proposed UNION is filtered to the same fleet, so it preserves the documented rule exactly. Nor is this a declared hole: docs/COVERAGE.md's 'Known holes, with owners' table (:243-248) lists the Bolt Ecosine roster entitlement and the Yango Ecosine 403 but not this one.
user_visible: Yes, and I measured it rather than inferring it. Sampling the tail of the Egari earner list through /api/driver/profile just now, 8 of the last 14 distinct driver_ext_ids return rating null — 89886d77, 3cf1fcd4, 41fab64a, e6c4ae1e, c4febff7, 716b5404, f77be3df, bb2aa3be, 55833ba1 — while every top earner sampled carries one (4.94-4.99). These are drivers with live trips and earnings in the window whose page shows no rating, no lifetime trip count, no is_banned flag, no compliance status and no driver_rating_history row, and by the module's own rule (uber_profile.js:35-37) NULL there means 'we did not ask' — which is exactly what happened. The Data-sources page shows both passes as a green 'ok' with rows_written equal to the number asked, so nothing on it distinguishes 'we profiled the whole roster' from 'we profiled the subset one 403-ing REST endpoint happens to list'. A ban on an unprofiled driver is invisible. Keeping the finder's 'high': it is a silent coverage hole with a green light over it, on the one field (is_banned) where a miss has operational consequences.
fix: src/sources/uber_profile.js:177-184 — give driverIdsFor the same same-fleet UNION src/sources/uber_timeline.js:189-205 already uses (`SELECT driver_ext_id FROM driver_platform_state WHERE platform='uber' AND fleet_id=$1 UNION SELECT driver_ext_id FROM trip WHERE platform='uber' AND fleet_id=$1`). title: Bolt's collection health is recorded with fleet_id null and joined on source alone, so every Egari page reports Bolt 'partial' quoting Ecosine's company-142868 entitlement refusal
area: Data sources page (#sources) and the 'Built from…' provenance line under every fleet-filtered page, including #revenue?fleet=egari
reproduced: GET /api/platforms?_=$RANDOM -> {"platform":"bolt","fleet_id":"ecosine","bookings":34771,"collection_status":"partial","collection_error":"FI roster ecosine: BOLT_CLIENT_ID is not entitled to company_id 142868 — code=503 NOT_AUTHORIZED hint=COMPANIES_NOT_ALLOWED"} and {"platform":"bolt","fleet_id":"egari","bookings":13530,...} with a byte-identical collection_error. GET /api/revenue?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31&fleet=egari&_=$RANDOM -> bolt row carries the same ecosine error. GET /api/auth?_=$RANDOM contradicts it on every credential: bolt/egari BOLT_CLIENT_ID state "ok" last_ok_at 2026-09-05T03:34:49.756Z, bolt/egari BOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EGARI "ok" 2026-09-05T03:34:59.231Z, bolt/egari BOLT_REFRESH_TOKEN "ok"; bolt/ecosine BOLT_CLIENT_ID "invalid", last_ok_at null. Code checks out: src/sources/bolt.js:937 `await logRun({ source: SRC, fleet_id: null, ...})`; api/channels_sql.js:31 `SELECT DISTINCT ON (source) source, status, error, ...`; api/server.js:2681-2683 spreads `byHealth.get(r.platform)` onto every (platform, fleet_id) row; api/public/ui.js:756-757 pushes `${sourceLabel(r.fleet_id)}: ${r.collection_status}`; api/public/ui.js:735-737 narrows by the selected fleet.
intent_check: Not deliberate — this exact bug shape is declared a bug ten lines below the route that serves it. api/server.js:2691-2699 documents that run rows were made per-fleet because 'Keyed on (source, mode) alone, one fleet's row won and the other vanished — so a fleet whose session had expired, or whose surface had never run at all, read as whatever the other fleet did. That is the exact shape of the bug this page exists to expose, and it was hiding it.' channelHealthSql() still has precisely that shape, and Bolt's own logRun passes fleet_id null so even per-fleet keying could not save it. Two load-bearing comments are now stale: api/public/ui.js:754 ('Bolt carries no fleet_id') and api/public/ui.js:735-737 ('A provider with no fleet of its own — Bolt — belongs to whichever fleet is being viewed'). Both are false of today's /api/platforms rows, which carry fleet_id, so the `|| !r.fleet_id` escape hatch is dead for Bolt and the fleet filter selects the egari row carrying ecosine's error. docs/COVERAGE.md:245 records the Ecosine hole as real and owned; nothing anywhere sanctions attributing it to Egari.
user_visible: Yes. Egari's Bolt integration is healthy on all three credentials, and every Egari-scoped page prints 'Bolt (Egari: partial)' with Ecosine's error text naming company_id 142868, which is not Egari's company. The remedy it implies — chase the Bolt portal for entitlement — is already correct for Ecosine and pointless for Egari. It inverts symmetrically: the single error column means an Egari-only failure would be reported against Ecosine identically.
fix: Make the health join fleet-aware, which needs both halves. (1) src/sources/bolt.js:937 must stop writing a fleet-less verdict — call logRun once per fleet with fleet_id: c.fleet, or add a fleet dimension to the chunk log. (2) api/channels_sql.js:31 -> DISTINCT ON (source, fleet_id), with api/server.js:2681 and api/revenue_routes.js:325-327 keying byHealth on (platform, fleet_id). Cheap interim that stops the false claim today: at api/server.js:2681, attach a fleet-less collection_error only to rows whose fleet_id is null, i.e. render it once for the provider rather than once per fleet.

title: 161 Bolt Ecosine drivers with no state row are rendered blocked_everywhere:false and holding_vehicle_while_blocked:false, so the playbook's 'reassign 30 vehicles' count is silently Egari-only and the gap appears in no gap report
area: Roster page (#roster/blocked), Roster states page, and the Playbook's recover_blocked_vehicles action
reproduced: GET /api/roster?platform=bolt&_=$RANDOM -> 233 people. By credential_fleets x whether any state row exists: 161 ecosine with states:[], 70 egari with states, 2 egari with states:[]. Every one of the 163 stateless people carries plates. A stateless row reads {stopped_everywhere:null, can_earn_anywhere:null, cannot_earn_anywhere:null, score:null, observed_at:null, reason:null, category:'working', blocked_everywhere:false, holding_vehicle_while_blocked:false}. totals {blocked:31, holding_vehicle_while_blocked:30, unclassified:0, activity_unknown:0} — 100% Egari. intent_check: No defence for the boolean collapse: the neighbouring three-valued fields are preserved as null on the very same production rows (can_earn_anywhere null, cannot_earn_anywhere null), and the SQL comment at api/roster_routes.js:275-283 is explicitly about building three-valued answers and about not conflating 'cannot earn' with 'stopped'. 'working'` outranking roster claims — two people with 50 and 23 completed trips had been filed as 'not yet able to earn', and 'Drove in this window' read 89 on a page where 91 people had trips. For a stateless person with 4,769 lifetime trips who drove on 2026-09-04, 'working' is the honest label. That part of the proposed fix should be dropped; the tri-state booleans and the gap disclosure are the defect. docs/COVERAGE.md:245 records the Ecosine roster hole as known and owned, but nothing licenses rendering it as a negative assertion.
user_visible: Yes, and the impact is larger than the finder estimated, not smaller — I re-derived it rather than taking the 2-3x. Stratify by dormancy on the fleet that HAS state: all 31 blocked Egari Bolt drivers last drove 90+ days ago, and among the 38 Egari people who are 90+ dormant, 31 are blocked — an 81.6% conditional rate. On the unread side, 89 of the 161 stateless Ecosine people are 90+ dormant and every one of them holds a plate (a further 11 are 31-90 days dormant; 57 drove within 7 days, for whom blocked:false is empirically well supported). At Egari's conditional rate the 89 dormant plate-holders imply roughly 73 more blocked drivers sitting on cars, against the 30 the playbook prints — about 3.4x. Ecosine is also the larger Bolt fleet (34,771 bookings vs Egari's 13,530). So the headline count of the cheapest recoverable capacity in the business is computed over one of two fleets, states 'false' where it means 'never asked', and the omission is disclosed on no page: /api/roster/states names only yango:12.
fix: Three small changes, none of them to the category ladder. (2) api/roster_routes.js:402 -> holding_vehicle_while_blocked: blocked == null ? null : !!(blocked && (r.plates||[]).length), and add a standing_unknown count beside blocked in the totals at :409. (3) Source /api/roster/states' gap list from credential_state (bolt/ecosine BOLT_CLIENT_ID = invalid) as well as from byState at api/roster_routes.js:481, since a person with no row can never appear in byState — emit a per-(platform, fleet) 'roster not collected' row. title: Bolt's FI getFleetOrders has never been called correctly — the probe sends company_id and the gateway answers 'Is not array, property company_ids', and because it answers HTTP 200 the surface is not even listed as failing
area: Probe / API surfaces page — a diagnostic and resilience defect, not a figure on any dashboard
reproduced: GET /api/probe/results?_=$RANDOM, last_probe 2026-09-05T03:33:56.352Z, live credentials. bolt ecosine:getFleetOrders -> {ok:true, http_status:200, record_count:1, fields:[{key:'error', values:['Is not array']},{key:'property', values:['company_ids']}]}. bolt egari:getFleetOrders -> identical. intent_check: Not deliberate. src/probe.js:425-432 says these surfaces were added precisely because 'the two surfaces that would carry the trips and the money this channel has never delivered were not probed at all, so the page could not say whether they exist' — the intent was discovery, and reusing getDrivers' singular field in the shared body defeats it. src/sources/bolt.js:762-769 documents the identical lesson verbatim on the portal path: '{"code":702,..."Is required","property":"limit"} ... user_visible: Nothing. Correcting the severity down from high: no page shows a wrong number because of this, and no operator reads a false figure. The cost is real but indirect. First, the product cannot say whether Ecosine's entitlement refusal extends to ORDERS or only to the roster, because the request never reaches an authorization check — so docs/COVERAGE.md:245 records a hole whose true width has not been measured. Second, every Bolt trip and fare depends on a Fleet Owner Portal refresh token with a measured ~7-day life (src/sources/bolt.js:7) that must be hand-captured from a portal session; it has already lapsed once in production (src/sources/bolt.js:295 handles 'refresh token expired', and /api/auth shows a 2026-08-27 expiry was hit for Egari), while an untested client-credentials orders surface with no expiry sits one field name away. Third, 'Bolt publishes no payout to us' — stated in docs/COVERAGE.md:167 and in every basis_note for the channel — rests on one guessed route spelling that 404s.
fix: At src/probe.js:449 pass `{ company_ids: [company.companyId], offset: 0, limit: 50 }` for getFleetOrders only, and stop that one surface inheriting the singular company_id from the shared body at :440 (getDrivers still wants the singular and works). Re-run the probe and record what each fleet gets — specifically whether Ecosine also gets COMPANIES_NOT_ALLOWED there. Separately and independently useful: make the probe treat an HTTP 200 body carrying validation_errors or an `error`/`property` pair as failing, so a surface refusing every request cannot sit in the ok list. Adopting getFleetOrders as a second trip source in src/sources/bolt.js is a larger, separate piece of work and should only follow the measurement.

title: /api/corporate/summary divides all-booking revenue by only-measured distance: revenue_per_km publishes AED 6.71 where the matched rate is 3.97, and AED 32.36 on July where it is 4.61, with no coverage disclosure
area: Corporate -> Overview KPI "Revenue per km" (desktop), the "Per km" stat on the phone, and the AED/km column on Corporate -> Properties
reproduced: Numbers unchanged. GET /api/corporate/summary?_=$RANDOM -> {priced:1698, revenue:136657, km:20368, revenue_per_km:6.71}. GET /api/corporate/summary?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31&_=$RANDOM -> {priced:651, revenue:58185, km:1798, revenue_per_km:32.36}. I re-derived from GET /api/export/trips.csv?from=2025-09-01&to=2026-09-05&platform=hotel&grain=trip — 1,714 rows (the finder's row count is right; a naive `wc -l` says 1,740 because address fields contain embedded newlines). Matched pairs, taking numerator and denominator from the same rows: all-time 1,121 rows, AED 80,706 / 20,308 km = 3.97; July 98 rows, AED 8,274 / 1,794 km = 4.61; August 884 rows = 3.83. 577 of the 1,698 priced non-complimentary bookings (34%) carry no usable distance. Every figure the finder quoted reproduces to the digit. Code exact: api/analytics_routes.js:430 `sum(price) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_complimentary) revenue`, :432 `sum(distance_km) FILTER (WHERE has_distance) km`, :467 the division; rendered api/public/corporate.js:110-111 and api/public/m/screens.js:1069. intent_check: Half-anticipated, and the anticipation is the interesting part. There IS a comment on the exact line — api/public/corporate.js:107-109 — recording that an earlier audit stood here: the sub-line used to read "over priced bookings only" and was corrected to "priced or not" because it "described a denominator the figure does not use". So the mismatch was seen and answered with a caption rather than with arithmetic. But the caption discloses only the trivial half (km from unpriced bookings: 20,368 vs 20,308, a 60 km difference) and is silent on the half that matters (577 priced bookings worth AED 55,951 contributing no kilometres). The finder's phrasing "the sub-line asserts a denominator it does not have" is WRONG and I am correcting it — the sub-line states exactly the denominator used. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md or docs/AUDIT.md defends the ratio, and COVERAGE.md's own house rule ("a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON, never as zero") cuts against publishing 32.36 on a window with 15% distance coverage.
user_visible: Yes. The default view a user gets with no window chosen shows AED 6.71 (+69% over the matched 3.97); any window reaching into July shows AED 32.36 (+602% over 4.61). The phone's "Per km" stat carries no sub-line at all, so it publishes the same number with no qualification whatsoever. Per-property column is affected the same way — but the finder's "'Office' reads 6.48 against a matched 4.13" mis-sources that 4.13: it is Office's PUBLISHED August revenue_per_km, not a matched recomputation. Per-property matched rates cannot be recomputed from public endpoints (the CSV export has no partner column); August is a fair proxy because coverage there is 98%, and it lands near 4.1, so the direction and rough size hold.
fix: In api/analytics_routes.js:427-467, take both halves from the same rows: add `sum(price) FILTER (WHERE has_distance AND price IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_complimentary)` and `count(*) FILTER (WHERE has_distance AND price IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_complimentary)` beside the existing km filter, divide those two, and return the row count so api/public/corporate.js:111 can print the real denominator. Where that row count over `priced` falls below a floor (July is 15%), return revenue_per_km null with a reason string so corporate.js:110 and m/screens.js:1069 render the absence instead of a number.

title: has_authorization is object-existence, not approval: all 219 authorisation objects in the entire record are `pending` with a null approver, so the leakage category "Charged with no authorisation on file" is pinned at 0 and 219 never-approved bookings render as compliance
area: Corporate -> Leakage (the category strip and the row table's Authorised column) and Corporate -> Overview KPI "Carried an authorisation"
reproduced: Code exact at sql/schema_v18.sql:182-183 — `(t.raw -> 'authorization' IS NOT NULL AND t.raw -> 'authorization' <> 'null'::jsonb) AS has_authorization` (the finder cited 181-183; 181 belongs to the preceding column). That is the only definition of has_authorization in sql/, so it is live. Consumed at api/analytics_routes.js:438 and :706, rendered at api/public/corporate.js:132-135 and :485-488. I did not sample — I enumerated. Walking GET /api/schema/raw-values?table=trip&platform=hotel&key=authorization in 7-day windows across 2026-07-01..2026-09-05 (every window under the endpoint's 60-group cap; largest returned 50 groups) yields exactly 219 non-null authorisation objects and 1,495 JSON-null ones — 219+1,495 = 1,714 = every hotel booking. All 219 carry authorizationStatus "pending" and authorizationBy null. Zero approved, anywhere, ever. GET /api/corporate/leakage?_=$RANDOM -> unauthorized n=0, disabled null, properties_requiring_approval 1. summary.authorized_trips equals the approval-requiring property's ("Office") booking count in every window probed: all-time 219=219, Jul 71=71, Aug 127=127, Sep 1-5 21=21 (and 71+127+21=219). NEW, and the finder missed it: the provider does publish a granted approval, under a different key. GET /api/schema/raw-fields?table=trip&platform=hotel lists `operatorApproval`, and GET /api/schema/raw-values for it returns two objects with `"status": "approved"`, approvedBy 69cb9d14b11d90e2dcc28690, dated 2026-09-04. src/sources/hotel.js:254 already reads it into a `trip.authorized` text column that no page consumes. So the finder's proposed predicate would return 0 across the whole record — right as a count, but it would miss the only two real approvals in the data.
intent_check: The property qualifier IS a deliberate, well-reasoned decision and the finding does not attack it: api/analytics_routes.js:686-693 records that without it the category fired on 1,095 of 1,254 bookings (87%), and the `disabled` branch at :735-744 handles "no property declares the flag" properly. Nothing anywhere defends reading OBJECT EXISTENCE as authorisation — there is no comment on schema_v18.sql:182-183 and no entry in docs/AUDIT.md or docs/COVERAGE.md. The only place the intent is written down is the leakage copy ("A billed booking with no authorisation object attached"), which describes the implementation rather than the control. Against it: docs/AUDIT.md pass 5 (lines 244-280) records this project already shipping and then fixing the identical failure on a different page — "Zero, on the page whose entire subject is unauthorized trips. That zero reads as 'no leakage'." The house standard is explicitly against this.
user_visible: Yes, on two surfaces and in opposite directions. (a) The leakage strip shows "Charged with no authorisation on file: 0" styled as a category that found nothing, not as one that is disabled, on the page whose subject is billing control. Under a status-based rule the count is the 219 billed Office bookings — AED 38,396, average fare 175.32, 127 of them in August — none of which any person ever approved. (b) The Overview KPI reads "Carried an authorisation 12.8%", sub "of bookings at properties that require one", and BOTH halves are wrong: 0% of the 219 were granted, and the denominator at api/analytics_routes.js:475 is `share(authorized_trips, bookings)` over all 1,714 channel bookings, so under the current definition the caption's own claim would read 100% (219/219), not 12.8%. The amber tone (`< 50 ? 'warn'`) makes it read as "a rate that is low" rather than "a control nobody is exercising". (c) The leakage row table paints a green `tag ok` "yes" for each pending stub at corporate.js:486-488.
fix: Redefine has_authorization as GRANTED, reading both keys the provider actually uses: `lower(t.raw->'authorization'->>'authorizationStatus') IN ('approved','authorized') OR lower(t.raw->'operatorApproval'->>'status') = 'approved'`, and add a separate `authorization_pending` column. Do it in a NEW migration (sql/schema_v59.sql) that drops and recreates trip_ext — schema_v18.sql:17-40 warns in its own words that editing an earlier schema file is silently reverted by the sha ledger. Then return the pending count from api/analytics_routes.js:438 so api/public/corporate.js:133 can print "0 of 219 granted, 219 pending", and change :475's denominator to bookings at approval-requiring properties so the KPI matches the caption it already prints.
