area: Corporate -> Approach legs (the "Ended more than 15 km from anywhere" KPI tile and the stranding table's Over 15 km column), plus the Corporate -> Overview approach-leg caption
reproduced: GET /api/corporate/stranding?from=2025-09-01&to=2026-09-05&_=$RANDOM -> 32 places, 30 shown, max worst_km 2.3, max avg_return_km 1.02, sum of over_15km = 0. user_visible: Yes, but narrower than billed, and this is 95% a symptom of finding 2 rather than an independent defect. What a reader sees at days=30: 100 rows, of which 79 are correctly dimmed 'too few fixes to judge' (the caption names them), 6 read 'never triggers', and 15 read a confident 'ok' on the strength of one occupied fix. Not one plate with a demonstrably working pad is in the list. Severity LOWERED from high to medium: the panel discloses its own truncation and unjudged count, the real damage is the 15 false 'ok' verdicts and the total absence of the working pads, and fixing finding 2 removes 92 of the 100 offending rows at source. fix: Two changes, both small. In api/server.js:2620-2623, stop letting an unjudgeable plate win the ranking — either add `HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE seat_occupied IS NOT NULL) >= 20` and report the excluded count separately, or make the sort key `(count(*) FILTER (WHERE seat_occupied IS NOT NULL) >= 20) DESC` first so judgeable pads always outrank unjudgeable ones. In api/public/app.js:3092-3094, move the FIX_FLOOR test ahead of the `occupied_fixes > 0` test so a single occupied fix can never print 'ok'.

title: FMS answers a past-retention alert window with HTTP 200 {"error":"Authentication failed"} and fms.js files it as a bad password — 82 unrepairable provider-ceiling windows become 1,280 days of 'outstanding collection' and 82 red credential writes per backfill
area: #sources (Collector health), Settings (the backfill panel), the credential panel on #auth
reproduced: GET /api/status NOW: fms/backfill/ecosine status 'partial', chunks_total 171, chunks_failed 40; fms/backfill/egari 'partial', 159 / 42 — both exactly as claimed, 82 in total. I found evidence stronger than the finder's. Within the SAME run, on the SAME operation (GetAlertData), the day-by-day split of the 2026-05-16…2026-06-15 month answered 2026-06-15 down to 2026-06-05 with 1,608–2,113 rows each and then refused 2026-06-04 and every day below it as 'Authentication failed'. A password cannot be valid for 5 June and invalid for 4 June, minutes apart, on the same call. And the boundary date is IDENTICAL for both fleets on separate credentials (deepest ok single-day alert = 2026-06-05 for ecosine and egari alike), which rules out a session expiring mid-run. /api/coverage dataset_calendar.alerts NOW: first_day 2026-05-23, days_with_data 106, missing_days 0, gaps [] — a ~105-day provider ceiling, matching the file's own 'FMS keeps roughly a hundred days of alerts' (src/sources/fms.js:367). Everything downstream follows from that: fmsAuthRefusal exempts HTTP 400 first (fms.js:56) precisely so the size ceiling never reaches the credential panel, and the header warns 'a banner that is sometimes wrong is one nobody reads'. Production says out-of-retention windows answer 200 with an auth-shaped body instead, so the one case the design left unguarded is the one that fires 82 times a backfill. The product already has the correct pattern two files away: src/sources/uber.js:566/712/916/1140 classify a refusal past the horizon as 'outside retention', and docs/COVERAGE.md:78-83 spells out the reasoning ('This is a ceiling, not a bug').
user_visible: Yes, and the finder undersold it — I re-derived it from collectionDebt() in api/public/app.js:4252-4293 against the live /api/status. Of 135 failed windows the page classifies 37 as unservable (Uber's 'outside retention') and 4 as invented, leaving 94 'owed' — which expand to 1,364 distinct outstanding DAYS, of which 1,280 (640 ecosine + 640 egari, 2024-09-03 → 2026-06-04) are these FMS alert refusals. So the Settings warning box (api/public/app.js:5124-5133) tells the operator '1,364 days of collection are outstanding … FMS telematics · Ecosine 640 days (3 Sep 2024 → 4 Jun 2026), FMS telematics · Egari 640 days …' directly above a Re-run backfill button that can never recover a single one of them. 94% of the product's stated collection debt is a provider ceiling wearing the label 'Authentication failed'. Both FMS backfills are permanently 'partial', so the one signal that would show a REAL alert hole is saturated. Severity high stands.
fix: Give FMS the alert-retention horizon uber.js already has. In src/sources/fms.js:393-400, before calling noteFmsRefusal, test whether the window's end is older than the observed retention floor (derive it as max(occurred_at) in `alert` for the fleet minus the deepest window that has ever answered, or simply persist the deepest successful alert day per fleet). If it is, set chunk.error = `outside retention: ${refused}` — the string collectionDebt()'s UNSERVABLE regex at api/public/app.js:4251 already recognises — do NOT call noteFmsRefusal, and do not count the chunk in chunks_failed. Keep the credential verdict for windows INSIDE retention, where a refusal is still a real password problem. Surface the horizon on /api/coverage beside dataset_calendar.alerts so the ~105-day ceiling is stated rather than inferred.

title: earners/payments serves only a window whose END falls inside the last ~24h; the collector walks every historical week of a backfill against it, and the code's written model of why they come back empty is wrong

That growth through the day is the tell: the server clamps the request to [now-24h, now] and answers with the intersection. DOC agrees: get-driver-payments marks start_time required, "This can not be less than 24 hours from current time", end_time "can not be more than current time". CODE matches: src/sources/uber_fleet.js:216 `for (const wk of weekChunks(from, to))` inside pullEarningsComponents, which receives the run's whole window (src/sources/uber_fleet.js:447) and is reached from HISTORICAL at src/run.js:40 on every mode. THIS REFUTES THE CODE'S OWN MODEL at src/sources/uber_fleet.js:198-203 ("what comes back is the CURRENT payment period and nothing else, however the window is asked"): 2 and 3 September both sit inside the current payment period (Mon 31 Aug - Sun 6 Sep) and both return zero. TWO OF THE FINDER'S CLAIMS ARE WRONG. (a) The COVERAGE.md citation is fabricated — grep -n -i "earner|oauth|rest|reimburse|entitle" docs/COVERAGE.md returns nothing about this surface; only src/sources/uber_fleet.js:230-245 carries the Egari diagnosis, and that diagnosis is about an org the finder never probed, since /api/probe/uber/window uses config.uber.org (Ecosine) — so it is untested, not disproven. (b) The waste is understated by half: /api/status shows the uber_fleet backfill window as 2024-09-03..2026-09-03, which is ~104 weekChunks per fleet, so ~208 empty round trips per backfill, not ~104.
intent_check: Partly deliberate and partly a wrong theory. src/sources/uber_fleet.js:194-211 already knows the historical weeks are legitimately silent and deliberately declines to treat that as a fault ("Every historical week in a backfill is legitimately silent and no request can change that"), and the run-level zero-earner check at :276-283 was deliberately moved from per-week to per-run for exactly that reason. So the empty calls are a knowingly accepted cost, not an oversight. What is not deliberate, and is simply wrong, is the mechanism recorded at :198-203 — the discriminator is the window's end against now, not the payment period. The finding's real contribution is that correction.
user_visible: Nothing, and the finder's positive case is weaker than stated. /api/status shows every uber_fleet run (backfill, catchup, incremental, both fleets) as status "ok" — the false-diagnosis throw at src/sources/uber_fleet.js:279 does not fire, because the last chunk of every catch-up and backfill is the running week whose end is in the future and which returns 50 earners. And the reimbursement bucket is already sampled daily by that same running-week chunk on the 21:00 catch-up, and does reach the product: src/rollup.js:374-375 maps categories net_fare/reimbursements/expenses into money_event under source 'uber_rest_payments'. Worth checking at the same time, because it is the one thing here that could corrupt data: a chunk whose end is ~20h ago (the prior week, asked by a Monday catch-up) is inside the clamp and returns rows, but those rows are stamped with the PRIOR week's period_start/period_end at :333 while the money is the current 24h — verify before adding the skip, since the skip would also close that hole.

title: Six August days (19–24) publish a AED 44,903 false reconciliation gap because a stray 4-day Uber REST window supersedes the full week already held in driver_earnings_component
area: #reconcile — the all-time month table (August row) and the August day view; the Gap tile is the page's headline output
reproduced: GET /api/reconcile?month=2026-08&_=$RANDOM (fetched now): 08-17 ontrip_net 16344.24 / delta_pct -5.1; 08-18 16344.24 / -2.6; 08-19 8243.50 / +109.0; 08-20 8275.52 / +136.3; 08-21 8275.52 / +169.0; 08-22 8275.52 / +103.8; 08-23 7972.28 / +70.8; 08-24 9762.57 / +83.3; 08-25 18773.40 / +7.0; 08-26 18773.40 / -3.7. ontrip_drivers 233 on every one. expected_period_days_min is 4 on exactly 19–24 and 7 on all 25 other days; statement_partial:false and period_cut:false on all six. totals {delta 64896.43, delta_pct 19.1, expected_covered 339900.66, reconciled_rows 31, not_comparable_rows 0}. The six deltas add to exactly 44903.26 = 69.2% of August. GET /api/reconcile?_=$RANDOM: totals {delta 117766.37, expected_covered 1687686.35, delta_pct 7.0}; month rows Mar–Jul read -2.4, 3.0, 5.0, 4.9, 5.7 against August's 19.1. ROOT CAUSE, which the finder got wrong: the week is NOT short in our collection, it is fully held and being overridden. GET /api/earnings/components?from=2026-08-17&to=2026-08-23&platform=uber&fleet=ecosine gives your_earnings 78963.94 (163 drivers), tip 756.01, taxes_earnings -1376.10 → net 79584.03; fleet=egari gives 34672.29 / 456.00 / -609.38 → net 34825.67. Sum 114409.70, and 114409.70/7 = 16344.24 — precisely the figure the page prints on 17 and 18 Aug. GET /api/earnings/components?from=2026-08-19&to=2026-08-22&platform=uber&fleet=ecosine returns a SEPARATE 4-day net_fare window of 12726.87 over 52 drivers (likewise 20–23: 10020.85, and 21–24: 10638.89); the same query with fleet=egari returns []. src/rollup.js:707 selects DISTINCT ON (platform, fleet_id, driver_ext_id, day) and :723 orders by (p.period_end - p.period_start) ASC — the SHORTEST window wins — so those three 4-day run-stamps beat the week on days 19–24. Confirmed Ecosine-only by subtraction: Egari's share is 16344.24-11369.15 = 4975.09 on 18 Aug and 8275.52-3300.43 = 4975.09 on 21 Aug, identical, exactly as an Ecosine-only REST feed predicts.
intent_check: Deliberate, but only half of it. src/rollup.js:664-668 states the rule outright — 'Same resolution as the payout view: periods first, then one winner per day — the FINEST period covering it.' The codebase has since PROVEN that rule wrong on the other side and never carried the correction across: sql/schema_v58.sql, measured against AED 440,445.31 of real bank credits, says 'finer here means period_days = 1, not "any shorter span". Uber files 2, 3 and 4-day windows too … and a stray 4-day backfill row must not be allowed to vouch for a week's coverage or to suppress it.' That guard was added to driver_payout_day_finest only; driver_statement_day still runs the superseded rule. Separately, reconcile_routes.js:474 and :497 are heavily documented and both are honest about their scope — statement_partial is Uber's 192-day retention edge and period_cut is an open report period — so neither is meant to catch this, and :594 `comparable` therefore counts all six days into the headline. api/public/reconcile.js:192 basis() does render a dim '4- and 7-day reports mixed' note in the Expected payout column, which is the only thing on screen hinting at any of this; it does not stop the delta being toned red or counted.
user_visible: Yes, and it is the page's headline. api/public/reconcile.js:107 deltaPill tones anything over 10% 'bad' (red) unless statement_partial, period_cut, or the salik floor applies; salik is populated on all six days (147.48, 151.68 …) and on the August month row (1456.92), so the floor branch does not fire and every one of them renders red. An operator sees six consecutive day rows accusing Uber of overpaying by +70% to +169%, an August month row at +19.1% beside neighbours at 3–6%, and a Gap tile reading AED 117,766 / 7.0%. Re-derived independently: restoring the weekly grid on 19–24 Aug raises expected_covered by 40,463.74 (5 × 13130.87 minus the 32,520.40 actually published for 19–23, plus 15071.69 − 7741.90 for the 24th) and cuts delta by the same, giving August 24,432.69 / 6.4% (in line with Jul 5.7%) and an all-time 77,302.63 / 1,728,150.09 = 4.5%. The finder's 3.9% is the wrong counterfactual — it deletes all of August rather than the six broken days.
fix: Carry schema_v58's rule to the statement fold: in src/rollup.js:707-723 stop letting any window shorter than the provider's filing period win. Change the ORDER BY at :723 from `(p.period_end - p.period_start) ASC, p.period_start ASC` to prefer a true daily report first and the provider's canonical (longest) filing window next — `(p.days = 1) DESC, p.days DESC, p.period_start ASC` — then re-run refreshStatements to rebuild the source='uber_rest' slice. Containment in the meantime, one line in api/reconcile_routes.js:594: treat a row whose statement side mixes grids (expected_period_days_min < expected_period_days) as not comparable, the same grey treatment statement_partial already gets, so the six days stop being coloured red and stop entering totals.delta.

intent_check: Not deliberate, and not documented. api/analytics_routes.js:340-352 documents the ageing at length, but only about the OTHER bound: oldest_days used to be computed inside the range chip, RECV_TO_DATE now drops the lower bound so 'the tile can finally mean what it has always said.' This is a straight violation of the house rule that file states as canonical: 'a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON, never as zero.'
user_visible: Partly. The two empty buckets do render, with the same weight as the populated ones, so a reader of the Outstanding tab sees 'over 90 days — 0 counterparties, 0 bookings, AED 0' and concludes the fleet holds no aged debt. Since the hotel feed was already running 23–35 bookings a day (~30% of them on-account or salary) on its first recorded day, pre-July receivables plausibly exist and are simply invisible. But the misstatement is bounded and decays: the total outstanding (AED 76,546 over 634 bookings) is right for what is held, the closing note already says 'this is the exposure, not the ledger', and the oldest receivable is dated ~8 July, so the 61-90 bucket starts filling on 2026-09-07 and over-90 on 2026-10-06. I am downgrading high → medium on that basis. The finder's secondary claim about the 'Oldest debt: 59 days' tile is weak: the tone rule is `(r.oldest_days ?? 0) > 60` (api/public/settlement.js:400), 59 is the true age of the oldest unsettled booking on record, the sub already reads 'on record', and the tile turns warn on 2026-09-07 regardless. fix: In api/analytics_routes.js, add min(local_day) over is_receivable to the same aggregate that already produces the buckets (query at :372-380), return it as e.g. record_starts, and in api/public/settlement.js:405-420 render any bucket whose entire span falls before that date as 'no record — the receivable record starts 7 Jul 2026' instead of AED 0. intent_check: Not deliberate — the file argues against itself. sql/schema_v18.sql:136-137 introduces the on_account bucket with 'business is Bolt Business: a company account settled by invoice, the same arrangement as a room charge and a corporate booking', and then sixteen lines later is_receivable answers 'Is this fare owed to us by somebody after the ride ended?' with a list that leaves business out. What a reader actually sees with the Bolt chip on: an 'On account' card reading 62 bookings, 'Outstanding until the hotel settles', Revenue AED 2,076, Priced 29 of 62, Channels Bolt, ending in 'Open →'; following it lands on a Receivables tab showing only 'Nothing to show — Nothing outstanding in this window'. Money at stake is AED 2,076 of known fare plus 33 unpriced Bolt Business bookings, 0.1% of trips — hence medium, not high.
fix: Widen is_receivable to the on-account set it already shares a bucket with: add 'company','corporate','invoice','business' at sql/schema_v18.sql:152-153, and update the identical predicate in the partial index at sql/schema_v31.sql:28 in the same change (per COVERAGE.md's CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW trap, rename the view rather than editing v18 in place if the column list moves). If the narrower predicate is wanted instead, then say so on both surfaces — name the classes the ledger covers in the receivables note at api/public/settlement.js:455 and on the mix card's meaning. Independently, change api/analytics_routes.js:387 to `t?.priced_trips ? round(NUM(t.amount) || 0, 0) : null` so an unpriced receivable set renders absent rather than as AED 0.

title: refreshMoneyEvents DELETEs money_event outside a transaction, so the Money provenance page states "No provider sent a figure for this window" for ~75s of every 900s, and a wrong-but-plausible total for ~35s more
area: Money provenance page (api/public/provenance.js, fed by GET /api/money/sources); every reader of money_event
reproduced: Reproduced independently on a different pass than the finder's. GET https://fleet-dashboard-wpeqb.ondigitalocean.app/api/money/sources?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31&_=$RANDOM, polled every ~2s across the */15 fire at 10:00 UTC 2026-09-05: 10:00:50-10:01:46 rows=21 amount=4,614,074.57 rows_seen=30,764; 10:01:49-10:03:04 rows=0 amount=0 rows_seen=0 (75 consecutive seconds); 10:03:05 rows=6 amount=740,768.19 (16%); 10:03:15 rows=9 amount=2,278,446.30 (49%); 10:03:25 rows=14 amount=4,257,358.45 (92%); 10:03:39 rows=21 amount=4,614,074.57 restored. Corrupt window 10:01:47->10:03:39 = 112s of 900s = 12.4% of wall-clock (finder said 137s/15% — same defect, slightly smaller). GET /api/rollups confirms money_event duration_ms=103582, finished_at 2026-09-05T09:48:14.639Z. Code checks out: src/rollup.js:421-422 is `async function refreshMoneyEvents(db) { await db.query('DELETE FROM money_event');` with no BEGIN, against BEGIN/COMMIT at src/rollup.js:523/553, :659/752, :1088/1126. One line number has drifted: the call site is src/rollup.js:478, not :484 as the finding says. Cache mechanism confirmed: api/cache.js:82-84 keys on max(collection_run.finished_at)|max(rollup_state.finished_at), and src/rollup.js:219-231 (runOne) writes finished_at only on completion, so the version is frozen for the whole rebuild and the first partial answer is cached and re-served to every later reader until the pass ends.
intent_check: Not deliberate, and the codebase says so itself. The comment at src/rollup.js:417-420 justifies rebuilding the table WHOLE rather than merging — it says nothing about doing so unprotected. Twelve lines earlier, refreshPayouts carries the opposite rule in writing (src/rollup.js:517-521): "DELETE, not TRUNCATE: TRUNCATE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and blocks every reader for the duration of the rebuild, while DELETE inside the transaction lets a concurrent reader see the previous complete answer until the commit swaps it." money_event is the only one of the four whole-table rebuilds that does not follow that stated rule. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md or docs/AUDIT.md addresses it.
user_visible: Yes, and worse than a blank. api/public/provenance.js:57-60: when d.rows is empty the page renders the sentence "No provider sent a figure for this window" with the subtitle "Not a quiet week necessarily — Collection gaps says which feeds ran." That is a confident false claim: 21 channels sent AED 4,614,074.57 across 30,764 figures. During the ~35s partial phase it shows AED 740,768 / 2,278,446 / 4,257,358 as finished totals with no indication of a rebuild.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the finder's proposed fix: its claim that refreshPayouts/refreshStatements/refreshLifetime are also broken because they issue BEGIN/COMMIT through pool.query() did NOT reproduce. title: Cron-fired catch-ups and backfills create no collector_job row, so they get no checkpoint, no boot requeue and no line on the Settings jobs table
area: Settings > jobs table; the nightly 21:00 catch-up and Sunday 22:00 backfill
reproduced: Code confirmed line by line. src/index.js:98 `cron.schedule('0 21 * * *', () => catchUp(30)` and src/index.js:100 `cron.schedule('0 22 * * 0', () => backfill()` — both called with no onProgress, fleet or jobId. src/run.js:159 `const ckpt = jobId ? await loadCheckpoint(jobId) : NO_CHECKPOINT;` takes the null branch; src/checkpoint.js:44 `if (!jobId) return NO_CHECKPOINT;` and :35-40 make has() always false and mark() a no-op. The boot requeue at src/index.js:344 is `WHERE status = 'running'` on collector_job, a row a cron run never creates. `grep -rn 'INSERT INTO collector_job'` returns api/server.js:3301 and :3328 only (plus sql/schema_v14.sql:41, a migration, and two test files — the finder's list is right for runtime paths). Production now, GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM at 2026-09-05T10:41:56Z: newest catchup finished_at across all eleven rows is still 2026-09-03T21:20:42.733Z — 37.4 hours old against a 24-hour cadence, so the 2026-09-04 21:00 catch-up is confirmed absent, exactly as the finder measured 5.5 hours earlier.
intent_check: Not deliberate. Nothing in the cron block's long comment (src/index.js:88-101) or in docs/ addresses job rows for scheduled runs. The opposite: docs/COVERAGE.md:181-185 publishes a schedule table promising "catch-up | 21:00 daily | 30 days | runs the fare walk: yes" — a documented promise production is not keeping, with no mechanism to notice.
user_visible: Partly — and the finder overstates this half. The Settings jobs table reads collector_job and shows nothing for a scheduled run, so a cron catch-up is invisible there whether it ran or not. But /api/status DOES carry a mode='catchup' row per source, so a completed cron catch-up leaves a trace and its 37.4-hour age is readable on the Data-sources page. What is missing is any statement of expected cadence for a scheduled source (silence and cadence are null on every incremental and catchup row), so nothing on screen says the nightly pass is a day and a half late. "No trace anywhere a reader looks" is too strong; "no row, no cadence expectation, and no alert" is accurate.
fix: Change src/index.js:98 and :100 to INSERT INTO collector_job (mode, requested_by) VALUES ('catchup'|'backfill', 'schedule') and let the existing poller at src/index.js:144-160 claim it. That buys progress, checkpoint resume, the boot requeue and a visible Settings row with no new machinery. Verified compatible: the poller's jobRunning guard makes a scheduled job wait in the database rather than in memory, which is strictly better than today.

title: One in-memory promise queue serialises every collection, so an operator backfill has blocked the half-hourly incremental for 7.1 hours and counting, and the queue dies with the container
area: Every page that reads trips — the day page most visibly; Settings > jobs
reproduced: Reproduced and materially worse than measured. GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM at 2026-09-05T10:41:56Z: newest incremental finished_at for every source is 2026-09-05T03:37:40.267Z — 7.1 hours against a 30-minute cadence, i.e. 14 */30 cron fires (04:00 through 10:30) landing nothing. The finder measured 95 minutes at 05:12; it has since grown to 426 minutes. GET /api/settings/jobs?_=$RANDOM at 10:30:00Z: job 50 (backfill, requested_by=admin, requested_at 2026-09-04T13:41:21Z, started_at 2026-09-05T03:33:49Z after a death at 03:33:11) is status=running with done=0 of 8, current='uber', step index 64 of 105 on fleet=egari, remaining=['uberFleet','yango','bolt','hotel','external','events','fms'] — 7 of 8 sources never reached after 21 hours, advancing ~1 window per 5 minutes, with FMS (documented at 4.5h) still to come. Code confirmed: src/run.js:65-77 is a module-level `let queued = 0; let tail = Promise.resolve();` with tail-chaining and no dedupe; `queued` is referenced only at src/run.js:68/69/72 and exposed by no endpoint.
intent_check: Half of this finding walks into a documented decision and half does not — the finder did not read src/run.js:42-64. The serialisation is deliberate and reasoned: the barrier exists because backfill and incremental both drive the Uber report pipeline, which the provider caps at three reports in flight per org. The chained queue specifically replaced a broken single-inFlight gate. So the finder's proposed fix (1), coalescing an arriving incremental over a queued one, directly contradicts the written rule at src/run.js:50-51 — "A queued run waits rather than being dropped: skipping it silently is how a collection gap opens without anything saying so" — and should not be adopted as stated. Its proposed fix (2) is the right one and the comment supports it: the contention named in the code IS the report-slot cap, not runWindow as a whole. What is nowhere documented, and is the real defect: unbounded head-of-line blocking, a queue no endpoint exposes, and a queue destroyed on restart. The mechanism has inverted its own stated purpose — it was built so gaps would not open silently, and it is now the cause of a 7-hour gap that nothing announces.
user_visible: Yes, directly and right now. GET /api/day?day=2026-09-05&_=$RANDOM at 10:15:18Z returns headline.bookings=71, drivers=30, last_at=2026-09-05T03:24:22Z — at 10:15 in the morning the day page shows the fleet's last trip as 03:24 and seven hours of the working day simply missing, with no banner, no staleness note and no indication that fourteen collections are stacked behind a backfill. Settings shows only "backfill running".
fix: Replace the whole-runWindow barrier with a per-org semaphore around the Uber report calls only (the contention src/run.js:44-48 actually names), so the cheap 3-day incremental interleaves with a long backfill instead of queueing behind it. Keep the no-drop rule the comment states. Separately, persist the queue — folding scheduled runs into collector_job (see the previous finding) gives durability across restarts for free, and exposing a queue depth would have made this visible on day one. Do not adopt the coalescing half of the finder's fix.

title: chunks_failed counts provider-retention refusals as failures, so Uber's backfill reads 4.75x more broken than it is on the Data-sources page
area: Data-sources page (api/public/app.js), Windows and Detail columns and the page's failure headline
reproduced: Production numbers reproduce exactly, unchanged. GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM 2026-09-05T10:05Z, classifying failed_windows by error text: uber/backfill/ecosine chunks_failed=38 of chunks_total=155 = 30 'outside retention: ... invalid date range' + 8 'Error: download timed out after 600s for report <uuid>'; uber/backfill/egari chunks_failed=8 of 79 = 7 retention + 1 'endDate is too late'; uber/catchup ecosine and egari chunks_failed=1 each, both 'endDate is too late'. Code confirmed: src/db.js:238 computes `const failed = chunks ? chunks.filter((c) => c.error).length : null;` with no `expected` test, and that value is written to chunks_failed at src/db.js:264-274 and also drives status='partial'. Decisively, src/sources/uber.js:731 already computes the correct figure one function away — `const failed = chunks.filter((c) => c.error && !c.expected).length;` — and logs it, so the source knows the answer and the column does not.
intent_check: Confirms rather than refutes. docs/COVERAGE.md:78-84 states the retention limit in terms that settle it: "Uber's report retention is about 12 months... the walk now classifies a refusal there as `outside retention` rather than as a hole. This is a ceiling, not a bug." The product's own documentation says these must not be counted as failures, and the counter counts them.
user_visible: Yes. api/public/app.js:4496-4497 renders the Windows column as chunks_total minus chunks_failed, so Uber's ecosine backfill shows "117 of 155" when 147 landed and only 8 are real holes; app.js:4512-4513 renders "38 windows did not land — see below"; app.js:4368 folds the row into the page's `partial` count and amber tone. An operator is sent after 30 windows that can never be fetched. Note this over-reports breakage rather than hiding it — the 8 genuine timeouts are still counted — which is why this is medium and not high.
fix: One line. src/db.js:238 becomes `const failed = chunks ? chunks.filter((c) => c.error && !c.expected).length : null;`, matching src/sources/uber.js:731. Note this does NOT require widening the detail projection the finder proposed — `expected` is still on the in-memory chunk objects at that point. Optionally carry the retention count as its own stated ceiling on the page.

title: logRun's detail projection drops eight chunk keys, so `unmatched` — the count of Uber payment rows that matched no trip — reaches no page
area: Data-sources page failed-window detail; Uber fare/trip reconciliation, which has no surface at all
reproduced: Split out of the same finding as the item above: it is a second, separable defect with a different fix. Projection confirmed at src/db.js:281-289, which emits only {from, to, rows, kind?, skipped?, error}. Every other key a source sets is dropped: `expected` (src/sources/uber.js:577, :714, :917), `throttled` (uber.js:578), `open` (uber.js:504), `orders` (uber.js:552), `unmatched` (uber.js:552), `settlements` (uber.js:553), `split_from_refusal` (src/sources/fms.js:163 and :383). Confirmed downstream on production: every entry in failed_windows from GET /api/status?_=$RANDOM carries exactly the keys ['error','from','to']. `unmatched` semantics verified at src/sources/uber.js:535-552 — priced counts rowCount from an UPDATE keyed on (platform, external_id, fleet_id), so unmatched = trips.length - priced is genuinely payment rows whose fare was fetched and then written nowhere. I did not confirm the finder's citation of bolt.js:690 for a `fleet` key.
intent_check: The projection is a whitelist that was never widened, not a reasoned exclusion. Its two comments (src/db.js:269-276 and :282-285) exist to explain why `kind` and `skipped` were ADDED after each caused a specific misreading on the page; no comment anywhere argues that the other keys should be withheld. docs/COVERAGE.md discusses the fare/trip agreement question at length but has no counter that answers it.
user_visible: Nothing on screen is wrong because of this one — correcting the finder, this is a hole, not a bad number. The consequence is an absence: the only counter that would prove the Uber payments report and the trip report describe the same trips is computed, logged to stdout, and discarded at the INSERT, so no page can answer it. `throttled` is the second loss — a payments-generation cap that halts a whole fleet's fare walk (src/sources/uber.js:602) is stored indistinguishably from a plain failure.

Averaging them into a first-third/last-third comparison drags both ends toward zero", and the panel's on-screen caption says "a month the record only partly covers holds fewer days than it looks like it does" and names Sep 26 as excluded for exactly that reason — while silently admitting Dec 24 as the first month of its baseline. AND bookings > 0`. Within the one endpoint the metric is bookings-only (Oct 24 and Nov 24 both report trips:0 despite 6,954 FMS journeys) while the coverage flag is all-trips.

Verdict panel, verbatim: "2,744 driver-hours were available and not dispatched. The worst-selling hour with real supply behind it is Sat 00:00 — 24 online hours on a typical one, selling 0 jobs. The best is Fri 11:00, at 1.46 against 0." and "Recommendation: Sat 00:00 sells 0 jobs an online hour against the fleet's own 0.78. Bringing just that hour up to average is about 19 more jobs over this window — or the same supply moved somewhere it sells." DOM read of the grid: Sat row cells = b0,b0,b0,b0 then 20 x none; every other populated cell on the whole grid is b1-b5, so the four Saturday cells are the ONLY "sold nothing" cells. Cell tooltips: "Sat 00:00 — on a typical one: 24 online h, 0 jobs, 23.1 h idle · 0 jobs per online hour · measured over 1 occurrence". The live band at the top of the same page reads "71 bookings so far today, as of 13:15 Dubai". Endpoints: GET /api/supply/balance?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-05 -> {dow:6,h:0,online_h:24,on_job_h:0.9,jobs:0,total_jobs:0,occurrences:1}; GET /api/compare?a=2026-09-05 hours[0..3] = {a:17},{a:14},{a:5},{a:11} = 47 real bookings in the four hours the grid calls empty.
intent_check: Read api/supply_routes.js:80-215 and api/public/supply.js:20-190. Clamping the demand/on-job halves to the availability feed's span IS deliberate and heavily commented (the 12-month "1% idle" bug). The defect is not the clamp, it is the CLOCK the clamp is expressed in, and the file itself proves the author knew: `measured.from/to` were deliberately converted with dubaiIso() (long comment at supply_routes.js:245-270 about "two clocks in one object"), while the very same span is fed to the occurrence series and to the demand filter as `String(bounded[1]).slice(0,10)` — the UTC calendar day of an instant. trip_norm.local_day is a Dubai day, so $2::date = 2026-09-04 and the whole Dubai day Sep 5 leaves the numerator while the supply query (which uses the raw window `p`) keeps its 54.2 online hours. Proved independently: GET /api/supply/balance?from=2026-08-29&to=2026-09-05 answers measured.to = "2026-09-05" yet occurrences:1 for dow 6 over a span containing TWO Saturdays, and returns Sat h0 as online_h 24 (that is Sep 5's supply) against jobs 16 (that is Aug 29's demand, identical to the isolated Aug 28-30 query) — supply from one Saturday divided by demand from another. Not a documented choice; a Dubai/UTC slip of exactly the kind DAYWIN() in api/server.js:243 exists to prevent.
user_visible: The single recommendation the page makes — which hour to cut supply in — points at Sat 00:00, an hour in which the fleet actually took 17 bookings on 24 online hours (0.71/h, near the fleet's own 0.78). An operator acting on it would pull drivers off an hour that is working. It also violates the documented house rule in docs/COVERAGE.md:31 ("a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON, never as zero") — the grid has a dedicated "no availability collected" band and this uses band 0 "sold nothing" instead. Because the default window is "This month", which always ends today, this misfires every day. One correction to the finder: the effect on the headline idle figure is trivial, not material — dropping the four Saturday cells moves 70% to 69%.
fix: In api/supply_routes.js:110, build `bounded` with dubaiIso(span.to_at)/dubaiIso(span.from_at) (already imported from src/util.js and already used for `measured`) instead of the UTC iso() slice, so the occurrence series (line ~186) and the demand/on-job filters (FB, lines 141-165) are clamped on the same Dubai calendar the local_day column is keyed on. Then in api/public/supply.js:127 exclude from `real` any weekday-hour whose demand span does not fully cover it, and draw those cells with the existing `none` class rather than band 0.

title: #compare reads the collector's lag as a collapse — the exact thing the page exists to prevent
seen_on_screen: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Complete-Dashboard/0660f87d-a2e3-59b6-b081-f0d983081bd1/scratchpad/audit/shots2/vB-compare.png. Tiles read "BOOKINGS 71 vs 304 / Sep 5 against Sep 4", "CHANGE ▼ 233 (77%) / both days to 12:30 Dubai". Basis note, verbatim: "Both days counted up to 12:30 Dubai, so a fall means less work done by the same hour — not a day that has not finished yet." Verdict at the foot: "233 bookings fewer than the day before … −77% ON THE DAY BEFORE / 71 against 304". The live band on the SAME page reads "71 bookings so far today, as of 13:17 Dubai" and "latest booking 07:24". (The finder saw 71 vs 110 / 35% at 09:00; the defect is unchanged and now larger.) Endpoint: GET /api/compare?a=2026-09-05&b=2026-09-04&cut=auto -> cut_minutes 795, cut_label "13:15", totals.a.last_at 2026-09-05T03:23:17Z = 07:23 Dubai, totals.b.last_at 2026-09-04T09:14:52Z. hours[7]={a:2,b:25}, hours[8]={a:0,b:39}, hours[9..13] a:0 against b 43/44/77/44/31.
intent_check: Read api/compare_routes.js:1-80 and api/public/compare.js:1-230. The cut-at-the-same-Dubai-minute design is deliberate and is the module's entire stated purpose. The unhandled case is that the cut is wall-clock NOW while side A's feed reaches only 07:23 — nowMinutes() never consults totals.a.last_at, which the same response already carries. The page's own rule 3 mitigation ("Was everything collected?") DOES fire, but for the wrong reason and with a threshold that misses this: it prints "5 sources last succeeded over a day ago" naming Bolt, events, ledger, uber_profile and Yango — while the source that actually stopped, Uber, shows Last success 07:34 and is not flagged, because staleness is judged at 24 h. So the caveat is luck, not coverage, and it sits below the fold under an unqualified −77%.
user_visible: Yes, and the sign is wrong, not just the magnitude. Through the hours today has actually been collected (00:00-06:59) today took 17+14+5+11+6+7+9 = 69 against yesterday's 4+16+6+7+2+2+9 = 46 — up 50%. The page states down 77%, in warn tone, with an explicit assurance that the fall is real work not lost. That the fleet is still working right now is directly checkable: GET /api/live at 13:21 Dubai returns 87 fresh trackers, 22 'Moving', 19 above 5 km/h, 5 'Engaged' and 1 'ONTRIP'. Every trip-writing collector last succeeded 07:34-07:37 Dubai; only cabman and uber_timeline have run since. Reaches the operator every morning the collector lags, and it also drives the Drivers-out delta (30 vs 90) and the 68-name NOT OUT list.
fix: In api/compare_routes.js, cap the auto cut at min(nowMinutes(), the Dubai minute of the running day's max(requested_at)) — that value is already computed as totals.a.last_at — and widen cut_note to name the reach when the two differ ("Sep 5 is collected to 07:23; the 13:15 cut leaves 5 h 52 m with nothing to compare"). api/public/compare.js:196-206 consumes cut_note unchanged, so the caption fixes itself.

intent_check: Read api/public/compare.js:221-224 (`if (partial && p.full_day.b)` emits "${dayStr(b)} finished on …" with no is_today guard), :396-402 (night-driver caveat guarded on `p.is_today.a` alone), :393-395 (roster headings assume a is the later day), and the verdict at :160-179 ("than the day before" assumes a > b). title: #platforms reports FMS telematics as a channel that "delivered nothing" and prints 0 where the code has an em-dash branch
seen_on_screen: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Complete-Dashboard/0660f87d-a2e3-59b6-b081-f0d983081bd1/scratchpad/audit/shots2/vB-platforms-share.png. Verdict panel, verbatim: "FMS telematics, FMS telematics are configured and have delivered nothing in this window — every rate computed "per platform" for those is arithmetic over no rows." Channel bar below: "FMS telematics · 0 / no booking in this window". Coverage table on the same screen: "FMS telematics | Ecosine | 0 | 135,657 | Oct 1, 2024 | Sep 5, 2026" and "FMS telematics | Egari | 0 | 85,462 | Nov 6, 2024 | Sep 5, 2026" — a literal 0, not the em-dash. The page footer on the same screen: "FMS telematics 221,119 in journeys rather than bookings — these feeds watch the cars, they do not sell rides." Endpoint: /api/platforms returns bookings:0 and window_bookings:0 for both fms rows, never null.
intent_check: Read api/public/app.js:1886-1935 and api/server.js:2652-2660. The page's author plainly intended absent-not-zero here: app.js:1931 carries a live branch `r.bookings == null ? '—'`, and docs/COVERAGE.md:31 states the house rule. That branch is dead code, because the SQL computes `count(*) FILTER (WHERE platform <> 'fms')`, which is 0 for an fms row by construction and never null. Separately, `dead` at app.js:1886 is built per platform+fleet ROW, so a telematics feed with no bookings will be flagged as a dead sales channel in every window forever. One correction to the finder's impact text: Bolt and Yango are NOT in that sentence — both have window_bookings > 0 (104/43 and 7), so `dead` contains only the two FMS rows.
user_visible: A tracker feed that by design sells no rides is named, in the page's most prominent sentence, as a configured sales channel that delivered nothing, with the alarming rider that "every rate computed per platform for those is arithmetic over no rows" — for a feed nobody computes per-platform rates for. The page contradicts itself in its own footer. Misleading rather than materially wrong: the 0 is arithmetically true (an FMS row is not a booking) and the label "FMS telematics" carries a hint. Downgraded from high.
fix: api/server.js:2652 — return `bookings: null` / `window_bookings: null` for a source with no is_booking rows at all, so the existing ent-off branches at app.js:1931 and :1951 fire; and in api/public/app.js:1886 exclude no-booking telematics feeds from `dead` so they get their own line rather than being reported as a dead channel every window.

GET /api/driver/kpis?period=month&id=64686123-… returns revenue "2710.55", priced_trips 44, avg_fare "61.60", accounted_fares null, statement_fares null. Fayed reproduces it: "FARES — no trip carries a fare and no statement reports one" beside "MONEY IN AED 435" while his Activity tab prints AED 635 of fares on Sep 4 (shots2/fayed-overview.png, shots2/fayed-activity2.png). At period=year the tile prints "FARES / AED 94,937 / the platform's own figure, over 32 weekly statements — no trip here carries a fare" (shots2/wisal-year-overview.png) while the Earnings tab on the same window reads "BOOKED REVENUE AED 149,158 … over 2,477 of 2,691 trips that report a fare" (shots2/wisal-year-earnings2.png). intent_check: Half deliberate, half not. api/income_sql.js:341-347 excludes a payout-basis platform from accounted_fares on purpose, with a long comment — "a platform counted on its payout does not also contribute its fares, or the total would exceed itself" — and that decision is correct for `accounted`. But api/public/ui.js:1329 is where the tile is built, and its own header comment states the contract it breaks: "the third is a real dash: no fare on any trip AND no statement reporting one is genuinely unmeasured, and says so." Here 44 of 49 trips carry a fare, so the dash branch is firing on a measured driver. docs/COVERAGE.md's house rule says the same thing from the other side: "a figure that CAN be answered better must not render absent." The premise the tile's comment rests on — "Uber's trip export carries NO fare column — /api/revenue reports priced_bookings 0 and fare_coverage_pct 0 for it in every period" — is stale: COVERAGE.md's own table shows Ecosine uber at 99.9-100% priced from Sep 2025 onward, and this driver's kpis prove it. So the exclusion is reasoned; printing "no trip carries a fare" over it is not.
user_visible: For 69 of 147 active drivers (AED 123,321 of fares this window) the flagship tile asserts the fleet holds no fare data at all, sending anyone to chase a missing-fare-column integration that is not missing; and at a year window the tile labelled Fares reads AED 94,937 against the AED 149,158 the next tab calls fares — a 36% gap, so the answer to "what did this person's work bring in" depends on which tab you land on.
fix: api/public/ui.js faresTile(): when accounted_fares and statement_fares are both null but k.priced_trips > 0, render k.revenue with a sub naming the denominator and warning against adding it to the payout beside it. Print "no trip carries a fare" only when priced_trips is 0. Same for the statement_fares branch — drop "no trip here carries a fare" when priced_trips > 0.

Adding the Statement column instead would count those days twice." (shots2/wisal-earnings.png). intent_check: The finder is on the code's own side. api/driver_routes.js:2062 emits counted_total with the comment "The sum the caption prints, computed here rather than left to the page to add up — the two disagreed by AED 1,538 in production", and driver.js's own comment above the table says "The column that adds up is Counted, so it is the one totalled and the one the note explains." intent_check: Same window on all three, confirmed. The code claims check out exactly: api/economics_routes.js:560 bands on money>0; api/playbook_routes.js:85 is count(*) FILTER (WHERE bookings > 0) labelled earning; api/public/vehicle.js:1176 is { label: 'Took a booking', value: fmt(earning), sub: 'earned in this window' } where the value counts bookings. Not documented anywhere as deliberate. BUT the magnitude is one vehicle and it is a short-window edge artefact I could not reproduce at any other range: /api/economics/assets?period=month has exactly one row (plate L10595, 3 bookings, money null, band moved_unpaid) that separates the two counts, and at days=30 the two definitions agree exactly (102 bookings>0, 102 money>0). The gap is a car whose September payout has not landed yet, not a standing definitional split in the data.
user_visible: One car in 273 (0.4%) is filed as "earning" on two pages and "moved, no money" on a third, and #vehicles states in words that 93 cars "earned" when 92 did. The caption is genuinely false for that car, and will be false for any car whose booking outruns its payout at a window edge — but there is no reader decision that flips on it, and it vanishes at any window wider than a few days. That is why I dropped this from high to low.
fix: Two one-liners: change playbook_routes.js:85 to FILTER on the money column so "earning" means money everywhere, and fix vehicle.js:1176 so the 93 is captioned "took a booking" with the money count stated separately — the house rule in COVERAGE.md already requires absence to carry a reason.

title: #platforms prints Hotel at AED 11,092 where every other money surface prints AED 11,002 — the complimentary-ride exclusion the schema comment says was already fixed
seen_on_screen: #platforms Share tab, "This month": "Hotel · 145 — AED 11,092 reported" (shots2/platforms.png, shots2/agree2-platforms-hotel-11092.png). #revenue channel table, same window (page footer: "Window Sep 1, 2026 – Sep 5, 2026, 5 Dubai days inclusive"): "Hotel 145 · 142 · 98% · FARES (GROSS) AED 11,002" (shots2/revenue.png). #unit channel table: "Hotel GROSS FARE AED 11,002" (shots2/unit-money.png). Uber, Bolt and Yango match to the dirham between #platforms and #revenue (152,159 / 4,807 / 246) — Hotel is the only row that differs, by exactly AED 90.
intent_check: Verified as an un-deliberate regression against the product's own written invariant. /api/mix?by=platform&period=month returns hotel revenue 11092, priced_n 145; /api/corporate/summary?period=month returns revenue 11002, priced 142, foc_trips 3 — 3 complimentary rides × AED 30. Cause is exactly as claimed: api/server.js:993-994 is `round(sum(price)::numeric,0) revenue, count(*) FILTER (WHERE price IS NOT NULL) priced_n` with no has_fare filter, while api/revenue_routes.js:190 is `sum(n.price) FILTER (WHERE n.has_fare)`. sql/schema_v18.sql:100-102 defines has_fare and the comment directly above it says this exact defect was found and closed at the view: "Excluded here rather than at each of the fifty call sites, because a rule applied in fifty places is applied in forty-nine." /api/mix is that fiftieth call site.
user_visible: The channel-share panel counts rides that were given away as money. I measured the magnitude myself rather than taking it on trust: AED 90 on the current window (0.8% of Hotel, 0.08% of the fleet), and AED 520 over 365 days (137,177 vs 136,656.92 — 16 FOC rides). Hotel is the only channel with FOC payment types, so it does not in fact propagate across every /api/mix dimension the way the finding implies. Real bug, cheap fix, correct to report — but under 1% of one channel, so medium rather than high.
fix: Add FILTER (WHERE has_fare) to the revenue and priced_n aggregates in the /api/mix handler (api/server.js:993-994), matching api/revenue_routes.js:190. trip_norm already exposes has_fare, so it is a one-line change introducing no new definition.

title: #reconcile's September money is exactly 6/5 of the same month's money on #finance, #revenue and #overview — a seventh day of a weekly statement counted on one page only
seen_on_screen: The numbers are exactly as reported. #reconcile Sep 2026 row: "3,164 | AED 89,250 | AED 635 | AED 1,357 | AED 7,766 | AED 83,476 · AED 69,563 compared · a 7-day report spread" (shots2/reconcile.png, shots2/agree2-reconcile-sep2026-row.png). #revenue same month: "ON-TRIP REVENUE AED 74,375", "TIPS AED 529", "CASH THE PLATFORMS REPORT AED 6,492". The 6/5 arithmetic holds to the cent: 74374.62 × 6/5 = 89249.54 (row: 89249.55); 529.29 × 6/5 = 635.15 (635.14); 1130.64 × 6/5 = 1356.77 (1356.77); 6471.50 × 6/5 = 7765.80 (7765.80).
intent_check: The two pages are NOT showing the same window, and the product says so in three places. api/public/data.js:347 puts 'reconcile' in NO_RANGE with the comment "NO_RANGE hides only the window (reconciliation is whole months by construction)" — and on screen #reconcile's toolbar genuinely has no date-range chip, unlike every other page in this cluster, which all carry "This month▾". The page states it in prose: "Every month on record — Oct 2024 → Sep 2026 … The date range at the top of the page does not apply to a table of months, so it is not offered here." /api/reconcile returns scope {kind:'all-time', from:'2024-10-01', to:'2026-09-30'} and the Sep row carries days_total:30, ontrip_days:6, period_cut:true. So the reconcile row is the CALENDAR month September, and the weekly Uber statement running 2026-08-31 → 2026-09-06 (visible on the same page: "2026-08-31 → 2026-09-06 Uber ecosine 163 AED 61,435 WHOLE") contributes 6 of its 7 days to that month. Every other page is on the product default "This month" = month-TO-DATE, Sep 1–5, and takes 5 of the same 7 days. Six-fifths, exactly.
user_visible: Nothing is contradicted. Per the cluster's own rule, a difference explained by a different window is refuted, and this one is: calendar month vs month-to-date, with the extra day being the sixth day of an already-published weekly statement. Two supporting claims in the finding are also misreadings. (1) "TRIPS 3,164 proves it is the same window" — it does not: no booking exists on Sep 6, so a calendar-month and a to-date trip count are necessarily identical while the statement-derived money columns are not. (2) "The row says '5 days' in its own last column while its money columns cover six" — that column is headed COMPARED OVER and renders matched_days (the driver-days BOTH sides describe, 5), not the span of the money columns; api/public/reconcile.js:255-260 and the comment above it say exactly that. The page also already flags the forward portion on the bank side ("AED 12,718 not yet paid", accrual_days 1) and pins a period_cut note reading "This month is still inside an open report period … cutting both at today compares an average against a measurement. It settles when the period closes."
why_refuted: Different windows: #reconcile's month table is whole calendar months by construction (NO_RANGE in api/public/data.js:347; no range chip on the page; the page says so in prose; /api/reconcile scope to 2026-09-30), so the Sep 2026 row takes 6 days of the Aug 31 → Sep 6 weekly statement, while #finance/#revenue/#overview are on the default month-to-date Sep 1–5 and take 5 of the same 7. That is the entire 6/5 factor, on all four money columns. Neither page is wrong about its own window.
fix: No cross-page fix needed. If anything survives, it is a much smaller cosmetic point outside this cluster: the on-trip net / tips / salik / cash columns silently include the share of an open period dated after today, while the bank column beside them flags its accrual explicitly ("AED 12,718 not yet paid"). Extending that same dim annotation to the other four columns would make the row self-describing — but it is a polish item, not a disagreement.

title: Completion: #overview's tile says 12.0% cancelled and its own chart, 400px below, says 11.0% did not complete
page: #overview (Completion tile vs Trip outcome panel), cross-checked against #demand and the phone Today screen
seen_on_screen: One page, one request, two answers. #overview tile: "COMPLETION 88.0% / 12.0% cancelled". Trip-outcome panel below it: "Completed · 88.0% / Did not complete · 11.0% / Other / not reported · 1.0%", with the roll-up "Did not complete: rider_cancelled 290, client_cancelled 35, driver_cancelled 16, driver_cancelled_after_accept 4, client_did_not_show 1, driver_rejected 1 · Other / not reported: driver_did_not_respond 31, optional_ride_driver_did_not_respond 1" (shots2/overview.png). Sharper than the finding states: #demand's day table uses the IDENTICAL phrase "DID NOT COMPLETE" and sums 15+104+86+96+78 = 379 over 3,164, with "NEITHER YET" 0 on every row (shots2/demand.png). Phone Today: "COMPLETED 88% / 12% cancelled" (shots2/m-today.png). Arithmetic checks: 347/3164 = 11.0%, 379/3164 = 12.0%, the 32 unanswered offers are the whole difference.
intent_check: Not deliberate — it contradicts a canonical rule the schema documents at length. sql/schema_v18.sql:68-77 folds status to outcome and puts driver_did_not_respond and driver_rejected explicitly into 'not_completed', with a comment recording that this was already fixed once: leaving those rows out made Bolt's cancellation rate read 55.8% where it is 61.4%, and "'other' is not NULL, so they sat in the denominator of every rate while being excluded from its numerator — the worst of the three possible places to put them." The front-page panel re-implements the fold locally at api/public/app.js:809-813 with a regex /cancel|no_?show|did_?not_show|reject|no_?response|expired|declin/i, which does not match "driver_did_not_respond" (the string is not_respond, not no_response), so those 32 rows land back in "Other / not reported" — the bucket the schema comment names as the worst one. /api/kpis?period=month returns completion_pct "88.0", cancel_pct "12.0", cancelled_trips 379, so the panel, not the tile, is the local re-implementation. Same window everywhere.
user_visible: The completion rate itself (88.0%) agrees on every surface — that part of the finding overstates. What genuinely disagrees is the failure side: the front page states it twice and gives 12.0% and 11.0%, and the phrase "did not complete" carries 347 on #overview and 379 on #demand for the same five days. The 32 in dispute are unanswered driver offers, which the schema has already ruled are not-completed. A supply reader tracking cancellation rate is off by 1pp (8% relative) depending on which panel they read. Kept at medium rather than high: one percentage point, no money moves, and the headline completion figure is consistent.
fix: Delete the local OUTCOME table at api/public/app.js:809-813 and fold through the canonical trip_norm.outcome the way /api/kpis and #demand already do. If "did not respond" is genuinely meant to be a third state, then the tile must say so too — "11.0% cancelled · 1.0% no answer" — so the two halves of the page describe the same partition.

title: #cohort/unit-licence-due ranks 38 already-expired licences under "runs out within 30 days", and the product's own action page says those dates are a system default
seen_on_screen: shots2/cohort-licence-due.png (1440px, period=month). Header: "38 people — licence expiring / Whose licence runs out within 30 days? A driver whose licence lapses stops earning on the day it does…". Tile, rendered in the red critical tone: "LICENCES DUE / 38 / expiring within 30 days". All 12 visible rows carry a red pill "EXPIRED 247 D" in the LICENCE column; member cards print "LICENCE / -247 d / Hotel · Jan 1". The contradicting page reproduced on screen at shots2/action-licence-unreliable.png: "94 of 94 drivers carry the identical expiry 2026-01-01. That pattern is a system default rather than 94 genuine expiries, so we are not raising individual compliance alerts against it." API: /api/economics/drivers?period=month returns 289 rows, exactly 38 pass the predicate, and [...new Set(...licence_days_left)] over the whole payload is [null, -247] — every non-null licence date in the fleet is the same placeholder. 2026-09-05 minus 2026-01-01 is 247 days, so -247 IS 2026-01-01.
intent_check: Not a documented choice — the opposite. The placeholder guard is the product's own deliberate rule and it exists in three other places: src/insights.js:378-408 refuses to raise per-driver licence alerts when one date dominates; api/public/app.js:3945-4153 (#compliance) excludes placeholder rows from its expiry tiles and pills them "a default, not a date"; api/probe.js:621 and :648 both record "94 licence dates that are all the identical placeholder 2026-01-01". cohorts.js's own membersOf() even passes the whole payload to the predicate specifically for this case ("the licence date a source writes when the field was never filled in is one value for the whole payload, and a row cannot know it is the placeholder without being told") — unit-licence-due's test simply does not use it. Nothing in docs/COVERAGE.md covers licences.
user_visible: Yes, in the two places a reader takes the claim from: the page's headline question and the tile sub-label. Downgraded from critical because the screen partly self-corrects — the LICENCE column shows a red "EXPIRED 247 D" pill on every row, the member card shows "-247 d", and the tile itself is drawn in the critical tone (over() at cohort.js:273 fires). No money or count figure is wrong. Breadth correction: the tile repeats on three other cohort pages, not four — I measured unit-drove-unpaid 3, unit-earned-nothing 12, unit-no-hours 18, all -247. It does NOT appear on #cohort/settlement-cash, whose source (/api/settlement/cash-exposure) carries no licence_days_left key at all, so that page was wrongly named in the finding.
fix: Give near() a lower bound at cohort.js:272 (`r[f] != null && r[f] >= 0 && r[f] < 30`) and count negatives into a separate "already expired" tile; change the unit-licence-due predicate at cohorts.js:57 to the same bound or retitle the cohort "Licence expired or expiring". Best: pass the placeholder date the compliance route already computes (app.js:3945 reads drvPage.placeholder_date) into the cohort predicate via the payload argument membersOf() already provides, so a set cannot rank people on dates the engine has declared unusable.

title: #cohort/settlement-cash prints "nothing here" notes directly above the figures it denies
seen_on_screen: shots2/cohort-settlement-cash.png (one 1440px screen). Under the "Every one of them" table: "Bookings — This list does not count bookings. / Money — No money figure reaches this list — either nobody was paid, or this source does not carry one. / Days worked — No day count reaches this list. / Online h — Availability was not collected for anybody on this list. / Standing — No provider describes the standing of anybody here. / Licence — No licence date is recorded for anybody here. / Months active … / Bookings, all time … / Last month worked … / Harsh events — No driving event is counted on this list. / Per 100 km …" (eleven notes, not the seven quoted). The next panel's first card: "Siyad Kallyanathoppil Paramba — BOOKINGS 33 · 1 channel · 347 km · PAID BY STATEMENT AED 666 · FARES CHARGED AED 1,443 · ONLINE 47 h · STANDING active Uber · can earn · HARSH EVENTS 471 worst: Sharp Turn · CAR HELD L59829 5 days". Five of the eleven notes (Bookings, Money, Online h, Standing, Harsh events) are contradicted on that one card and on the five after it.
intent_check: The absent-note mechanism is deliberate and documented — it is the COVERAGE.md house rule ("a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON") applied per table COLUMN, and cohort.js:415-461 attaches each note to a column key. What is not deliberate is the wording: the notes say "this list" and "anybody here", not "this table", and the same generic strings are reused across every cohort (I saw "Cash we can see — No cash booking on this list reports a fare at all" on #cohort/unit-licence-due, a page with no cash column).
user_visible: Yes, but weaker than "critical". The notes render in small dim type inside the table panel, and the cards sit in a separate panel under its own heading "What every source says". A reader who takes "this list" to mean the table above is reading it as intended; a reader who takes it to mean the cohort is told the fleet holds no standing, hours or safety record for 139 people it then shows all three for. No number is wrong on either surface, which is why I moved this off critical.
fix: Scope the wording to the table ("not in this table — see the cards below"), or suppress any absent-note whose measure is populated on the detail payload the cards already fetched (/api/cohort/drivers is requested at cohort.js:470, before the notes would need to be finalised).

title: Every cohort page prints "0 km" where the endpoint returns km: null
seen_on_screen: shots2/cohort-drove-unpaid.png: tile "BOOKINGS / 20 / 2,513 km"— no: tile reads "BOOKINGS / 20 / 0 km", and all eleven member cards read "1 channel · 0 km". shots2/cohort-moved-unpaid.png: tile "BOOKINGS / 3 / 0 km"; L37810's card reads "BOOKINGS 0 / 1 channel · 0 km" three lines above its own "JOURNEYS, NO BOOKING / 8 / 26 km the tracker saw". shots2/cohort-roster-blocked-holding.png: tile "BOOKINGS / 0 / 0 km". API: /api/economics/drivers returns km:null on all 11 drove_unpaid rows; /api/economics/assets returns km:null on both moved_unpaid plates; /api/cohort/drivers returns work:[{bookings:2,km:null,fares:null,…}] for the same people, so the card path is null too; /api/vehicles/directory returns km null on all 9 untracked rows and /api/economics/assets on all 39 idle-documented rows.
intent_check: A straight breach of the product's own stated rule at docs/COVERAGE.md:32-34 — "a figure that cannot be measured renders ABSENT WITH A REASON, never as zero". The correct pattern is eight lines below the offending tile: cohort.js:302-309 prints "ONLINE / — / availability was collected for nobody on this list" with the comment "Null everywhere and zero are different answers", and that tile renders correctly on the same screen as the "0 km" one. The card builder makes the same distinction for fares (`if (fareSum)` at cohort.js:62, `if (fares)` at cohort.js:150) and not for km. Cause is sumOf at cohort.js:32, `Number(f(r)) || 0`.
user_visible: Yes, but never as the page's headline — the count beside it is always correct. Downgraded from high on that basis. The sharpest instance is L37810's card, which prints "0 km" and "26 km the tracker saw" within three lines of each other. On #cohort/unit-drove-unpaid the reader is told eleven drivers took twenty bookings and drove zero kilometres, which reads as phantom bookings rather than "Bolt does not report distance" — that does change what an operator chases.
fix: Apply the Online tile's guard: if no row carries a km, print "— / distance was not reported for anybody on this list"; if some do, print the sum with its measured denominator. Same guard on the card sub-line at cohort.js:62 and :129-130.

title: #cohort/unit-moved-unpaid: the page's why-text asserts tracker mileage and no bookings for a car with neither
seen_on_screen: shots2/cohort-moved-unpaid.png. Page text: "2 vehicles — moved without earning / Which cars drove in this window with no money against them? The tracker logged the kilometres and no channel reported a booking that pays for them." Row 1 is L10595 with BOOKINGS 3, JOURNEYS 0; its card reads "BOOKINGS 3 … Answered by fleet register, ride platforms, custody, fleet portal. Silent: no tracker has ever reported a position." Tile row: "NO TRACKER FIX / 1". API /api/economics/assets?period=month for L10595: {bookings:3, telematics_journeys:0, km:null, last_fix:null, days_moved:2, band:"moved_unpaid"}.
intent_check: Structural, not a data accident, and not documented. api/economics_routes.js:560 bands on `money > 0 ? 'earning' : (r.days_moved > 0 || r.bookings > 0) ? 'moved_unpaid' : 'still'`, and days_moved itself (line 215) is `count(DISTINCT local_day)` over bookings AND telematics rows — so nothing in the band ever requires a tracker. km (line 216) is booking distance only, which is why it is null here. The comment above the band says only "A car that moved without earning burned a day of custody…", which the label supports; it is the cohorts.js:75-76 why-text that overreaches.
user_visible: Yes, but I corrected the finding's framing: L10595 did not "never move" — three bookings is movement, and "moved without earning" is a fair label for it. What is false is the explanatory sentence, on both clauses, for that row: the tracker logged nothing (no fix, ever) and a channel did report three bookings. The card self-corrects with "Silent: no tracker has ever reported a position". n=2 today, but the defect is in the band definition so it recurs on any window. Downgraded from high.
fix: Either require a measured journey or a tracker fix for `moved_unpaid` and route booking-only rows to a differently worded band, or (cheaper) rewrite the why-text at cohorts.js:75-76 so it does not assert tracker evidence the band never checks, and print the movement basis per row (journeys vs bookings) — the JOURNEYS column already carries it.

title: #cohort/settlement-cash's lede contradicts the coverage figure in the payload it fetched, and its money column has no denominator
seen_on_screen: shots2/cohort-settlement-cash.png. Lede: "Money the fleet is owed by its own drivers. Most of these fares carry no value at all in the record, so the exposure is larger than the figure — and who is still driving, and who has stopped, decides which of them will be settled." Tile: "CASH BOOKINGS / 574 / AED 22,816 of it reports a fare". Table row 1: "Siyad Kallyanathoppil Paramba — Uber — 16 — AED 391 — L59829". API /api/settlement/cash-exposure?period=month: value_known_pct 75.1, caveat "143 of 574 cash trips come from a channel that does not report a fare, so the value column is a floor, not the total.", total_cash_value_known 22817; row 1 carries priced_cash_trips 8 and value_known_pct 50. Summing the 139 rows: 431 of 574 priced, cash_value 22,816.
intent_check: I checked whether the lede could be true on some other window, since that is the usual escape: it cannot. value_known_pct is 75.1 (month), 72.8 (quarter) and 64.2 (year) — most cash fares carry a value under every window the page can be set to. The caveat string does not appear anywhere in the rendered page text. priced_cash_trips genuinely has no column: the driver column list at cohort.js:449-451 defines "Cash bookings" (cash_trips) and "Cash we can see" (cash_value) and nothing between them. Not documented anywhere.
user_visible: Partly. The "most" claim is a plain factual inversion — it tells the reader the unmeasured share dominates when it is one trip in four, so it overstates hidden exposure by roughly threefold in the direction of alarm on the page used to pick who to settle with first. The missing-denominator half is softer: the column is not labelled per-trip, so 391/16 is the reader's own arithmetic, not the page's. The 22,816-vs-22,817 gap is a rounding artefact of summing already-rounded rows and is not worth reporting. Downgraded from high to medium on the strength of the first claim alone.
fix: Render the endpoint's own `caveat` verbatim in place of the hard-coded "Most of these fares carry no value at all" at cohorts.js:256-258, and add priced_cash_trips as the denominator beside the value column at cohort.js:451 ("AED 391 over 8 of 16 priced") — the field is already on every row.
